# One round of the Muse agent: a swarm explores, then builds

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed on main and tagged `muse-code-era` before the first Muse Code session; each later version is committed before the round that uses it. [Who made what](../../../PROVENANCE.md).*

**Skill version 8.** This file, the role cards and tracking.md are versioned together; [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists every version. Each round records the version it ran (see *Versions* in tracking.md).

You are the **lead** of a Muse Code session in your own worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. The first prompt names the Meta model you run as, the name your commit subjects start with, and the co-author line every commit ends with. `claude/muse-agent-brief.md` fixes the task, the slots, the tools and limits, the grader command and the pass criteria (G1, G2). Four ADRs change it in five ways:

1. **Harness** ([ADR 0006](../../../claude/adr/0006-muse-spark-in-muse-code.md)). You are a Muse Code session, not a Claude Code one. Muse Code adds no trailer, so you write the first prompt's co-author line on every commit yourself (see *Commits*).
2. **No attempt limit and no stop rule** (ADR 0006). The brief's *When a slot stops* no longer applies: you decide when a slot is done. Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try.
3. **A swarm** ([ADR 0007](../../../claude/adr/0007-muse-spark-swarm.md)). Helpers explore and build; you coordinate and commit.
4. **Files** (ADR 0007, [ADR 0009](../../../claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md)). Each round writes in its own **round folder**: round 1 at the top of `muse-spark/`, round N from 2 on in `muse-spark/round-<N>/`. It holds `exploration/` and `implementation/`, the round's shared documents, which replace `strategy.md`; `kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>/`; and `summary.md`. tracking.md writes it `<round>/`.
5. **Rounds build on each other** (ADR 0009). A finished round's files are frozen: read them and cite them, and the hooks refuse any change to them. From round 2 on, a slot may have a **baseline**: the best attempt so far that passes the current G2 and that Claude's G3 accepted: against the unchanged model and the compiled reference, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A new attempt must beat it in the same grader run. A slot without one has a **starting point** instead: an earlier attempt to build from, which Claude's measurement names, with what kept it from being a baseline.

The rest of the brief stands. The goal: kernels that make whole requests faster. In the grader they pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither (ADR 0011), and where the slot has a baseline `beats_baseline` true too, because they remove a cause you can name. Then the **ready check**, the same G3 Claude runs after the round, run by you inside it, must pass them before they are `ready` ([ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)). A faster decode step bought with a slower prefill is no improvement, and a claim no one measured is no result. An attempt built for decode sizes may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference with `max_rows` (the brief's launch spec). The Muse agent was Muse Spark in round 1 and Muse Wonder in round 2 ([ADR 0008](../../../claude/adr/0008-muse-wonder.md)), and is Muse Spark's contributor model again from round 3 ([ADR 0012](../../../claude/adr/0012-muse-spark-contributor-unattended.md)); the first prompt names the model you run as, and documents from earlier rounds say the model of their round. No one approves your tool calls during the round, so the rules here are yours to keep.

## The swarm

| Role | Name | Task | Card |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lead** (you) | | Start the helpers, keep the two READMEs, settle clashes, commit | this file |
| **Explorer** | `explorer-<territory>` | Map one territory into entries, and find where it loses time | [explorer.md](explorer.md) |
| **Verifier** | `verifier` | Check every inefficiency against its sources | [verifier.md](verifier.md) |
| **Builder** | `builder-<n>-<letter>` | Write and grade one solution for one hypothesis: one attempt | [builder.md](builder.md) |
| **Boundary agent** | `boundary-<n>` | Write what a hypothesis's solution must keep identical, and check passing attempts against it | [boundary.md](boundary.md) |
| **Checker** | `checker-<n>`, `checker-final` | Check every speed claim against the file it cites: a hypothesis's before it closes, and the round's final claims | [checker.md](checker.md) |

You don't explore, build or grade yourself; the one GPU job you run is the ready check (step 4). Start each helper with a prompt of this shape:

> You are `<name>`, a `<role>` in round `<N>`'s swarm; this round writes in `<round folder>`. Read `.agents/skills/muse-round/<card>` and `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md`, then: `<task>`.

[tracking.md](tracking.md) describes the shared documents (the two phase folders, their READMEs, entries and logs) and the rules every agent keeps. Read it before starting anyone. Up to 12 agents run at once, you included.

**A checkpoint** is what you do each time a helper returns, and whenever the log shows something to settle:
1. **Read the log.** Read the phase log since your last checkpoint.
2. **Settle clashes.** When two entries describe one cause, keep the fuller one and set the other's status to `superseded by <entry>`. When two helpers work on one item, redirect one of them (`subagent_send_message`). Log what you decided.
3. **Refresh the tracker.** Update the phase README's tracker table, and raise the version of each hypothesis entry that changed.
4. **Raise the version.** Raise the phase README to its next version, and add its line to `## Versions`, naming the entries that changed and their versions (see *Versions* in tracking.md).
5. **Commit** the phase folder, plus any attempt that came back, as that version (see *Commits*).

## The round

### 0. Find where you are

- Run `git log --oneline main -1`, then `git tag --list -n1 'muse-round-*'`, which lists the finished rounds. **This round** is one more than the highest; with none, it is round 1. Its folder is `muse-spark/round-<N>/` (round 1: `muse-spark/`).
- `git log --oneline --grep '^Muse ' muse-code-era..HEAD` lists the Muse agent's commits of every round.
- **From round 2 on,** read Claude's measurement of the previous round, `claude/findings/muse-round-<N-1>.md`. It has the G3 results and names each slot's baseline or starting point. If it is missing, stop and reply "Claude's measurement of round <N-1> is missing": this round builds on it.
- If this round's folder already exists, a session stopped partway: carry on from its READMEs' last versions.
- Read the brief.

**Done** when you can name the round number and its folder, and from round 2 on each slot's baseline or starting point and the latest G3 results.

### 1. The starting point (from round 2 on)

This is the round's plan, built on what the earlier rounds learned. Read:
- the previous rounds' final exploration and implementation READMEs and `summary.md`;
- the `notes.md` of each baseline or starting-point attempt;
- Claude's measurement.

Then write the opening of this round's `exploration/README.md` (set up as in step 2.1), a section **Starting point**:
- **Per slot:**
  - the baseline, or the starting point where there is none, and its piece timing;
  - its G3 effect, and how that compares with what was predicted, with the reason where Claude's measurement gives one;
  - what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time.
- **What is left:**
  - the confirmed inefficiencies not yet built or not fully removed, ranked by predicted saving against the baselines, or the reference where a slot has none;
  - the slots not yet tried, for example `routing+combine`;
  - the recommendations outside the slots.
- **Refuted claims,** which no one chases again.
- **Territories** this round opens (step 2.2), each with the line of this section that reopens it.

Commit it as exploration v1. **Done** when every slot has its baseline or starting point and every territory has its reason.

### 2. Exploration

1. **Set up the folder.** Write `<round>/exploration/README.md` with a heading, its version line (v1, with skill version 8), the tracker (one row per territory) and `## Versions`, and an empty `log.md`.
2. **Start the explorers and the verifier,** all at once.
   - **Round 1** starts with these territories:

     | Territory | Covers |
     |---|---|
     | `model` | `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py`: the decoder layer, `MoE.__call__` and everything around the slots |
     | `switch-layers` | `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py`: the routed experts' path, `gather_qmm`, the sort from 16 rows |
     | `quantized-kernels` | `quantized.h` and `quantized_utils.h` in `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/`: the `affine_gather_*` kernels behind `gather_qmm` |
     | `other-kernels` | the other Metal kernels in the same folder that the routing and combine slots launch: sort, softmax, reductions, elementwise, copies |
     | `vllm-metal` | `third_party/vllm-metal/vllm_metal/`: how the engine runs a decode step and a prefill chunk around the model |
     | `grader` | `bench/grader/`: the slot interface, what G1, G2 and the piece timing measure, and so the boundary every solution keeps |
     | `findings` | `claude/findings/` and `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/` |
     | `runs` | `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/`, `2026-10-29-baseline/` and `2026-10-30-micro/` |

   - **From round 2 on,** the starting point lists the territories:
     - `baseline-<slot>` for each slot: its baseline's kernels and `spec.json`, which are now the code in the slot, or its starting point's. Map them with the checklist, and find where they still lose time and, for a starting point, why it fails G2;
     - `g3`: Claude's measurement of the previous round, where the end-to-end change differs from the piece timing, and why;
     - of round 1's territories, only those the starting point reopens. An explorer starts from that territory's earlier entries and writes only what is new.
3. **Refocus as costs show up.** When an entry shows that one file holds most of a territory's cost, split it off as a territory of its own, with its own explorer. Merge or close a territory that turns out to hold nothing, and add one when an inefficiency points somewhere no one covers. Log each change and update the tracker.
4. **Checkpoint** each time a helper returns.

**Done** when every territory entry is `done`, the verifier has returned, and every inefficiency is `confirmed`, `refuted` or `superseded`.

### 3. The analysis

Write the final `<round>/exploration/README.md`. It is the round's report on the code, for this round's builders and for future improvements:

- **Tracker:** the final table.
- **Starting point** (from round 2 on), as written in step 1, with any correction exploration made.
- **Context:** the decode step and the prefill, the MoE block and its slots, and what the measurements say about where the time goes in each.
- **Territory map:** how the territories feed each other. For each territory: what it receives, what it passes on, and its measured cost.
- **Inefficiencies, ranked:**
  - the confirmed ones inside the slots, ranked by predicted saving as a share of the decode step, averaged over 1, 8 and 32 rows, or of the prefill chunk, averaged over 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows; from round 2 on, the saving is against the baseline where the slot has one;
  - each with what removing it does to the other phase, and whether a hand-off (`max_rows`) keeps that phase unchanged;
  - each with its cost, kind and entry;
  - Claude's findings marked as Claude's, earlier rounds' entries linked as theirs, and this round's own reading marked as yours.
- **Recommendations:** the confirmed inefficiencies outside the slots, with their evidence. They're for surucuonur's team.
- **Refuted claims,** in one line each, so no one chases them again.
- **Files read:** links to each territory entry's list.

Commit it. **Done** when every ranked item links a confirmed entry and every number in the README has its source.

### 4. Implementation

Take the ranked inefficiencies in order, at most two at a time, in different slots so their attempts never touch. Write `<round>/implementation/README.md` with a heading, its version line, the tracker and `## Versions`, and an empty `log.md`. For each hypothesis:

1. **Open the hypothesis.** Write `<round>/implementation/hyp-<n>-<slug>.md`, with status `boundary`, the inefficiency, the slot and, from round 2 on, the slot's baseline folder or `none`. Add its tracker row and log it.
2. **Draw its boundary.** Start `boundary-<n>` to write the boundary, and wait for it.
3. **Compete.**
   - Set the status to `building`.
   - Start 2 or 3 builders, `builder-<n>-a`, `-b` and `-c`. Give each a different direction drawn from the analysis: for example, fusing kernels, reading each weight byte once, or a different threadgroup shape. From round 2 on, a direction may start from the baseline's or starting point's kernels, or from scratch.
4. **Collect.** Each time a builder returns:
   - checkpoint, committing its attempt folder with the hypothesis entry, the README and the log;
   - if the attempt passed G2, start `boundary-<n>` to check it.
5. **Harden.**
   - Pick the best attempt: it passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline`, and it is the fastest across the six sizes.
   - Set the status to `hardening`, and start a builder for that attempt's next single change.
   - Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove.
   - **Change approach after three alike failures.** Keep the hypothesis entry's failure ledger at each collect: every graded attempt that lost, the size or phase it lost at, and its named cause. When three attempts have lost at the same phase for the same cause, the next one changes approach (another kernel structure, parallelisation or dataflow, not a tuning), and its `notes.md` says "approach change: from X to Y"; or you log why not. A cause renamed without a measurement that refutes the old one is the same cause.
6. **Close.**
   - **`candidate`:** the best attempt passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline` true, and you can name no further change worth making. Write the **Decision**: the attempt, why it is best, and the change in whole requests you predict, labelled a prediction. Then start `checker-<n>` on the entry; the hypothesis is a candidate once its **Checks** section says `pass`.
   - **`dropped`:** say why. A slot whose hypotheses are all dropped keeps its baseline, or the reference where it has none.

Then open the next-ranked inefficiency.

**The ready check** ([ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)). Once no hypothesis is building or hardening and at least one is a `candidate`, run it yourself, over every candidate in one call:

```bash
.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_ready.py <round>/checks/ready-<k> <slot>=<attempt folder> [<slot>=<attempt folder> ...]
```

It times the candidates in vLLM exactly as Claude's G3 will after the round, each alone and, with more than one, all together, then audits its own log and writes `ready-verdict.json`. It takes about 10 to 15 minutes per slot, more for an attempt with a slow prefill, and waits its turn for the GPU. Commit its folder at the next checkpoint.
- **Exit 0 or 1: a verdict, and it stands.** A candidate whose `muse-<slot>` passes becomes `ready`; one that fails goes back to `hardening` with the failure in its ledger, or to `dropped`. Cite the file either way. With more than one candidate, submitting them together needs `muse-all` to pass; if some pass alone and `muse-all` fails, a second check may take only those.
- **Exit 2: no verdict.** The run stopped or broke the protocol; run it again in a new folder.
- **At most two ready checks per round.**

**Done** when no confirmed inefficiency is left that you judge will pay, and every candidate has a ready-check verdict. Write why in the implementation README.

### 5. Finish

1. **The implementation README:** the final tracker, one paragraph per hypothesis, and a **Ready to test** section. It names the attempt per slot that goes to Claude's G3: a `ready` attempt, the baseline kept, or the reference. For the `ready` ones it shows the ready check's measured change in the four workloads (the decode step, the prompt time and the whole request, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference), citing `ready-verdict.json`, with your earlier prediction beside it, labelled PREDICTION, and the **Unverified** list. Nothing else in it is an end-to-end number.
2. **The exploration README:** add *What building taught*, the analysis corrected by what the attempts showed.
3. **`<round>/summary.md`:** a `## Round N` section with:
   - the model, the skill version this round ran, and the final versions of both READMEs;
   - the final attempt per slot;
   - the number of graded attempts per slot, this round and over all rounds;
   - the ready check's measured change, citing its file;
   - what you'd try next;
   - your recommendations outside the slots.
4. **Check, commit, reply.** Start `checker-final` on *Ready to test* and the summary, and fix what it finds until it signs `pass`. Then commit, and reply with this round's commits and the words "Round N finished".

## Your own rules

- **Writes:**
  - you write the two READMEs, the hypothesis entries' status blocks and decisions, and `summary.md`;
  - every helper writes only what its card names;
  - all of it stays in this round's folder.
- **Claude's G3 after the round is the authority;** your ready check is the same measurement, made earlier. vLLM runs only through the ready check.
- **The rules every agent keeps** are in tracking.md.

## Commits

You are the only agent that commits. Commit only on `muse-agent`.
- **What to add:** this round's phase folders that exist so far (only `exploration` until implementation starts) and the attempt folders that came back. An attempt another builder is still writing waits for its own commit. An entry that is mid-edit is committed as it stands, and finished in a later commit.
- **The message:**
  - every subject starts with the name the first prompt gives you, then a colon;
  - a checkpoint's subject is `<name>: <phase> v<N>: <what changed>`, the version it records;
  - every message ends with the first prompt's co-author line, exactly.

For example, in round 2 as Muse Wonder:

```bash
git add muse-spark/round-2/exploration muse-spark/round-2/implementation muse-spark/round-2/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>
git commit -m "Muse Wonder: implementation v4: experts attempt 3 graded, beats baseline" \
  -m "Co-Authored-By: Muse Wonder (Meta Model API) <muse-wonder@meta-model-api.invalid>"
```

Use no other co-author. The hooks refuse a commit without a Muse agent's co-author, a commit outside `muse-spark/`, a change to a finished round's files, a new file outside this round's folder, and any merge. Push, merge, rebase, tags, git config and hook skipping stay with surucuonur.

</skill-body>
</read-skill-result>

111|4. **One section per builder:** its direction, its attempts (folder, predicted and measured µs per layer at the six sizes with each size's verdict, G1, G2, `beats_compiled`, and where the slot has a baseline its time and `beats_baseline`), and what each attempt taught.
112|5. **Boundary checks** of the attempts that passed G2.
113|6. **Decision:** the best attempt and why, with the change in whole requests it predicts, labelled a prediction; once a ready check has run, its `ready-verdict.json` and the measured change.
114|7. **Failure ledger,** kept by the lead: each graded attempt that lost, the size or phase it lost at, its named cause and its approach (`SKILL.md` step 4, *Harden*).
115|8. **Unverified:** what no one measured, the boundary's *can't see* list at least.
116|9. **Checks:** each checker's verdict, `pass` or its defects with file and line.
117|
118|## The checklist
119|
120|Fill it in for each piece of code you inspect, so that no piece is judged without its neighbours:
121|
122|- **Callers:** who calls it, and with what shapes at 1, 8 and 32 rows of a decode step and in a prefill.
123|- **Callees:** what it calls, down to the Metal kernel it launches.
124|- **Data:** each input and output with shape, dtype and layout. Where it is produced, and where it is consumed next.
125|- **Neighbours:** what runs just before and after it in the decode step, and what a replacement must keep identical.
126|- **Cost:** the kernels it launches, the bytes it reads and writes (weight bytes counted per read), and its measured time with the table the time comes from.
127|- **Invariants:** what correctness depends on: G2's bit-exact rule at every size, the tie rule for the 4th and 5th expert, the bfloat16 rounding points, and which MLX kernel the reference uses at each size.
128|
129|## The log
130|
131|Append one line per event with the shell, so lines from several agents never mix. In round 2:
132|
133|```bash
134|printf '%s | %s | %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "explorer-baseline-experts" "posted ineff-baseline-experts-2: each weight byte read 4 times at 32 rows" >> muse-spark/round-2/exploration/log.md
135|```
136|
137|Log when you start, claim something, post or confirm an entry, change direction (what from, what to, and which entry made you), grade an attempt (with its verdict), and finish.
138|
139|## Adapting to the others' work
140|
141|Before every new piece of work, and after every post:
142|1. Read the phase README's tracker and the newest 30 lines of the phase log (`tail -n 30`).
143|2. Then change direction when:
144|   - **someone else covers it:** another entry already covers the same code or cause, so append to that entry instead of starting a second one;
145|   - **its premise fell:** the claim your work rests on was refuted;
146|   - **something pays more:** an open item in your territory or task predicts a larger saving than what you're on, and nobody owns it.
147|3. When you change direction, log it with the reason, and write it in your own entry's status block.
148|
149|Two claims on the same item go to the lead, who settles them.
150|
151|## Rules for every agent
152|
153|- **Writes go only to this round's folder, in the files your role names.** Earlier rounds' folders, everything else in the worktree, and everything outside it are read-only.
154|- **Only the lead commits.** Helpers never run `git add` or `git commit`.
155|- **The grader and the ready check are the only GPU jobs.** Builders run the grader through the brief's command; the lead runs the ready check (`SKILL.md` step 4). Both wait their turn for the GPU. Start no other GPU work and load no model outside them: the machine has 16 GB and slows down sharply when memory runs short. A run of `time_candidates.py`, `breakdown.py` or any other timing script made directly is evidence of nothing.
156|- **Every number has a source,** and every speed number says its level and its kind:
157|  - **measured, piece:** the grader verdict that timed exactly that slot, `grade.json` in its attempt folder;
158|  - **measured, whole request:** the `ready-verdict.json` that timed exactly that slot or combination;
159|  - **prediction:** anything else. It counts only the candidate's own measured effect, shows its arithmetic, and stands beside the measured value once there is one.
160|
161|  A combination is measured as one, never added up from its slots. What no one measured goes under **Unverified**, never assumed free, neutral or zero. Other numbers cite a file and line, a table (path and row), or arithmetic shown in full.
162|- **Credentials stay unread:** `.env` files, `~/.config/muse/` and any key store.
163|- **The API-stage kernels** in the history before the tag `agent-era` are from an earlier, removed stage (PROVENANCE.md) and stay unread.

1|# Exploration: round 3 — analysis
2|
3|**Version:** v1 · 2026-11-04T17:36:02Z · skill version 8

5|## Tracker

16|## Starting point
17|
18|Round 3 builds on rounds 1 (`muse-spark/`, frozen, tagged `muse-round-1`) and 2 (`muse-spark/round-2/`, frozen, tagged `muse-round-2`) as measured independently by Claude in `claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` (2026-11-04, on `main` after merging round 2 at `4033cae`). Round 2 ran skill version 5 as Muse Wonder. The judgment changed for round 3 ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)): an improvement must hold in both phases, decode and prefill — faster in one, slower in neither — against the unchanged model and the compiled reference, in the piece timing (`beats_compiled`) and in G3, where no whole request may be slower. A slot's baseline is its best attempt so far that passes the current G2, has `beats_compiled` true, and passes G3; anything else that passes G2 is a starting point. **No slot has a baseline.** A new attempt must pass G1 and G2 (bit-exact at 1, 8, 32 and 127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) and beat the compiled reference in the chained two-phase timing; there is no `--baseline` to pass. Inside the round, the lead's ready check (`bench/grader/check_ready.py`, [ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)) times every candidate exactly as Claude's G3 will, and only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`.
19|
20|Round 2's final attempts, their piece timings and G3 effects are summarised per slot. Piece timings are Claude's re-grade on main with the two-phase grader (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`), chained µs per layer as reference / compiled / candidate. G3 is the vLLM decode-step change against the unchanged model (median of 3 shuffled repeats, `console-vllm.txt`) plus the whole-request throughput change at 1×128, 8×128, 32×128 and 32×1,024 (prompt-time multiple in brackets, `results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/`). Round 2's own prediction was decode-only (piece basis × 20 layers plus compiled G3 offsets); both are quoted so the gap can be seen.
21|
22|### Per slot
23|
24|#### `experts` — starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7`
25|
26|- **What it is.** One fused per-pair kernel (512 threads per (row, expert-slot) pair, `rows*4` threadgroups): interleaved gate/up plus interleaved down in a merged K loop, intermediates in threadgroup memory (3,840 B), full-bfloat16 silu-mul. Per-block numerics replicate MLX's `affine_gather_qvm` bitwise at decode sizes; a `rows >= 60` branch runs a scalar `qmm_accum` (bfloat16-rounded dequant, contiguous `BK=32` order) to match `gather_qmm_rhs` at prefill sizes. See `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7/notes.md` and `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md`.
27|- **Piece timing** (`grade-phases-experts-attempt-7.json`). Decode: 84.0 / 78.6 / **92.1** at 1 row (slower), 239.3 / 235.5 / **162.8** at 8 rows, 806.5 / 797.8 / **515.3** at 32 rows. Prefill: 963.4 / 960.8 / **15220.0** at 127 rows (15.8× compiled), 3979.3 / 4306.0 / **119154.4** at 1,016 rows (27.7×), 7359.8 / 11998.9 / **240681.1** at 2,048 rows (20.1×). `beats_compiled` false: decode `slower` (the 1-row size), prefill `slower` (every size).
28|- **G3 effect vs prediction.** Round 2 dropped this attempt and predicted nothing for it; Claude timed it anyway. Per decode step in vLLM: +0.29 ms (+5.4%) with 1 request, −1.22 ms (−8.4%) with 8, −5.35 ms (−17.5%) with 32. Over whole requests (with routing attempt-4): throughput −10.0% / −37.5% / −48.0% / −82.5%, with prompt processing 6.63× / 14.50× / 12.50× / 13.09× slower than the unchanged engine. The fastest exact decode step measured (routing + experts: −20% with 32 requests in plain MLX) is the slowest whole request.
29|  - **Reason (measured).** The scalar prefill branch copies `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding but not its speed: every prompt chunk here has at least 128 rows, so it always runs that branch. At 1 row the fused designs plateau at 92–110 µs per layer chained against 73–87 for the compiled reference across six exact attempts — width, group count, interleave and store parallelism moved 8/32 rows and none moved 1 row by more than ~12 µs (round 2's *What building taught*).
30|- **What keeps it from being a baseline.** It passes G2 bit-exact at all six sizes, but it is slower than the compiled reference at 1 row and at every prefill size, so prompts take 6.6 to 14.5 times as long and whole requests lose 10% to 83% of throughput.
31|- **Where it still spends its time.** At 1 row: the ~19 µs gap to compiled is the `tg_x` load, silu, the two barriers and chained fixed cost — the down interleave proved the down waves were already hidden across simdgroups (attempt-7 notes, miss analysis). At prefill sizes: the scalar `qmm_accum` branch, 15,220 µs per layer where compiled takes 961. Per-pair weight re-reads remain at all sizes (552,960 B per pair).
32|
33|#### `routing` — starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-4`
34|
35|- **What it is.** One fused kernel per layer: scalar sums over the same partition/K order as MLX's three regimes (GEMV at `rows == 1`, split-K while `rows <= 768`, regular above), staged `w_router` blocks in threadgroup memory (coalesced `float4` loads, 28,080 B of 32 KB, 24 barriers on the scalar path), MLX's verbatim sigmoid, strictly-greater insertion top-4, `((w0+w1)+w2)+w3` normalise. See `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-4/notes.md` and `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-2-routing-exact.md`.
36|- **Piece timing** (`grade-phases-routing-attempt-4.json`). Decode: 68.4 / 65.1 / **49.8** at 1 row, 169.2 / 135.7 / **113.5** at 8 rows, 159.3 / 145.2 / **121.3** at 32 rows — faster at every decode size. Prefill: 102.3 / 87.3 / **227.1** at 127 rows (2.6× compiled), 231.3 / 221.1 / **1298.8** at 1,016 rows (5.9×), 310.0 / 290.4 / **2513.0** at 2,048 rows (8.7×). `beats_compiled` false: decode `faster`, prefill `slower`.
37|- **G3 effect vs prediction.** Per decode step in vLLM: −0.47 / −0.43 / −0.54 ms at 1 / 8 / 32 requests — it passed every rule of its time (faster than both the unchanged model and the compiled reference at all sizes, in both engines). Round 2 predicted −0.48 / −0.50 / −0.49 ms from the chained piece timing; the 8-request figure came in 0.07 ms short, the others match. Over whole requests: throughput +10.2% / +1.8% / +0.3% / −3.5%, with prompts 1.07–1.10× slower. Under the rule set after this measurement it fails, so it is no baseline.
38|  - **Reason (measured).** The staged scalar path wins at decode sizes but scales badly: 227 µs per layer at 127 rows where compiled takes 87, widening to 8.7× at 2,048 rows. The 28 KB threadgroup footprint caps residency as row counts grow.
39|- **What keeps it from being a baseline.** It passes G2 bit-exact at all six sizes, but it is slower than the compiled reference at every prefill size, so prompts take 7–10% longer and whole requests with 1,024-token prompts lose 3.5%.
40|- **Where it still spends its time.** At prefill sizes: the staged scalar chain and its 24 barriers per row (2,513 µs per layer at 2,048 rows vs 290 compiled). At decode sizes it already beats compiled everywhere (49.8 / 113.5 / 121.3); the per-row `w_router` re-read and the serial thread-0 scan are untouched.
41|
42|#### `combine` — starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1`
43|
44|- **What it is.** One fused kernel per layer: thread per output element on a `rows×768` grid, volatile-barrier stepwise fold `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3` with a rounding after every op, one bfloat16 round, single-rounding bfloat16 `+ shared`. See `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1/notes.md` and `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-3-combine-exact.md`.
45|- **Piece timing** (`grade-phases-combine-attempt-1.json`). Decode: 52.8 / 53.4 / **45.7** at 1 row, 71.2 / 56.4 / **47.9** at 8 rows, 87.0 / 69.1 / **64.6** at 32 rows. Prefill: 87.8 / 66.1 / **62.8** at 127 rows, 425.2 / 271.6 / **226.5** at 1,016 rows, 846.2 / 520.4 / **273.0** at 2,048 rows — faster at all six sizes. `beats_compiled` true. It is the only starting point that beats the compiled reference in both phases.
46|- **G3 effect vs prediction.** Per decode step in vLLM: −0.37 / −0.20 / **+1.05 ms** at 1 / 8 / 32 requests. Round 2 predicted −0.36 / −0.35 / −0.35 ms; at 32 requests the sign flips. With 8 requests its median sits above the compiled reference in vLLM. Over whole requests (with routing): throughput +15.9% / +2.1% / −2.7% / −4.1%.
47|  - **Reason (not known).** A G3 loss of 1.05 ms is about 52 µs per layer, more than the kernel's whole chained time in the grader (64.6 µs per layer at 32 rows, of which the loss alone exceeds the kernel's work as the grader runs it). The cost comes from how the kernel sits in the step, which the grader doesn't reproduce. Round 3's first question is why.
48|- **What keeps it from being a baseline.** It passes G1, G2 and `beats_compiled`, but its decode step in G3 was 1.05 ms slower than the unchanged model's with 32 requests, for a reason the grader doesn't show.
49|- **Where it still spends its time.** In the grader: nothing further — it sits on the chained floor (~32–40 µs per layer at decode sizes) and wins everywhere. In the step at 32 requests: the unexplained ~52 µs per layer.
50|
51|#### All three together
52|
53|Round 2's submission (routing + combine) changes the vLLM decode step by −0.73 / −0.74 / **+0.53 ms** at 1 / 8 / 32 requests, against a prediction of −0.84 / −0.85 / −0.84 ms: combine's slowdown outweighs routing's saving with 32 requests. Round 2's pairings run (plain MLX) found every pair within 0.5 ms of its parts' sum, but all three together with 8 requests 2.8 ms slower than their parts (+0.94 ms measured against −1.87 ms summed) — the second set of kernels to show it, so the cause is likely in how the step runs with all three slots replaced at that size, not in one kernel. Not explained. Every round-2 variant keeps the model's greedy tokens in both engines at 1 and 32 requests (round 1's change them with 32).
54|
55|Round 2 ran the grader exactly once per attempt: 13 runs for 13 attempts (experts 7, routing 4, combine 2).
56|
57|### What is left
58|
59|Confirmed inefficiencies not yet built or not fully removed, ranked by predicted saving against the compiled reference (no slot has a baseline, so the reference is the bar everywhere). Savings span both phases now: decode shares use the plain-MLX step denominators 4.75 / 13.37 / 28.19 ms at 1 / 8 / 32 rows, prefill effects are prompt-time multiples and whole-request throughput from Claude's engine comparison. Exactness gates are solved in every slot — all three starting points pass G2 at all six sizes — so nothing below is blocked on correctness.
60|
61|1. **Experts prefill path 15–28× slower than compiled.** The slot's scalar `qmm_accum` branch takes 15,220 / 119,154 / 240,681 µs per layer where compiled takes 961 / 4,306 / 11,999, and prompt processing runs 6.6 to 14.5 times slower, costing 10% to 83% of whole-request throughput. Removing it — a fast exact prefill branch, or a `max_rows` hand-off that keeps prefill-sized inputs on the compiled reference (Claude checked the hand-off bit-exact on a copy with `max_rows` 59, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`) — recovers the whole loss while keeping the 8/32-row decode wins (−1.22 / −5.35 ms per step). This is Claude's question 4 for round 3 (prefill half).
62|2. **Experts 1-row decode latency.** The starting point chains at 92.1 µs per layer against 78.6 for compiled (+13.5; G3 +0.29 ms with 1 request), the last size where it loses. Six exact fused packings plateaued at 92–110 µs; round 2's summary suggests copying the reference's unfused structure exactly for small row counts. Worth up to ~0.3 ms per step at 1 request plus unlocking `beats_compiled` on the decode phase. Claude's question 1.
63|3. **Routing prefill 2.6/5.9/8.7× slower than compiled.** 227 / 1,299 / 2,513 µs per layer against 87 / 221 / 290; prompts take 7–10% longer and 1,024-token-prompt requests lose 3.5% throughput. Same two outs as experts: a prefill branch that scales, or `max_rows`. Decode already wins everywhere, so the hand-off alone banks the slot if the decode win survives composition. Claude's question 4 (prefill half).
64|4. **Why combine attempt-1 costs ~1 ms in the step with 32 requests and not in the grader.** The chained piece timing has it faster (64.6 vs 69.1 µs per layer); G3 has it 1.05 ms slower per step. No hypothesis can bank combine until the mechanism is found — it may be a property of the kernel (grid shape, cache behaviour) or of the step around it. Claude's question 2.
65|5. **Why all three slots replaced at once lose 2.8 ms with 8 requests.** Every pair adds up; all three together miss by 2.8 ms in plain MLX (round 2 pairs run), repeating round 1's shape. Until it is understood, per-slot piece wins may not compose into a G3 win. Claude's question 3. Carried as a constraint on every hypothesis; the ready check measures each candidate alone and all together, so round 3 sees composition inside the round.
66|6. **Experts per-pair weight re-reads persist** (round 2 `ineff-baseline-experts-3`, confirmed): 908 MB read vs 443 MB distinct at 32 rows, floor 2.33 ms per step at 32 rows, 0 banked — grouped designs lost in both rounds on duty-cycle ceilings. Banks only if a grouped design holds the chained rate on distinct bytes.
67|7. **Routing `w_router` re-read per row** (round 2 `ineff-baseline-routing-4`, confirmed): excess floor 0 / 0.13 / 0.57 ms per step; round 1's tiled-sharing attempt was slower everywhere, and attempt-4 already wins in spite of it. Upper bound only.
68|8. **Prefill-only reference waste, now judged** (round 2 `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`, `-2`, confirmed): BM=16 padded tiles waste 47.1 / 15.3 / 5.2% of issued row-work at 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows, and `gather_mm_offsets` is recomputed 3× per layer (≤0.26 ms per chunk forward). Round 2 ranked these at 0 µs of decode time; under two-phase judgment they are prompt-time savings a fast prefill branch takes for free.
69|
70|**Slots not yet tried.** `routing+combine` (brief: both slots, each with its own kernels, in one candidate; the grader tests each part on its own and the combine part receives the reference routing weights). Neither round has graded one `routing-combine` folder. It remains available; since the parts are graded independently it is packaging unless a shared design emerges.
71|
72|**Recommendations outside the slots** stand as written in `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md` and round 2's exploration README *Recommendations*; Claude's measurement did not test them. In brief: attention K/V re-read per query head (up to ~2 ms at 32 rows); split-K partial traffic from 14 rows (≈2.4 ms upper bound at 32 rows, unmeasured); 60 q/k/v `[0]` gathers + copies (−0.21 ms measured at 8 rows, `squeeze(0)` fix); ~2 ms engine CPU per 1-row step (≈0.5 ms of Python fixes); prefill tile waste and redundant `gather_mm_offsets` in MLX's `gather_qmm_rhs` (time-to-first-token only — now prompt time, item 8 above). They are for surucuonur's team; no hypothesis targets them.
73|
74|### Refuted claims
75|
76|No one chases these again.
77|
78|- `ineff-runs-3` (round 1, refuted): the micro sorted/unsorted gaps measure per-pair vs grouped kernel choice on identically ordered pairs, not pair order — sorting serving's pairs at 8 rows cannot yield 1.3 ms, and the 32-row gap was never collected.
79|- Round 1's implicit timing claim — that the independent piece timing ranks attempts as the model does — is refuted by the chained measurement: the round-1 experts starting point was 29% faster overlapped and 66% slower chained at 1 row. Round 3 ranks by the chained two-phase timing only.
80|- Round 2 exploration's claim that scalar sums cannot reproduce MMA rounding (round 2 `ineff-baseline-routing-1` as written): refuted by building — routing attempts 2–4 and experts attempt-1's scalar paths are bit-identical to `simdgroup_float8x8` accumulation at all six sizes. Scalar first.
81|
82|### Territories this round opens
83|
84|Each territory below is opened by the line of this section that names it. Explorers of a `baseline-<slot>` territory map that slot's starting-point kernels and `spec.json` — now the code in the slot — with the checklist, and find where they still lose time and why the starting point is no baseline. 92|| `quantized-kernels` (reopened) | Items 1 and 8 of *What is left* — round 2 mapped `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding; round 3 needs its speed: tiling, occupancy and what a fast exact prefill branch (or `max_rows` hand-off) must match or skip. |

1|# Territory: quantized-kernels
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
4|- **Status:** done
5|- **Version:** 3
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-03T22:05Z
7|- **Next:** none (territory mapped; 1 inefficiency open, 1 superseded)
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|This territory is the `affine_gather_*` Metal kernels behind `mx.gather_qmm`
12|(`quantized.h`, `quantized_utils.h`). In MobileMoE-S decode they run the routed
13|experts' gate/up/down products: one `gather_qmm` each per layer per step, always
14|dispatched to `affine_gather_qvm` (proof below). 60 `GatherQMM` launches per step
15|at every row count (`results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md:152-154`).
16|
17|## The checklist
18|
19|### A. `affine_gather_qvm` + `qvm_impl` — the kernel decode actually runs
20|
21|- **Callers:** `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` in
22|  `github.com/ml-explore/mlx`, tag `v0.32.4`,
23|  `mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp:1980-2094`. MobileMoE calls
24|  `mx.gather_qmm(..., transpose=False, group_size=32, bits=4, mode="affine")`
25|  with `x` `[pairs,1,K]` so `M=1` (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:172-184`,
26|  `switch_layers.py:176-199`). Dispatch: `M==1 < vector_limit==4`
27|  (`quantized.cpp:2005,2034`) rules out `gather_qmm`; the rhs fast path needs
28|  `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ && B/E>=4` (`quantized.cpp:2012`) but
29|  `B/E = rows*4/60 <= 2.1` at `rows<=32` (needs `rows>=60`), so it never fires;
30|  `transpose_==false` selects `gather_qvm` (`quantized.cpp:2073-2093`).
31|  Shapes at 1/8/32 rows: gate/up `M=1,N=384,K=768,B=rows*4`; down
32|  `M=1,N=768,K=384,B=rows*4`.
33|- **Callees:** `gather_qvm` launches `affine_gather_qvm` (`quantized.h:2355-2416`,
34|  via `quantized.cpp:1461-1529`) with `group_dims=(32,2,1)=64` threads,
35|  `bn = min(group_size,32)*2 = 64`, grid `(M,(N+63)/64,B)`: gate/up
36|  `(1,6,B)`, down `(1,12,B)`. Each threadgroup runs `qvm_impl`
37|  (`quantized.h:1222-1330`): 2 simdgroups x 32 lanes; each lane owns one K
38|  element per iteration and decodes 32 outputs via `qouter`
39|  (`quantized.h:452-553`, bits=4 path `:503-509`).
40|- **Data:** `w` uint32 `[E,in,out/8]` (4-bit, 8 per word along out),
41|  `scales`/`biases` bfloat16 `[E,in,out/32]`, `x` bfloat16 `[B,1,K]`,
42|  `rhs_indices` uint32 `[B]`, `y` bfloat16 `[B,1,N]`; per-pair offsets via
43|  `adjust_matrix_offsets` (`quantized.h:1636-1688`). Weights/scales read
44|  exactly once per pair: gate pair traffic = 6 tiles x 64 lanes x 24 iters x
45|  16 B weights = 144 KB = `768*384/2` B, scales+biases 36 KB; `x` row re-read
46|  12x per pair per product (each of 6 tiles' 2 simdgroups streams the full row:
47|  `qvm_impl:1275-1287`), ~55 KB x per pair over gate+up+down vs 3.75 KB needed.
48|- **Neighbours:** before: router `inds` (model territory) + `_gather_sort` at
49|  `indices.size>=64` (switch-layers; sort buys only L2 locality since rhs never
50|  fires). Between gate/up and down: activation (other-kernels). After: combine
51|  (model). Replacement must keep G2: every element within 2 bfloat16 ulp of the
52|  reference (1e-3 floor), float32 accumulation, bfloat16 rounding points.
53|- **Cost:** 60 launches/step (~6 us each: routed experts 140 kernels/0.92 ms @1,
54|  `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md:179-185`). Bytes (GPU counters,
55|  `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md:17-18`): experts saves
56|  51 MB read in 0.92 ms @1 (55 GB/s), 908 MB in 14.67 ms @32 (62 GB/s, 31% of
57|  peak). Grids @1 row are 24/24/48 threadgroups (~1.5-3K threads, ~5-10% of
58|  slots; whole-step Compute Occupancy 9%, same table).
59|- **Invariants:** `w = scale*q + bias` per group of 32 along out; output column
60|  `o` in word `o/8` bits `4*(o%8)` (brief); float32 accumulate, bfloat16 store
61|  (`qvm_impl:1324-1329`); fully K/N-aligned launches (384/768 % 64 == 0,
62|  768/384 % 32 == 0), no tail waste.
63|
64|### B. `affine_gather_qmm_n` / `affine_gather_qmm_t` + `qmm_n_impl` / `qmm_t_impl` — never run in decode
65|
66|- **Callers:** only `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` when `M >= vector_limit`
67|  (`quantized.cpp:2034-2051`); decode has `M=1`. Documented so no one chases them.
68|- **Callees:** `affine_gather_qmm_n` (`quantized.h:2501-2568`) /
69|  `_t` (`:2418-2499`), `BM=BN=BK=32`, `QuantizedBlockLoader`
70|  (`quantized.h:665-791`) + `BlockMMA`, `gemm_loop_*` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`).
71|- **Data / Neighbours / Cost / Invariants:** same dtypes and `scale*q+bias`
72|  decoding as (A); zero cost in decode.
73|
74|### C. `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` + `schedule_row_tile` — never run in decode
75|
76|- **Callers:** only when `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ && B/E>=4`
77|  (`quantized.cpp:2012-2032`); needs `rows>=60`, unreachable at `rows<=32`.
78|  This is the kernel that would batch same-expert pairs (offsets +
79|  `schedule_row_tile`, `utils.h:501-542`); its absence is why each pair keeps
80|  its own grid (see ineff-quantized-kernels-1).
81|- **Callees:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` (`quantized.h:2570-2718`), `BM=16,BN=32,
82|  BK=32`, same loader/MMA helpers as (B).
83|- **Data / Neighbours / Cost / Invariants:** same as (A); zero cost in decode.
84|  Note for switch-layers: model sorts at `>=16` rows but dispatch ignores
85|  sortedness below `B/E>=4`.
86|
87|### D. `affine_gather_qmv_fast` / `affine_gather_qmv` — never run in decode
88|
89|- **Callers:** only when `transpose_==true` and `M < vector_limit`
90|  (`quantized.cpp:2053-2071`); MobileMoE uses `transpose=False`.
91|- **Callees:** `qmv_fast_impl` (`quantized.h:850-962`) / `qmv_impl` (`:964-1123`)
92|  via `affine_gather_qmv_fast` (`:2231-2291`) / `affine_gather_qmv` (`:2293-2353`).
93|- **Data / Neighbours / Cost / Invariants:** non-transposed `[E,out,in]` layout
94|  only; zero cost in decode.
95|
96|### E. Shared helpers
97|
98|- `dequantize` (`quantized.h:557-663`), `qdot`/`qdot_safe` (`:221-450`),
99|  `load_vector`/`load_vector_safe` (`:28-219`): per-bit paths, bits=4 used.
100|- `QuantizedBlockLoader` (`:665-791`): dequantize-on-load into threadgroup
101|  memory; used by (B)/(C), not by (A).
102|- `adjust_matrix_offsets` gather variant (`:1636-1688`): per-threadgroup index
103|  lookup, negligible cost.
104|- `gemm_loop_aligned/unaligned/finalize` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`): the
105|  K-loop for (B)/(C) only.
106|
107|## Relations
108|
109|- Feeds from: model (router `inds`, `x`), switch-layers (`_gather_sort` order).
110|- Feeds to: other-kernels (activation reads gate/up outputs), model (combine
111|  reads `y`).
112|- Shared expert uses non-gather quantized matmul: other-kernels territory.
113|
114|## Inefficiencies
115|
116|- `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (open): per-pair qvm grids run expert traffic at

118|- `ineff-quantized-kernels-2` (superseded by `ineff-switch-layers-2`): launch
119|  fusion already covered there, broader; kernel-side numbers moved to a note.

1|# Territory: quantized-kernels (round 2 — prefill path)
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
4|- **Status:** done
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:24:31Z
7|- **Next:** none — prefill checklist filled (§A–§H), 2 inefficiencies posted, note left on `territory-baseline-experts`
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|This territory is MLX's `mx.gather_qmm` Metal kernels behind the `experts`
12|slot (`quantized.h`, `quantized_utils.h`, `utils.h` in the installed
13|0.32.4 headers, dispatch in MLX v0.32.4 `quantized.cpp`). Round 1 mapped
14|it as decode-only: `affine_gather_qvm` runs at every decode size and
15|`affine_gather_qmm_rhs` was listed as never run
16|([`muse-spark/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`](../../exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md)
17|§A/§C, frozen). Round 2 reopens it because the new G2 is bit-exact at
18|prefill sizes too: from 60 rows the reference switches to
19|`gather_qmm_rhs`, whose rounding is now on the correctness path at
20|prefill 127/1,016/2,048 rows. This entry writes only what is new: the
21|prefill dispatch, the `qmm_rhs` arithmetic, and exactly how it diverges
22|from `qvm`. Decode facts that still hold are cited, not rewritten.
23|
24|## The checklist
25|
26|### A. Dispatch — `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` (which kernel runs at each size)
27|
28|- **Callers:** `ref_experts` (`bench/grader/slots.py:55-82`) and the
29|  served twin `SwitchGLU.__call__`
30|  (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:176-199`) both call
31|  `mx.gather_qmm(..., transpose=False, group_size=32, bits=4,
32|  mode="affine", sorted_indices=do_sort)` three times per layer (gate,
33|  up, down), with `do_sort = inds.size >= 64` ⇔ rows ≥ 16
34|  (`slots.py:62`, `switch_layers.py:181`). MLX is 0.32.4
35|  (`.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; print(mx.__version__)"`).
36|  Served weights are `[E, in, out]` via `TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear`
37|  (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:142-184`), hence
38|  `transpose=False`; the `transpose=True` twin in `switch_layers.py:75-90`
39|  is not the served path.
40|- **Callees:** `GatherQMM::eval_gpu`
41|  ([quantized.cpp v0.32.4:1980-2094](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1980-L2094)).
42|  It shapes `K = x.shape(-1)`, `M = x.shape(-2)`,
43|  `N = out.shape(-1)`, `B = out.size()/M/N`,
44|  `E = w.size()/w.shape(-1)/w.shape(-2) = 60`,
45|  `vector_limit = 4` for `transpose=False` (`:2000-2005`). Branch order:
46|  (1) rhs fast path iff `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ && B/E>=4`
47|  (`:2012-2031`); (2) else `gather_qmm` iff `M >= vector_limit`
48|  (`:2034-2054`); (3) else `gather_qmv` iff `transpose_` (`:2056-2075`);
49|  (4) else `gather_qvm` (`:2077-2094`). With `M=1` always (below),
50|  branch (2) never fires in this model.
51|- **Data / shapes at every grader size.** `x` reaching `gather_qmm` is
52|  `[B, 1, K]` with `B = rows*4`: `xx = expand_dims(x, (-2,-3))` then,
53|  when sorting, `_gather_sort` gathers to one row per pair
54|  (`slots.py:61-65`, `switch_layers.py:12-17`); hence `M = 1` and the
55|  `M` argument later passed to `gather_qmm_rhs` is `x.size()/K = B`
56|  (`:2013-2027`). Gate/up: `K=768, N=384`; down (input is the
57|  bfloat16 `silu*up` hidden): `K=384, N=768`.
58|
59|  | rows | B = rows·4 | B/E | sorted (`inds.size≥64`) | MLX kernel |
60|  |---|---|---|---|---|
61|  | 1 (decode) | 4 | 0.07 | no | `gather_qvm` |
62|  | 8 (decode) | 32 | 0.53 | no | `gather_qvm` |
63|  | 32 (decode) | 128 | 2.13 | yes | `gather_qvm` (sorted, still `B/E<4`) |
64|  | 127 (prefill) | 508 | 8.47 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
65|  | 1,016 (prefill) | 4,064 | 67.73 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
66|  | 2,048 (prefill) | 8,192 | 136.53 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
67|
68|  The switch is `rows >= 60` (`B >= 240 ⇔ B/E >= 4`; `B>=16` already
69|  holds from 4 rows). Two thresholds must not be conflated: sorting
70|  starts at 16 rows, the kernel switch at 60. The grader tests 32 and
71|  127, only bracketing 60; the exact threshold comes from this source,
72|  not from grader probing (cf. `territory-grader.md` *What the grader
73|  still cannot see* §1).
74|- **Neighbours:** before: router `inds` + `_gather_sort` (switch-layers
75|  territory); the sort is what sets `right_sorted_`. Between gate/up
76|  and down: compiled `swiglu` on bfloat16 values (other-kernels).
77|  After: `_scatter_unsort` back to positional `[rows, 4, 768]`, then
78|  combine. A replacement slot kernel sees only positional `inds`
79|  (any order, duplicates allowed) — the reference's sort is internal
80|  and invisible in `y` except through the bits.
81|- **Cost:** the dispatch itself launches nothing. Kernel counts and
82|  times per branch are in §C/§F. Prefill sizes are correctness-only in
83|  the grader (no timing; `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`),
84|  so every prefill cost below is arithmetic, not a measured time.
85|- **Invariants:** `right_sorted_` is the Python `sorted_indices`
86|  argument trusted as-is; `gather_qmm_rhs` (§C) is only correct if
87|  `rhs_indices` really is sorted ascending by expert. `M` in the rhs
88|  call means total pairs `B`, not the `M=1` matrix height — the rhs
89|  kernel re-derives row tiles from `offsets` (§D).
90|
91|### B. Host wrapper — `gather_qmm_rhs` (legacy path, the one this GPU runs)
92|
93|- **Callers:** only §A branch (1) (and the `GatherQQMM` twin at
94|  `quantized.cpp:2233-2251`, not this model).
95|- **Callees:** [gather_qmm_rhs v0.32.4:1676-1830](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1676-L1830).
96|  First gate: `is_nax_available() && (enable_tf32 || dtype != float32)`
97|  diverts to `gather_qmm_rhs_nax` (`:1692-1714`). On this machine that
98|  is false: device is Apple M1 Pro `applegpu_g13s`
99|  (`mx.device_info()`), architecture generation 13 < 17, and NAX also
100|  needs macOS 26.2
101|  ([device.cpp v0.32.4:978-995](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/device.cpp#L978-L995)).
102|  So the legacy tiling below is the prefill path here; the NAX variant
103|  (`bm=32/64, bn=bk=64` in the same function, NAX MMA in
104|  `quantized_nax.h`) never runs on the grader GPU. Legacy tiles
105|  (`:1748-1749`): `bm=16, bn=32, bk=32`, `wm=1, wn=2`;
106|  `align_N = (N%32==0)`, `align_K = (K%32==0)` — both true for
107|  384/768, passed as function constants 201/202. Then
108|  `offsets = gather_mm_offsets(indices, E, M=B, ...)` (`:1795`), one
109|  `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` launch with
110|  `group_dims = (32, wn, wm) = 64` threads and
111|  `grid_dims = ((N+31)/32, min(B, ceil(B/16)+E-1), 1)` (`:1817-1819`).
112|- **Data:** `broadcast_with_indices` (`:1721-1733`) copies `x` to
113|  `[B, 1, K]` only if `x.size()/x.shape(-2)/x.shape(-1) != B`; on the
114|  sorted path `x` already has `B` rows (the sort gathered it), so this
115|  is a no-op apart from `ensure_row_contiguous` flag checks, as are
116|  the `w`/`scales`/`biases` normalisations (already contiguous).
117|  `offsets` is `int32[E=60]` (240 B), the per-expert start rows in
118|  sorted order, built by one tiny kernel launch
119|  (`gather_mm_offsets`, host side at
120|  [matmul.cpp v0.32.4:2247-2265](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp#L2247-L2265):
121|  `dispatch_threads(60)`, one threadgroup). Inputs to the Metal kernel,
122|  in buffer order: `x` bfloat16 `[B, K]`, `w` uint32, `scales`/
123|  `biases` bfloat16, `offsets` int32, out `y` bfloat16 `[B, N]`, then
124|  `M=B, N, K, num_groups=60` as constants (`:1821-1835`).
125|- **Neighbours:** same slot edges as §A. The three products in one
126|  layer share the same sorted `idx`, hence the same `offsets` — yet
127|  each of the three calls recomputes it (see
128|  `ineff-quantized-kernels-2`).
129|- **Cost (arithmetic, per layer):** 3 offsets kernels + 3 main kernels
130|  per prefill layer-call (60 + 60 per 20-layer prefill forward),
131|  against 0 + 3 on the decode `qvm` path. Main-kernel dispatched
132|  threadgroups (64 threads each): gate/up `12 × grid_y`, down
133|  `24 × grid_y` with `grid_y = min(B, ceil(B/16)+59)` = 91 / 313 / 571
134|  at B = 508 / 4,064 / 8,192 → gate/up 1,092 / 3,756 / 6,852 and down
135|  2,184 / 7,512 / 13,704 threadgroups per call. Useful row tiles are
136|  fewer (§C, `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`).
137|- **Invariants:** `grid_y` over-provisions by up to `E-1 = 59` tiles:
138|  `ceil(B/16) + E - 1` is the worst case (every expert contributing a
139|  partial tile). Threadgroups whose tile index exceeds the real tile
140|  count return early inside the kernel (§C) — they are launched,
141|  scheduled, and discarded, never incorrect.
142|
143|### C. Metal kernel — `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` + `schedule_row_tile`
144|
145|- **Callers:** §B only. Instantiated for this model as
146|  `affine_gather_qmm_rhs<bfloat16, group_size=32, bits=4, BM=16,
147|  BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2, transpose=false>`
148|  (`quantized.h:2570-2593`).
149|- **Callees:** `schedule_row_tile<BM=16>` (`utils.h:501-542`) maps
150|  `tid.y` to `(y_row, group, tgp_bm)`: it scans experts in lane-parallel
151|  chunks of 32, prefix-summing `ceil((end-start)/16)` per expert from
152|  `offsets`, and returns the expert owning tile `tid.y`, its first
153|  row, and `tgp_bm = min(16, end - row)` valid rows (`utils.h:524-537`).
154|  If no expert owns the tile it returns false and the whole
155|  threadgroup exits (`quantized.h:2637-2640`). Then
156|  `QuantizedBlockLoader` (§D) fills threadgroup `Ws`, `BlockLoader`
157|  fills `Xs` (§E), and `gemm_loop_aligned` /
158|  `gemm_loop_unaligned<...>` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`) drive
159|  `BlockMMA::mma` over `K_it = K/BK` tiles (24 gate/up, 12 down),
160|  with an extra `gemm_loop_finalize` only when `!align_K` — never
161|  here, since `K % 32 == 0` (`quantized.h:2631, 2676-2717`).
162|- **Data:** threadgroup memory `Xs[16 × 40]` + `Ws[32 × 40]` bfloat16
163|  = 1,280 B + 2,560 B = 3,840 B (`BK_padded = BN_padded = 32 + 16/2 =
164|  40`, `quantized.h:2596-2597, 2623-2624`; padding is the usual
165|  16-byte bank-conflict pad). Weight addressing for
166|  `transpose=false`: `wl += group * stride_w` with
167|  `stride_w = K * N_w`, `N_w = N/2` bytes-worth per row — i.e. the
168|  `[E, K, N]`-quantized expert block selected by `group`
169|  (`:2627-2633, 2655-2674`). `x` rows are the sorted pair rows
170|  `y_row .. y_row+tgp_bm-1` of the already-gathered `[B, K]` matrix;
171|  `y` writes go to those same sorted rows, unsorted later by the
172|  caller. Per-output values never mix rows: padded rows (§E) occupy
173|  separate accumulator rows and are discarded by
174|  `store_result_safe` (`:2694`).
175|- **Neighbours:** consumes the sorter's output order directly; this
176|  is the only gather kernel whose addressing depends on pair order
177|  (all others index per pair via `adjust_matrix_offsets`,
178|  `quantized.h:1636-1688`). Its output rows are in sorted-pair order,
179|  so `_scatter_unsort` after the down product is load-bearing for
180|  position, not for bits.
181|- **Cost (arithmetic):** balanced-expert model (counts near the

203|### D. Dequantization — `QuantizedBlockLoader` + `dequantize` (rounding point 1)
204|
205|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` with
206|  `QuantizedBlockLoader<T=bfloat16, BROWS=BK=32, BCOLS=BN=32,
207|  dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=0, tgp_size=64, group_size=32, bits=4>`
208|  (`quantized.h:2613-2621`); same loader family as `qmm_n`/`qmm_t`
209|  (§G).
210|- **Callees:** `load_unsafe`/`load_safe` (`quantized.h:736-770`) call
211|  `dequantize<T, pack_factor=2, bits=4>` (`quantized.h:557-663`,
212|  bits=4 at `:617-623`) per packed byte: with `s = float(scale)`,
213|  `b = float(bias)` it writes
214|  `w_local[2i] = (bfloat16)(s * (w[i] & 0x0f) + b)` and
215|  `w_local[2i+1] = (bfloat16)((s/16) * (w[i] & 0xf0) + b)` into
216|  threadgroup `Ws`. Scales: one `scale`/`bias` pair per thread from
217|  `scales + bi * N/32` (`:733-734`); `group_steps = 32/32 = 1`, so
218|  `next()` advances `scales/biases` by `32*N/32 = N` per K tile
219|  (`:772-790`) — exactly one scale group per `BN=32` output tile and
220|  per `BK=32` row of `K`, matching the `[E, K, N/32]` layout.
221|- **Data:** packed uint32 weights are viewed as bytes (`(device
222|  uint8_t*)w`); each byte yields 2 outputs (low/high nibble), each
223|  `BK×BN = 1,024`-element weight tile dequantized once per
224|  (row tile, K tile) visit into `Ws`, then read by the MMA (§E).
225|  `x` tiles by contrast are copied verbatim (bfloat16 → bfloat16,
226|  exact) by `BlockLoader` (`steel/gemm/loader.h:74-80`).
227|- **Neighbours:** this is the first of the two divergence points
228|  vs `qvm` (§F): the dequantized weight is **rounded to bfloat16
229|  before any multiply**. In `qvm` the same `scale*q + bias` value
230|  stays in float32 registers through the product.
231|- **Cost:** dequant element-ops per product per layer =
232|  `T × K × N` = `T × 294,912` (both products have `K·N = 294,912`):
233|  17.7M / 88.5M / 159.2M at the three prefill sizes (balanced `T`
234|  from §C), each a float mul+add, a float→bfloat round, and a
235|  threadgroup store+reload. This recompute-per-row-tile is the
236|  loader's design (no dequantized-weight cache exists; the full
237|  dequantized expert is 294,912 × 2 B = 590 KB, far above the
238|  32 KB threadgroup limit, so cross-tile reuse would need a device
239|  buffer and an extra kernel — not a free fix).
240|- **Invariants:** `scale`/`bias` themselves are bfloat16 values
241|  upcast to float exactly (bfloat→float is exact), identical to
242|  `qvm`'s inputs; the *only* added rounding is
243|  `static_cast<bfloat16>(s*q + b)`. Relative error up to half a
244|  bfloat ULP (≈2⁻⁹ ≈ 0.2%) per weight element, deterministic per
245|  `(expert, k, n)` — the same rounded weight is reused for all
246|  ≤16 rows of the tile, so errors are correlated across rows
247|  sharing an expert, unlike per-pair float weights.

250|
251|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` instantiates
252|  `BlockMMA<bfloat16, bfloat16, BM=16, BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2,
253|  false, transpose=false, ...>` (`quantized.h:2599-2610`) and
254|  `BlockLoader<bfloat16, BM=16, BK=32, dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=1,
255|  tgp_size=64>` for `x` (`:2611-2612`).
256|- **Callees:** `BlockMMA` (`steel/gemm/mma.h:439-537`) with
257|  `AccumType = float` by default (`mma.h:451`): accumulator
258|  fragments `Ctile` are `float` 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` tiles
259|  (`TM = 16/(8·1) = 2`, `TN = 32/(8·2) = 2` frags per simdgroup).
260|  `mma()` (`mma.h:513-537`) steps `kk` over `BK` in 8-wide frags

262|  `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` (`mma.h:181-206, 406-427`).
263|  Operand fragments are loaded from threadgroup bfloat16 and
264|  widened to float (`BaseMMAFrag::load` casts, `mma.h:57-67`), so
265|  the multiply is float×float with float accumulate — but the
266|  weight operand is the already-bfloat-rounded value of §D, and
267|  the 8-term dot inside each frag is the hardware's tree order,
268|  not a serial FMA chain. `gemm_loop_*` then adds tile results
269|  sequentially over the 24/12 K tiles. Store:
270|  `store_result`/`store_result_safe` cast float → bfloat16 once
271|  (`mma.h:100-112, 540-592`; `quantized.h:2683, 2694`) — the same
272|  single final rounding as `qvm`.

274|  (rows zero-padded by `load_safe` when `tgp_bm < 16`,
275|  `loader.h:83-128`); `Ws` holds the §D dequantized tile. Partial-row
276|  tiles take the `gemm_loop_unaligned<false, true, ...>` branch

278|  discarded.
279|- **Neighbours:** identical bfloat16 store boundary as `qvm`, so
280|  the downstream `swiglu` (gate/up) and down product see the same
281|  *kind* of rounding point — only the float value arriving at the
282|  cast differs.
283|- **Cost:** per product, MMA flops are `2·B_padded·K·N` with
284|  `B_padded = T·16` = 960 / 4,800 / 8,640 vs useful `B` = 508 /
285|  4,064 / 8,192 (padded fractions in `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`).
286|  At 5.2 TFLOPS peak (`claude/GLOSSARY.md:14`) the useful MMA
287|  floors at `2·B·K·N/5.2 TFLOPS` = 57.6 / 461.0 / 929.2 µs per
288|  layer-product (B = 508 / 4,064 / 8,192) if it ran at peak — it
289|  cannot, at `BM=16` tiles with two barriers per 32-K step
290|  (`quantized_utils.h:14-29`), so the path is
291|  overhead/latency-bound, not compute-bound; no measured prefill

294|  **[contiguous 8-wide frag dots] sequentially over BK=32 tiles**,
295|  in increasing K. This is the second divergence from `qvm` (§F):
296|  even with bit-identical weight operands, regrouping a 768-term
297|  float sum this way rounds differently on generic data. Reproducing
298|  it with scalar FMAs is not bit-safe; reproducing it requires the
299|  same 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` fragmentation (same `BK`, same
300|  frag step order) or a proof the hardware order coincides — none
301|  exists in the sources. Warp tiling `WM/WN` only partitions frags
302|  across simdgroups; it does not change a single output's add order.

304|### F. Comparator — `qvm_impl` + `qouter` (what decode runs; delta only)
305|
306|Round 1 §A mapped this kernel fully; only the contrast is new.
307|
308|- **Callers/Callees:** `gather_qvm` host (`quantized.cpp:1462-1529`)
309|  → `affine_gather_qvm` (`quantized.h:2355-2416`) → `qvm_impl`
310|  (`quantized.h:1222-1330`): grid `(1, (N+63)/64, B)` threadgroups of
311|  64 threads; gate/up `(1, 6, B)`, down `(1, 12, B)`. Each lane owns
312|  one strided `K` element per 32-step (`x += block_size` with
313|  `block_size = 32`, `:1275-1287`) and accumulates 32 outputs in
314|  float registers via `qouter` (`quantized.h:452-553`, bits=4 at
315|  `:503-509`): `result += x * (scale*q + bias)` with
316|  `scale`/`bias`/`x` all float, **no bfloat16 rounding of the
317|  weight**, serial per-lane adds in strided-K order
318|  (`k = lane, lane+32, ...`), then one `simd_sum` tree over the 32
319|  lane partials (`:1317-1321`) and a single float→bfloat16 store
320|  (`:1324-1329`).
321|- **The two divergences, side by side:**
322|
323|  | aspect | `gather_qvm` (decode, rows < 60) | `gather_qmm_rhs` (prefill, rows ≥ 60) |
324|  |---|---|---|
325|  | weight value | `float(scale)·q + float(bias)` kept in float32 | same value rounded to bfloat16 in threadgroup (§D) |
326|  | K grouping | strided lanes: lane `l` sums `k≡l (mod 32)` serially, then `simd_sum` tree | contiguous: 8-wide frag dots, sequential over BK=32 tiles (§E) |
327|  | rows sharing work | none: one grid slice per pair | ≤16 sorted rows share each weight tile |
328|  | final rounding | float → bfloat16 once after `simd_sum` | float → bfloat16 once after MMA — identical point |

330|  Either divergence alone breaks bit-equality (measured: 62.4–62.6%
331|  of experts outputs differ at all three prefill sizes, max
332|  43/65/110.5 ULP, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-experts.json`;

335|  `float(scale·q+bias)` not representable in bfloat16 and any
336|  `x ≠ 0` — the two references already disagree on that product

338|  size branch is required** — `qvm` arithmetic below 60 rows,
339|  `qmm_rhs` arithmetic (bfloat-rounded dequant tiles + 8-wide frag
340|  accumulation) at/above 60 rows — or a proof of coincidence that
341|  the 62% differ rate rules out empirically. The branch threshold
342|  must be the dispatch rule `rows >= 60` (pairs `>= 240`, `E=60`),

345|  prefill branch is free (§C invariant); per-row accumulation is
346|  not.

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write faster MobileMoE-S kernels, for decoding and prompt processing
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|A request goes through two phases: **prompt processing** (the prefill), which runs its whole prompt through the model, and **decoding**, one step per generated token. An improvement must hold in both: faster in one, and no slower in the other ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A kernel that speeds up the decode step but slows the prefill is not an improvement.
12|
13|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
14|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
15|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
16|
17|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
18|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
19|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
20|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
21|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
22|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
23|
24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
95|
96|## Tools and limits
97|
98|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
99|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
100|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes, longer for an attempt much slower than the reference at the prefill sizes; stop one that runs past 15.
101|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
102|
103|## Rules of this session
104|
105|These keep your work apart from everyone else's. Git hooks and an audit script enforce them, and a commit that breaks them is refused.
106|
107|- **Write only inside `muse-spark/`.** Never change `bench/`, `claude/`, `results/`, `tools/`, `third_party/`, or any other file. A copy of the grader you edit is never used.
108|- **Commit only on `muse-agent`,** with the co-author trailer your settings add: `Co-Authored-By: Muse Spark (Meta Model API) <muse-spark@meta-model-api.invalid>`. Start each subject with `Muse Spark:`. No other co-author.
109|- **Never push, merge, rebase, change git config, or skip hooks.**
110|- **Don't read `.env`** or any credentials file.
111|- One commit per attempt, after you've run the grader on it, so the history shows every attempt in order.
112|
113|## Your files
114|
115|```
116|muse-spark/
117|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
118|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
119|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
120|    spec.json                                the launch spec
