{"content":"# Territory: grader — what changed in round 3 (ADR 0011, ADR 0013)

- **Owner:** explorer-grader
- **Status:** exploring
- **Version:** 1
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T17:37:46Z
- **Next:** fill checklist for the two-phase judgment, max_rows, check_sizes, G3 and check_ready; deliver notes to baseline-*/g3 entries when they land

## What it does

Rounds 1 and 2's entries ([`muse-spark/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../exploration/territory-grader.md) and [`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md), frozen) mapped the grader through ADR 0010: bit-exact G2 at six sizes, chained piece timing at decode sizes only, median-vs-median `beats_compiled`, and the paired sign-test `--baseline` bar. Round 3 changes the judgment ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)): the piece timing runs at all six sizes with paired per-size verdicts, `beats_compiled` needs one phase faster and neither slower, and a spec may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference via `max_rows`. G3 moves to vLLM-only two-phase judgment (decode step, prompt time, whole-request time), and the lead's ready check ([`bench/grader/check_ready.py`](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py), [ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)) runs that same G3 inside the round. This entry writes only the delta. G1/G2 mechanics, the spec language, `capture`, and `gpu_lock` are cited to rounds 1–2, not re-described.

## Checklist

### 1. `check_candidate.py` — paired per-size verdicts and the two-phase judgment (check_candidate.py:51-58, 224-264, 345-378)

- **Callers:** builders: `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt> <slot> [--out FILE]` ([check_candidate.py:15](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); no `--baseline` this round — no slot has one (round-3 README *Starting point*). Holds the GPU lock for the whole run ([check_candidate.py:294](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). One grader run is one attempt (ADR 0013); builders keep `grade.json` in the attempt folder.
- **Callees:** unchanged: `slots.build`/`load_inputs`/`capture_prefill`/`load_model`; `mx.eval` for correctness and timing; `mx.compile(ref)` for the compiled bar only.
- **Data:** `ROWS = (1, 8, 32)`, `PHASES = {"decode": "rows ", "prefill": "prefill rows "}` ([check_candidate.py:51-52](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); `REPEATS = 30`, `WINS_NEEDED = 22` computed by the same one-sided sign test at p < 0.01 as round 2 ([check_candidate.py:53-58](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).
- **What is new — paired timing at all six sizes:** timing runs only if G2 passes ([check_candidate.py:345](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), over the same six size inputs as correctness (decode `load_inputs` + prefill `capture_prefill`, [check_candidate.py:308-312,349](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per size and part, `paired_times` runs candidate and compiled (plus baseline when given) in rotating order within each of 30 repeats, each repeat a full chained 20-layer eval ([check_candidate.py:224-236](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per-part times are summed per repeat before wins are counted ([check_candidate.py:364-366](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), so for `routing+combine` the verdict is on summed time, as in round 2. The plain `reference` is still timed by unpaired median `timed()` ([check_candidate.py:360](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) — informational only, no verdict against it.
- **What is new — `compare`/`judge`:** per size, the candidate is `faster` with ≥22 wins, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same` ([check_candidate.py:239-245](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per phase: `faster` iff every size is, `slower` iff any size is, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` (and `beats_baseline`, same rule) is true iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower` ([check_candidate.py:248-264,377-378](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Consequences: two `faster` + one `same` in a phase is `not slower`, not `faster` — a single noisy size now blocks the bar instead of passing it (round 2's median-only rule passed on noise up to 5%, [ADR 0011:26](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); a `same` everywhere attempt never beats.
- **Invariants:** verdict JSON gains per-size `wins_vs_compiled`/`vs_compiled` (and baseline twins) plus `phases_vs_compiled`/`beats_compiled` ([check_candidate.py:368-378](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:207). On G2 failure there is still no timing at all.

### 2. `slots.py` `build` — the `max_rows` hand-off (slots.py:304-337)

- **Callers:** `check_candidate.load` and `time_candidates.Variants`/`implementations`, via `slots.build(spec, sources, slot)` — so the hand-off applies identically in the piece timing, G2, G3 and the ready check.
- **What it does:** with `"max_rows"` in the spec (per part for `routing+combine`, brief:174), `run()` sends inputs with `rows > max_rows` to the slot's reference under `mx.compile` instead of the kernels ([slots.py:333-337](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). `rows` is read from the first slot input's `shape[0]` ([slots.py:334](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Validation: int ≥ 1, bools rejected ([slots.py:327-331](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); `compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])` is built once per `build` call.
- **Grading:** "bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes" (brief:173). G2 checks `run()`, so sizes above `max_rows` exercise the compiled reference through the attempt's own dispatch; the compiled reference of each slot was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes on 2026-11-04 (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`, [ADR 0011:34](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). Timing above `max_rows` runs the bar's own code, so it reads `same` by construction, never better ([ADR 0011:35](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)) — the claim for such an attempt is "faster decode, unchanged prefill" ([ADR 0011:48](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)).
- **The experts switch at 60 rows:** from 60 rows MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`) with different rounding ([slots.py:219-220](../../../bench/grader/slots.py); brief:187). Kernels running at rows ≥ 60 must match the large kernel's rounding; `max_rows` ≤ 59 keeps decode-built kernels on the `gather_qvm` side only. The boundary agent checks the hand-off sits on the right side of 60 for experts ([ADR 0011:47](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). Round 2's checked hand-off copy used `max_rows` 59 (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).
- **What the grader cannot see here:** any `max_rows` in 32..126 behaves identically at all six G2 sizes and all six timing sizes (tested sizes on each side are 32 and 127) — the grader cannot tell 59 (right side of 60) from 100 (wrong side). §4's `check_sizes.py` (59/60/61) is what distinguishes them; see *What the grader still cannot see* item 1.

### 3. `capture_prefill`'s `tokens` parameter and `check_sizes.py` — G2 between the six sizes (slots.py:214-255; check_sizes.py)

- **New to these entries** (`check_sizes.py` arrived with Claude's "Measure round 2" commit `f679d23`, after round-2 exploration; the `tokens` parameter serves it). `capture_prefill(model, requests, with_weights, tokens)` with `tokens=N` records the first N tokens of a one-request prefill — N rows per layer ([slots.py:214-255](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)).
- **What it does:** `check_sizes.py <out.json> SLOT=FOLDER...` applies `check_candidate`'s checks and pass rule to every layer's slot inputs at `SIZES = (2,3,5,15,16,17,31,33,40,59,60,61,64,65,100,128,129,200,256,257,500,768,769,1024,1500)` ([check_sizes.py:26-27](../../../bench/grader/check_sizes.py)) — either side of the 16-row sort switch and the 60-row MLX switch, and inside each row-count regime an attempt names ([check_sizes.py:1-13](../../../bench/grader/check_sizes.py)). It loads the attempt's `run()` functions, so `max_rows` dispatch is exercised: sizes above `max_rows` test the hand-off path. GPU job under the lock ([check_sizes.py:38](../../../bench/grader/check_sizes.py)); prints per-size pass/FAIL and writes the report JSON.
- **Status:** boundary tooling, not a gate — G1/G2 still test exactly the six sizes. It closes round 2's *can't see* item 1 (branch-on-rows kernels exact at six sizes, wrong between) where the boundary agent runs it, and it is the tool that verifies a hand-off's side of 60.

### 4. `time_candidates.py` — two-phase vLLM G3 (time_candidates.py:51-55, 163-201, 204-265)

- **Callers:** Claude after the round; inside the round, only `check_ready.py` calls it (in-process, pinned argv). Plain-MLX mode still runs token checks and timing for diagnosis, but the G3 verdict reads vLLM runs only ([time_candidates.py:170](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)).
- **Protocol:** `G3_SETTINGS = "1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024"`, `G3_REPEATS = 5`, 256 output tokens ([time_candidates.py:51-55,217](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)); vLLM with 512 MiB KV cache, 1 GiB when a prompt length exceeds 128 ([time_candidates.py:247-257](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)).
- **What it times** (`MEASURES`, [time_candidates.py:54](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)): `decode` = `period_median_ms`, the steady decode-step period; `prompt` = `prompt_ms`, first forward pass to the first step with no prompt tokens left — "until every prompt was processed" ([repeat_fixes.py:277-282](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)); `request` = `wall_ms`, the whole run's wall time. Variants: `base`, `compiled-<slot>`, `muse-<slot>`, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` with several slots ([time_candidates.py:111-132](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)) — a combination is measured as one, never summed.
- **The pass rule** (`against`/`g3`, [time_candidates.py:163-201](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)): per setting and measure, `faster`/`slower` mean the two 5-repeat ranges don't overlap, else `same`. Per measure: `faster` iff every setting is, `slower` iff any is, else `not slower`. A `muse-*` variant passes against a bar iff decode or prompt is `faster` and none of the three is `slower`; `g3` needs that against both `base` and its `compiled-*` counterpart. A `muse-*` variant without its compiled counterpart is not judged ([time_candidates.py:179-181](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)). Verdict to `g3-vllm.json`.
- **Why 5 repeats:** with 3, two identical engines' ranges miss per direction with p = 1/20, and 8 "never slower" checks per phase fail an unchanged phase ~1/3 of the time; with 5 it is 1/252 per check, ~3% over 8 ([ADR 0011:40](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). The motivating case: a hand-off copy at `max_rows` 59 read `slower` on prompt time at 32×1,024 by 0.5% (ranges 16 ms apart) although above 59 rows it *is* the compiled reference. Residual ~3% false-`slower` risk per phase stands.
- **Token checks:** `rf.vllm_checks` — greedy tokens (24, temperature 0) at 1 and 32 requests of 128-token prompts, plus one steady decode step's kernel count, per variant ([repeat_fixes.py:175-176](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)).

### 5. `check_ready.py` — the in-round ready check (whole file)

- **Callers:** the lead only, at most twice per round (ADR 0013, skill v8). `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_ready.py <new out folder> SLOT=FOLDER...`, or `--audit <out folder>` ([check_ready.py:24-25](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
- **What it runs:** `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3 protocol fixed in code — four workloads, 5 repeats, 256 tokens, every submitted slot in one call so the combination is measured as `muse-all` ([check_ready.py:48-56,81-86](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). No flag changes the protocol; `check_protocol` stops before any GPU work if `time_candidates.py`'s G3 constants changed ([check_ready.py:63-70](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). The out folder must be new ([check_ready.py:76-78](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Cost: ~10–15 min per slot, ~21 min for two, blocking builders' grader runs (ADR 0013).
- **What it audits** (the log, never the verdict file, [check_ready.py:103-150](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)): (1) exactly one `ready-check` marker with the protocol; (2) every timed run is vLLM at a G3 workload with 256 tokens and all three measurements present; (3) the variants are exactly `base`, `compiled-<slot>`/`muse-<slot>` per slot, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` with >1 slot, with repeats 0–4 at each workload; (4) every non-base variant keeps the unchanged model's greedy tokens at 1 and 32 requests — and a `compiled-*` variant that changes tokens is "no bar", invalidating the run ([check_ready.py:131-140](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)); (5) `g3-vllm.json` equals the G3 verdict recomputed from the log ([check_ready.py:142-148](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
- **What it writes:** `ready-verdict.json` — per `muse-*` variant its pass (G3 and same tokens), `vs` per bar, `phases` per bar, plus per-variant/workload/measurement median/min/max/n, `same_tokens`, `pass`, `judged`, `problems` ([check_ready.py:152-174](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Exit 0: every `muse-*` passes; 1: a variant fails — the verdict stands; 2: the run stopped or broke the protocol — no verdict, may rerun in a new folder ([check_ready.py:20-22,205-213](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
- **`--audit`:** re-checks a finished folder without the GPU; compares `pass`, `judged`, `variants`, `medians`, `same_tokens` against the saved `ready-verdict.json`, writes nothing, exits 2 on disagreement ([check_ready.py:195-203](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Used by the swarm's checker and by Claude after the round. Tested against 13 gaming tricks plus the control (`bench/grader/test_check_ready.py`, ADR 0013); verified live on round 2's submission (`results/runs/2026-11-04-ready-check/`, exit 1: routing fails on prompt time, combine on the decode step, the pair on all three).
- **Invariants:** only a passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's post-round G3 stays the authority (ADR 0013).

### 6. Verdict shape delta (check_candidate.py:296-302, 336-378)

`{slot, g1, g2, beats_compiled, correctness: {"<part> <kind> <rows>": {...}}, timing_us_per_layer: {"rows N"/"prefill rows N": {reference, candidate, compiled, wins_vs_compiled, vs_compiled}}, phases_vs_compiled}` plus, with `--baseline`, `{baseline, beats_baseline, wins_needed, phases_vs_baseline}`. Size labels carry the phase prefix (`rows 32` vs `prefill rows 127`), which is what `judge()` splits on.

## What the grader still cannot see

Round 2's list stands except item 3 (prefill speed — now timed) and item 5c (median-only `beats_compiled` — now a sign test at every size). What is new or still open:

1. **`max_rows` between the tested sizes.** Any value in 32..126 is identical at all six G2/timing sizes; the grader cannot see which side of 60 an experts hand-off sits on. `check_sizes.py` (59/60/61) closes it where the boundary agent runs it — the piece verdict never does.
2. **Kernel speed at 33–126 rows is unmeasured by the piece timing** (decode sizes stop at 32, prefill starts at 127). With `max_rows` > 32 the kernels run there in real serving (vLLM chunked prefills), and only G3's prompt time at its four workloads can show it — and only if a chunk lands there. Hypotheses with `max_rows` above 32 carry this as **Unverified**.
3. **Sizes above 2,048 rows** are tested nowhere (G2 stops at 2,048, `check_sizes` at 1,500); real prefill chunks reach 2,048 under `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`, so this is the top edge, not a gap in practice.
4. **Prefill beyond the first chunk** of 128-token seeded-random prompts, other prompt lengths, real-token distributions, mixed prefill+decode batches — unchanged from round 2. `check_sizes` varies the first chunk's length but nothing else.
5. **Hand-off exactness above `max_rows` at untested sizes** rests on compiled==reference there, shown at the six sizes (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`) plus the hand-off path at `SIZES` wherever `check_sizes` runs the attempt.
6. **Whole-request noise at 1 request:** repeats spread 6–41%, so G3/ready-check there mostly say `same` — which passes "never slower" without showing a gain ([ADR 0011:52](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A real small gain hidden by noise is lost too, because a verdict stands (ADR 0013).
7. **A log invented whole** passes the audit; only Claude's independent G3 catches it ([ADR 0013:69-72](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)). Old logs without marker/token count are refused, not evidence.
8. **Threadgroup memory** still unchecked (only the ≤1024-thread product, [slots.py:341-342](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); Metal rejects oversize kernels as opaque G1 exceptions.
9. **Link-kernel caveats carried over** (round-2 item 5a/b/d): 20 link kernels' additive cost in every timed eval; the 10% chain-fidelity figure unverified by the grader; host wall time with CPU dispatch inside; clocks unpinned.
10. **Plain-MLX behaviour is no longer gated** — G3 and the ready check judge vLLM runs only (`time_candidates plain` remains for diagnosis). Round 2's plain-vs-vLLM divergences (combine at 32, all-three at 8) are now visible in-round only through the ready check's vLLM lens.

- **Fed by:** model territory (`MoE.__call__`, what `make_moe_call` mirrors); `bench/micro/breakdown.py` (`MODEL`, `PREFILL_TOKENS`, chunking, vLLM runner); `bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py` (`time_variants`, `vllm_checks`, `prompt_ms`); quantized-kernels territory (the 60-row switch, prefill tiling); `models/muse-inputs/` (captured decode inputs).

# Exploration: round 3 — analysis

**Version:** v1 · 2026-11-04T17:36:02Z · skill version 8

## Tracker

| Territory | Agent | Status | Inefficiencies | Updated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline-experts` | `explorer-baseline-experts` | exploring | — | 2026-11-04 17:36Z |
| `baseline-routing` | `explorer-baseline-routing` | exploring | — | 2026-11-04 17:36Z |

## Starting point

Round 3 builds on rounds 1 (`muse-spark/`, frozen, tagged `muse-round-1`) and 2 (`muse-spark/round-2/`, frozen, tagged `muse-round-2`) as measured independently by Claude in `claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` (2026-11-04, on `main` after merging round 2 at `4033cae`). Round 2 ran skill version 5 as Muse Wonder. The judgment changed for round 3 ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)): an improvement must hold in both phases, decode and prefill — faster in one, slower in neither — against the unchanged model and the compiled reference, in the piece timing (`beats_compiled`) and in G3, where no whole request may be slower. A slot's baseline is its best attempt so far that passes the current G2, has `beats_compiled` true, and passes G3; anything else that passes G2 is a starting point. **No slot has a baseline.** A new attempt must pass G1 and G2 (bit-exact at 1, 8, 32 and 127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) and beat the compiled reference in the chained two-phase timing; there is no `--baseline` to pass. Inside the round, the lead's ready check (`bench/grader/check_ready.py`, [ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)) times every candidate exactly as Claude's G3 will, and only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`.

Round 2's final attempts, their piece timings and G3 effects are summarised per slot. Piece timings are Claude's re-grade on main with the two-phase grader (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`), chained µs per layer as reference / compiled / candidate. G3 is the vLLM decode-step change against the unchanged model (median of 3 shuffled repeats, `console-vllm.txt`) plus the whole-request throughput change at 1×128, 8×128, 32×128 and 32×1,024 (prompt-time multiple in brackets, `results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/`). Round 2's own prediction was decode-only (piece basis × 20 layers plus compiled G3 offsets); both are quoted so the gap can be seen.

### Per slot

#### `experts` — starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7`

- **What it is.** One fused per-pair kernel (512 threads per (row, expert-slot) pair, `rows*4` threadgroups): interleaved gate/up plus interleaved down in a merged K loop, intermediates in threadgroup memory (3,840 B), full-bfloat16 silu-mul. Per-block numerics replicate MLX's `affine_gather_qvm` bitwise at decode sizes; a `rows >= 60` branch runs a scalar `qmm_accum` (bfloat16-rounded dequant, contiguous `BK=32` order) to match `gather_qmm_rhs` at prefill sizes. See `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7/notes.md` and `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md`.
- **Piece timing** (`grade-phases-experts-attempt-7.json`). Decode: 84.0 / 78.6 / **92.1** at 1 row (slower), 239.3 / 235.5 / **162.8** at 8 rows, 806.5 / 797.8 / **515.3** at 32 rows. Prefill: 963.4 / 960.8 / **15220.0** at 127 rows (15.8× compiled), 3979.3 / 4306.0 / **119154.4** at 1,016 rows (27.7×), 7359.8 / 11998.9 / **240681.1** at 2,048 rows (20.1×). `beats_compiled` false: decode `slower` (the 1-row size), prefill `slower` (every size).
- **G3 effect vs prediction.** Round 2 dropped this attempt and predicted nothing for it; Claude timed it anyway. Per decode step in vLLM: +0.29 ms (+5.4%) with 1 request, −1.22 ms (−8.4%) with 8, −5.35 ms (−17.5%) with 32. Over whole requests (with routing attempt-4): throughput −10.0% / −37.5% / −48.0% / −82.5%, with prompt processing 6.63× / 14.50× / 12.50× / 13.09× slower than the unchanged engine. The fastest exact decode step measured (routing + experts: −20% with 32 requests in plain MLX) is the slowest whole request.
  - **Reason (measured).** The scalar prefill branch copies `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding but not its speed: every prompt chunk here has at least 128 rows, so it always runs that branch. At 1 row the fused designs plateau at 92–110 µs per layer chained against 73–87 for the compiled reference across six exact attempts — width, group count, interleave and store parallelism moved 8/32 rows and none moved 1 row by more than ~12 µs (round 2's *What building taught*).
- **What keeps it from being a baseline.** It passes G2 bit-exact at all six sizes, but it is slower than the compiled reference at 1 row and at every prefill size, so prompts take 6.6 to 14.5 times as long and whole requests lose 10% to 83% of throughput.
- **Where it still spends its time.** At 1 row: the ~19 µs gap to compiled is the `tg_x` load, silu, the two barriers and chained fixed cost — the down interleave proved the down waves were already hidden across simdgroups (attempt-7 notes, miss analysis). At prefill sizes: the scalar `qmm_accum` branch, 15,220 µs per layer where compiled takes 961. Per-pair weight re-reads remain at all sizes (552,960 B per pair).

#### `routing` — starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-4`

- **What it is.** One fused kernel per layer: scalar sums over the same partition/K order as MLX's three regimes (GEMV at `rows == 1`, split-K while `rows <= 768`, regular above), staged `w_router` blocks in threadgroup memory (coalesced `float4` loads, 28,080 B of 32 KB, 24 barriers on the scalar path), MLX's verbatim sigmoid, strictly-greater insertion top-4, `((w0+w1)+w2)+w3` normalise. See `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-4/notes.md` and `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-2-routing-exact.md`.
- **Piece timing** (`grade-phases-routing-attempt-4.json`). Decode: 68.4 / 65.1 / **49.8** at 1 row, 169.2 / 135.7 / **113.5** at 8 rows, 159.3 / 145.2 / **121.3** at 32 rows — faster at every decode size. Prefill: 102.3 / 87.3 / **227.1** at 127 rows (2.6× compiled), 231.3 / 221.1 / **1298.8** at 1,016 rows (5.9×), 310.0 / 290.4 / **2513.0** at 2,048 rows (8.7×). `beats_compiled` false: decode `faster`, prefill `slower`.
- **G3 effect vs prediction.** Per decode step in vLLM: −0.47 / −0.43 / −0.54 ms at 1 / 8 / 32 requests — it passed every rule of its time (faster than both the unchanged model and the compiled reference at all sizes, in both engines). Round 2 predicted −0.48 / −0.50 / −0.49 ms from the chained piece timing; the 8-request figure came in 0.07 ms short, the others match. Over whole requests: throughput +10.2% / +1.8% / +0.3% / −3.5%, with prompts 1.07–1.10× slower. Under the rule set after this measurement it fails, so it is no baseline.
  - **Reason (measured).** The staged scalar path wins at decode sizes but scales badly: 227 µs per layer at 127 rows where compiled takes 87, widening to 8.7× at 2,048 rows. The 28 KB threadgroup footprint caps residency as row counts grow.
- **What keeps it from being a baseline.** It passes G2 bit-exact at all six sizes, but it is slower than the compiled reference at every prefill size, so prompts take 7–10% longer and whole requests with 1,024-token prompts lose 3.5%.
- **Where it still spends its time.** At prefill sizes: the staged scalar chain and its 24 barriers per row (2,513 µs per layer at 2,048 rows vs 290 compiled). At decode sizes it already beats compiled everywhere (49.8 / 113.5 / 121.3); the per-row `w_router` re-read and the serial thread-0 scan are untouched.

#### `combine` — starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1`

- **What it is.** One fused kernel per layer: thread per output element on a `rows×768` grid, volatile-barrier stepwise fold `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3` with a rounding after every op, one bfloat16 round, single-rounding bfloat16 `+ shared`. See `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1/notes.md` and `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-3-combine-exact.md`.
- **Piece timing** (`grade-phases-combine-attempt-1.json`). Decode: 52.8 / 53.4 / **45.7** at 1 row, 71.2 / 56.4 / **47.9** at 8 rows, 87.0 / 69.1 / **64.6** at 32 rows. Prefill: 87.8 / 66.1 / **62.8** at 127 rows, 425.2 / 271.6 / **226.5** at 1,016 rows, 846.2 / 520.4 / **273.0** at 2,048 rows — faster at all six sizes. `beats_compiled` true. It is the only starting point that beats the compiled reference in both phases.
- **G3 effect vs prediction.** Per decode step in vLLM: −0.37 / −0.20 / **+1.05 ms** at 1 / 8 / 32 requests. Round 2 predicted −0.36 / −0.35 / −0.35 ms; at 32 requests the sign flips. With 8 requests its median sits above the compiled reference in vLLM. Over whole requests (with routing): throughput +15.9% / +2.1% / −2.7% / −4.1%.
  - **Reason (not known).** A G3 loss of 1.05 ms is about 52 µs per layer, more than the kernel's whole chained time in the grader (64.6 µs per layer at 32 rows, of which the loss alone exceeds the kernel's work as the grader runs it). The cost comes from how the kernel sits in the step, which the grader doesn't reproduce. Round 3's first question is why.
- **What keeps it from being a baseline.** It passes G1, G2 and `beats_compiled`, but its decode step in G3 was 1.05 ms slower than the unchanged model's with 32 requests, for a reason the grader doesn't show.
- **Where it still spends its time.** In the grader: nothing further — it sits on the chained floor (~32–40 µs per layer at decode sizes) and wins everywhere. In the step at 32 requests: the unexplained ~52 µs per layer.

#### All three together

Round 2's submission (routing + combine) changes the vLLM decode step by −0.73 / −0.74 / **+0.53 ms** at 1 / 8 / 32 requests, against a prediction of −0.84 / −0.85 / −0.84 ms: combine's slowdown outweighs routing's saving with 32 requests. Round 2's pairings run (plain MLX) found every pair within 0.5 ms of its parts' sum, but all three together with 8 requests 2.8 ms slower than their parts (+0.94 ms measured against −1.87 ms summed) — the second set of kernels to show it, so the cause is likely in how the step runs with all three slots replaced at that size, not in one kernel. Not explained. Every round-2 variant keeps the model's greedy tokens in both engines at 1 and 32 requests (round 1's change them with 32).

Round 2 ran the grader exactly once per attempt: 13 runs for 13 attempts (experts 7, routing 4, combine 2).

### What is left

Confirmed inefficiencies not yet built or not fully removed, ranked by predicted saving against the compiled reference (no slot has a baseline, so the reference is the bar everywhere). Savings span both phases now: decode shares use the plain-MLX step denominators 4.75 / 13.37 / 28.19 ms at 1 / 8 / 32 rows, prefill effects are prompt-time multiples and whole-request throughput from Claude's engine comparison. Exactness gates are solved in every slot — all three starting points pass G2 at all six sizes — so nothing below is blocked on correctness.

1. **Experts prefill path 15–28× slower than compiled.** The slot's scalar `qmm_accum` branch takes 15,220 / 119,154 / 240,681 µs per layer where compiled takes 961 / 4,306 / 11,999, and prompt processing runs 6.6 to 14.5 times slower, costing 10% to 83% of whole-request throughput. Removing it — a fast exact prefill branch, or a `max_rows` hand-off that keeps prefill-sized inputs on the compiled reference (Claude checked the hand-off bit-exact on a copy with `max_rows` 59, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`) — recovers the whole loss while keeping the 8/32-row decode wins (−1.22 / −5.35 ms per step). This is Claude's question 4 for round 3 (prefill half).
2. **Experts 1-row decode latency.** The starting point chains at 92.1 µs per layer against 78.6 for compiled (+13.5; G3 +0.29 ms with 1 request), the last size where it loses. Six exact fused packings plateaued at 92–110 µs; round 2's summary suggests copying the reference's unfused structure exactly for small row counts. Worth up to ~0.3 ms per step at 1 request plus unlocking `beats_compiled` on the decode phase. Claude's question 1.
3. **Routing prefill 2.6/5.9/8.7× slower than compiled.** 227 / 1,299 / 2,513 µs per layer against 87 / 221 / 290; prompts take 7–10% longer and 1,024-token-prompt requests lose 3.5% throughput. Same two outs as experts: a prefill branch that scales, or `max_rows`. Decode already wins everywhere, so the hand-off alone banks the slot if the decode win survives composition. Claude's question 4 (prefill half).
4. **Why combine attempt-1 costs ~1 ms in the step with 32 requests and not in the grader.** The chained piece timing has it faster (64.6 vs 69.1 µs per layer); G3 has it 1.05 ms slower per step. No hypothesis can bank combine until the mechanism is found — it may be a property of the kernel (grid shape, cache behaviour) or of the step around it. Claude's question 2.
5. **Why all three slots replaced at once lose 2.8 ms with 8 requests.** Every pair adds up; all three together miss by 2.8 ms in plain MLX (round 2 pairs run), repeating round 1's shape. Until it is understood, per-slot piece wins may not compose into a G3 win. Claude's question 3. Carried as a constraint on every hypothesis; the ready check measures each candidate alone and all together, so round 3 sees composition inside the round.
6. **Experts per-pair weight re-reads persist** (round 2 `ineff-baseline-experts-3`, confirmed): 908 MB read vs 443 MB distinct at 32 rows, floor 2.33 ms per step at 32 rows, 0 banked — grouped designs lost in both rounds on duty-cycle ceilings. Banks only if a grouped design holds the chained rate on distinct bytes.
7. **Routing `w_router` re-read per row** (round 2 `ineff-baseline-routing-4`, confirmed): excess floor 0 / 0.13 / 0.57 ms per step; round 1's tiled-sharing attempt was slower everywhere, and attempt-4 already wins in spite of it. Upper bound only.
8. **Prefill-only reference waste, now judged** (round 2 `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`, `-2`, confirmed): BM=16 padded tiles waste 47.1 / 15.3 / 5.2% of issued row-work at 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows, and `gather_mm_offsets` is recomputed 3× per layer (≤0.26 ms per chunk forward). Round 2 ranked these at 0 µs of decode time; under two-phase judgment they are prompt-time savings a fast prefill branch takes for free.

**Slots not yet tried.** `routing+combine` (brief: both slots, each with its own kernels, in one candidate; the grader tests each part on its own and the combine part receives the reference routing weights). Neither round has graded one `routing-combine` folder. It remains available; since the parts are graded independently it is packaging unless a shared design emerges.

**Recommendations outside the slots** stand as written in `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md` and round 2's exploration README *Recommendations*; Claude's measurement did not test them. In brief: attention K/V re-read per query head (up to ~2 ms at 32 rows); split-K partial traffic from 14 rows (≈2.4 ms upper bound at 32 rows, unmeasured); 60 q/k/v `[0]` gathers + copies (−0.21 ms measured at 8 rows, `squeeze(0)` fix); ~2 ms engine CPU per 1-row step (≈0.5 ms of Python fixes); prefill tile waste and redundant `gather_mm_offsets` in MLX's `gather_qmm_rhs` (time-to-first-token only — now prompt time, item 8 above). They are for surucuonur's team; no hypothesis targets them.

### Refuted claims

No one chases these again.

- `ineff-runs-3` (round 1, refuted): the micro sorted/unsorted gaps measure per-pair vs grouped kernel choice on identically ordered pairs, not pair order — sorting serving's pairs at 8 rows cannot yield 1.3 ms, and the 32-row gap was never collected.

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*

You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.

## The task

Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.

A request goes through two phases: **prompt processing** (the prefill), which runs its whole prompt through the model, and **decoding**, one step per generated token. An improvement must hold in both: faster in one, and no slower in the other ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A kernel that speeds up the decode step but slows the prefill is not an improvement.

1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.

**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
=== ADR0010:35,50 ===
  - `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` now takes several `SLOT=FOLDER` attempts.
  - It times each slot alone, against its own compiled reference, and all of them together.

## Consequences

- **No round-1 attempt passes the new G2,** so round 2 has no baseline in any slot. Its bar is the compiled reference. Round 1's final attempts are its starting points, named in Claude's findings.
- **The experts slot needs a kernel exact at prefill sizes,** matching `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding from 60 rows on, or a single design whose rounding matches both of MLX's kernels.
- **A grader run takes longer.** It loads the model (760 MB) for every slot and runs three prefill chunks.
- **The piece timing now includes one small link kernel per layer** for every function timed. That brings the reference and the candidate closer in relative terms, but not in µs.
- **Not covered:** prefill speed. G3 times decode steps only, so a kernel slower at prefill sizes would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token.

## Considered options

- **Decode calls only,** with MLX's code in the prefill. The kernels would need to be exact only at decode sizes, but they would no longer replace the whole MoE block. Not chosen: surucuonur asked for every call.
- **Keep the tolerances, and relax the token rule** to counting the sequences that differ. Simpler kernels, but the claim would become "the same model up to rounding", with a threshold to pick.
- **Keep independent timing,** and rely on G3 to catch latency. Round 2's builders would again rank attempts by a number that hid a 22% slowdown.
=== GLOSSARY:30,50 ===

## Bottlenecks and fixes

**Bandwidth-bound**:
A decode step whose achieved bandwidth is close to peak bandwidth.

**Compute-bound**:
A decode step whose operation rate is close to peak compute.

**Overhead-bound**:
A decode step far below both limits, because its time goes to work other than reading weights or doing arithmetic, such as launching GPU jobs, routing tokens to experts or scheduling.
_Avoid_: latency-bound, CPU-bound (unless the CPU specifically is the cause)

**Bottleneck**:
The single cause, identified from measurements, that most limits throughput for a given workload.
_Avoid_: issue, slowness

**Kernel**:
One program the GPU runs as a unit, such as one matrix product or one element-wise add; a decode step is a chain of hundreds of them, each with a fixed start-up cost.
_Avoid_: GPU job, op (for a kernel launch)

## Why the prediction missed (predicted 15 / 15 / 18, off by 142 / 133 / 172%)

1. Wrong fixed-cost model. I charged 2 x 6.81 µs = 13.6 µs from
===S3.1===
#### 3.1 The router product `x.astype(f32) @ w_router.T` — DOES NOT MATCH (main cause)

The kernel accumulates each expert's dot product **serially, in one thread,
in increasing `d` order**: `acc += xsh[d] * w_router[wbase + d]` for
`d = 0..767` (`block-0.metal:31-34`; the Metal compiler may contract each
mul+add to an FMA, but the grouping stays a 768-long left-to-right chain).

The reference never does that. `Matmul::eval_gpu` (MLX v0.32.4,
`mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp`, fetched 2026-11-04) sees A = `x` [rows,768]
f32 (not transposed), B = `w_router.T` [768,60] (transposed view), so
`transpose_a=false, transpose_b=true`, M=rows, N=60, K=768:

- **rows = 1 → GEMV.** `min(M,N)==1` routes to `gemv`
  (matmul.cpp, `Matmul::eval_gpu`); the `gemv_wide` shortcut is skipped
  because the output is float32 (`gemv_wide_config` requires float16/bfloat16

30|   groups 0–7) is 768 (gate) + 768 (up) + 768 (down, two
31|   blocks) = 2,304 dependent iterations, plus silu. Gate

40|   3)`, `:217`) and all 32 lanes of a block share `S`,
41|   `B` and `xv[k]`. Issued per pair: W 884,736 words =
42|   3.54 MB vs 442,368 unique B (8×); S+B 884,736×2×2 B =
43|   3.54 MB vs 110,592 unique B (32×). All scalar,

13|## What happens
14|
15|At 1 row the slot kernel (`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7/block-0.metal`,
16|`!prefill` path) launches 4 threadgroups of 512 threads —
17|one per pair — each running a barrier-serialized chain:
18|`tg_x` load + barrier (`:29-32`); gate/up interleaved, 24
19|strided steps (`K=768`) over 12 of 16 simdgroups
20|(`:51-58`); barrier (`:73`); full-bfloat16 silu-mul, 384
21|of 512 threads (`:77-85`); barrier (`:86`); down
22|interleaved, 12 merged steps (`K=384`) over 12 of 16
23|simdgroups (`:95-102`). That is 36 heavy K steps per
24|thread — each ~2×(2 scale/bias + 4 weight words) plus 64
25|dependent accumulates — with 4 of 16 simdgroups idle in
26|every phase, 4 `simd_sum` trees per thread, and an
27|exp/divide silu between two of the three barriers.
28|
29|Why the gap survives everything round 2 tried (six fused
30|exact packings plateaued at 92–110 µs/layer chained:
31|104.3 / 103.6 / 109.5 / 94.0 / 92.1 / 93.8 — attempts
32|1–5, 7 own runs, per the builder notes on round-2
33|`ineff-baseline-experts-2.md:120-251`, frozen):
34|
35|1. **The chain is at the register ceiling.** Widening
36|   threads/pair bought ~29 µs (132.9 → 104.3) and the
37|   gate/up interleave ~10 µs (104.3 → 94.0, cross-run),
38|   but attempt-6 proved a third 32-float accumulator
39|   fails G1 at 512 threads (pipeline max 448); exactly
40|   two fit (`attempt-7/notes.md:10-15, 227-240`). The
41|   per-thread chain cannot be widened further in this
42|   packing.
43|2. **Merging spent the available parallelism.** The down
44|   interleave is latency-neutral at 1 row (93.8 vs 92.1
45|   cross-run, +1.8%): down's blocks already overlapped
46|   across the 16-simdgroup wave, so merging trades
47|   cross-simdgroup parallelism for in-step parallelism
48|   while each step doubles its loads
49|   (`attempt-7/notes.md:237-255`). Group count past 4
50|   is not the lever either — 4, 48+96 and 12+24 groups
51|   all plateaued at 103.6–109.5 before the interleave
52|   (attempt-3 builder note). What remains is chain
53|   depth: 24 merged gate/up steps + 12 merged down
54|   steps that no packing shortens.
55|3. **The structural remainder is fixed.** `tg_x` load,
56|   silu (serial exp + divide per element), three
57|   barriers, and the chained launch/link cost sit
58|   outside every K-loop change; attempt-1 priced that
59|   block at ~20 µs of the 1-row layer time
60|   (`attempt-1/notes.md:46`, cross-harness model,
61|   indicative). Parallel stores saved only ~2 µs at 1
62|   row (94.0 → 92.1): stores were never the 1-row
63|   bottleneck.

66|per layer at 1 row (3×(Arange+GatherQMM) + silu-mul,

69|groups, round-2 territory §F) and no cross-phase
70|barriers inside any kernel — each kernel short, each

# MobileMoE Bandwidth Study

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*

How efficiently an inference engine turns an Apple Silicon GPU's memory bandwidth and compute into generated tokens when serving a small mixture-of-experts model.

## Hardware limits

**Peak bandwidth**:
The most bytes per second the GPU can read from unified memory, as rated by the manufacturer (about 200 GB/s on this project's M1 Pro).
_Avoid_: max bandwidth, memory speed

**Peak compute**:
The most floating-point operations per second the GPU can perform (about 5.2 TFLOPS on the 16-core M1 Pro GPU).
_Avoid_: max compute, TFLOPS (as the name of the limit)

def chained(fn, layers, names):
    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.

    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
    """
    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
    outs = []
    for layer in layers:
        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
        if outs:
            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
        out = fn(**args)
        if isinstance(out, dict):
            out = list(out.values())
        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
    return outs


def timed(fn, layers, names):
    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
    for _ in range(3):
        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
    times = []
    for _ in range(REPEATS):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

1|# Inefficiency: baseline-combine-1 — volatile rounding barriers cost ~1.4 ms/step in the step, ~0 in the grader
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-combine
4|- **Status:** open
5|- **Version:** 1
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T17:44:55Z
7|- **Next:** verifier to check; builders: exactness without volatiles (e.g. noinline barriers)
8|
9|## Slot
10|
11|`combine`.
12|
13|## What happens
14|
15|The code in the slot
16|(`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1/block-0.metal:33-39`)
17|enforces the reference's per-op rounding with seven `volatile float`
18|thread variables (`p0..p3`, `s01`, `s012`, `acc`). By `volatile`
19|semantics each is a real memory access — 7 stores + 7 loads per output
20|element, 14 accesses × 4 B = 56 B of thread-private stack traffic per
21|thread — that the compiler cannot keep in registers, forward, elide, or
22|reorder. Everything else about the kernel is identical to round-1
23|attempt-1: the spec is byte-identical (empty `diff`), the index/base
24|lines and the final `bfloat(acc) + shared` line are verbatim; only the
25|sum's middle lines changed (one contracted expression → seven volatile
26|steps; `territory-baseline-combine.md` checklists A–B).
27|
28|In the grader this kernel wins at all six sizes (decode 45.7 / 47.9 /
29|64.6 vs compiled 53.4 / 56.4 / 69.1 µs/layer). In the step it loses
30|+1.051 ms at 32 requests where its volatiles-free twin saved −0.390 ms
31|(`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §3 vs `claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`
32|§3). The twin swing — the only code delta is the barriers — is the
33|barriers' in-step cost (table under Cost). The prefill twin in
34|`ineff-g3-1` (+1501.7 ms on the 32×128 all-three prompt where the
35|prefill piece implies a saving) is the same barriers at prefill thread
36|counts (up to 88 MB/layer of spill bytes at 2,048 rows).
37|
38|Ruled out as the main cause (detail in the territory entry): the G3
39|install path (lazy for candidate and compiled alike, checklist D — no
40|per-layer eval or sync exists to blame); hidden contiguity copies (exact
41|−80-kernel op balance, and any copy would hit the twin equally,
42|checklist E); grid/occupancy/wave shape (spec identical across the
43|twin, so shape cannot discriminate); tokens and noise (bit-exact at all
44|6 + 25 sizes and end to end; G3 ranges disjoint in both engines).
45|
46|## Cost
47|
48|Per layer, at decode 1 / 8 / 32 rows and prefill 127 / 1,016 / 2,048
49|rows (peak 200 GB/s, `claude/GLOSSARY.md`):
50|
51|- Kernels × fixed cost: 1 kernel/layer either way — the barriers add no
52|  launch; the chained floor (~32–40 µs/layer decode) is shared with the
53|  twin. Not the cost.
54|- Bytes ÷ peak: slot traffic 9,232 B/row plus spill traffic 56
55|  B/thread = rows×43,008 B/layer, i.e. 52,240 B / 418 KB / 1.67 MB at
56|  decode = **0.26 / 2.1 / 8.4 µs**, and 6.6 / 53 / 107 MB at prefill =
57|  **33 / 265 / 533 µs**. Spill bytes alone: 43 KB / 344 KB / 1.375 MB
58|  decode, 5.5 / 43.7 / 88 MB prefill.
59|- Measured (the twin swing, round-2 G3 minus round-1 G3, per decode
60|  step over 20 layers; vLLM medians, plain in brackets):
61|  1 row **+0.142 (+0.433)** ms, 8 rows **+0.508 (+0.641)** ms, 32 rows
62|  **+1.441 (+1.574)** ms — i.e. **+7.1 / +25.4 / +72.1 µs/layer**
63|  (+21.7 / +32.1 / +78.7 plain). Cross-run drift is bounded at ±0.1 ms
64|  by the control both runs timed (round-1 triple within 0.06–0.09 ms;
65|  territory checklist B), so the 8- and 32-row swings are signal; the
66|  1-row swing is within 1-row cross-run noise and claimed as ≈0.
67|  At 32 rows the paid +72.1 µs/layer is ~9× the spill bytes' 8.4 µs
68|  bandwidth time — the cost is stalls on thread-private traffic
69|  (dependent store→load pairs the compiler cannot schedule across,
70|  fetched in cache lines far wider than the 4 B values), not bytes.
71|
72|Why the grader prices it near zero is only partly understood: its
73|20-layer link chain runs the kernel against a quiet cache with nothing
74|but the tiny `link` kernel between layers, while the step buries each
75|call between megabytes of neighbouring traffic; the store→load reuse
76|that the quiet chain absorbs on-chip stalls in the busy step. The exact
77|on-chip accounting (L1 absorption, line amplification on strided
78|frames, register pressure) needs GPU counters and is **unverified** —
79|but the attribution does not depend on it: same spec, same grid, same
80|inputs, only delta the barriers, 1.44 ms swing with a ±0.1 ms control.
81|
82|## Kind
83|
84|Overhead-bound (`claude/GLOSSARY.md`): at decode 32 the kernel pays
85|+72 µs/layer for 1.375 MB of thread-private traffic (6.9 µs at peak)
86|and ~0.03 µs of arithmetic — far below both limits, the time going to
87|stalled memory traffic that reads no weights and does no arithmetic.
88|
89|## Spans
90|
91|`baseline-combine` (the barrier lines), `g3` (`ineff-g3-1` owns the
92|measurement side; this entry owns the mechanism), `grader` (the chained
93|timing cannot see context-dependent stall costs — note in round-3
94|`territory-grader.md`).
95|
96|## Predicted saving
97|
98|Remove the volatiles while keeping the exact per-op rounding — e.g.
99|`__attribute__((noinline))` device-function barriers for the mul and
100|the adds, which the compiler cannot contract across and which pass
101|values in registers with no memory traffic (expressible in the spec
102|surface: helpers in `header_block`, calls in the body; `slots.build`
103|supports both, `slots.py:313-322`). Predicted effect, labelled
104|prediction:
105|
106|- Decode step (vLLM basis): recover the twin swing, i.e. return to
107|  ≈ −0.51 / −0.71 / −0.39 ms/step: **≈0.5 ms/step at 8 requests and
108|  ≈1.4 ms/step at 32 requests**; ≈0 claimed at 1 row (within noise).
109|- Prefill: the same barriers at prefill thread counts drive the
110|  +1501.7 ms prompt twin (`ineff-g3-1`); removing them is predicted to
111|  recover it (order 1 s on 32×128 combine-including prompts) — no
112|  round-1 prefill twin exists to calibrate against, so this is the
113|  looser half of the prediction.
114|- Grader basis: the kernel already beats compiled everywhere; fewer
115|  stalls can only improve the chained time, so `beats_compiled` is
116|  predicted kept with a wider margin — the fix risks exactness (G2),
117|  never speed, and a saving in decode cannot cost prefill here since
118|  both phases run the identical lines.
119|- Net vs the compiled reference if the fix lands: ≈ −0.5 / −0.9 /
120|  −0.2 ms/step at 1 / 8 / 32 requests (twin's engine numbers), plus
121|  the prompt recovery above.
122|
123|Discriminating checks: the ready check must time the fix combine-alone
124|at 32 requests (reproduces-or-refutes in-round); G3-timing round-1
125|attempt-1 in the same run would isolate the barriers in-run but the
126|fix's own G3 supersedes it.

15|Revisit of round 2's confirmed
16|[`ineff-quantized-kernels-2`](../round-2/exploration/ineff-quantized-kernels-2.md)
17|(same mechanism, frozen — not re-derived here): every `gather_qmm_rhs`
18|call recomputes `offsets = gather_mm_offsets(indices, E, M=B, ...)`
19|(`quantized.cpp:1795`; 60 threads in one threadgroup,
20|`matmul.cpp:2247-2265`), and the three products of one layer share
21|the same sorted `idx`, so the same 240 B result is computed 3× per

24|round 2 ranked this at unbanked time-to-first-token; under two-phase
25|judgment it is prompt time a fast prefill branch (or the prompt-time
26|leg of `beats_compiled`) banks directly. No new mechanism; this entry
27|re-states the cost per layer at all six sizes so builders can rank it.
28|
29|## Cost
30|
31|Decode 1/8/32 rows: **0 kernels** — the `qvm` path builds no offsets
32|(round-2 territory §A). Prefill, per 20-layer chunk forward (one
33|chunk at 127/1,016/2,048 rows; chunking in
34|`bench/grader/slots.py:242`): 3 products × 20 layers = **60** offsets
35|launches, of which **40 are bit-identical recomputations** (20
36|distinct results, one per layer) — counts verified in the round-2
37|entry. Bytes negligible (<0.2 µs per call at 200 GB/s peak); the cost
38|is the fixed launch of a 60-thread kernel. Upper bound per launch

40|round-2 entry; no per-launch prefill figure exists, and pipelined
41|reality is smaller): 40 × ≤6.6 µs = **≤0.26 ms per chunk forward**,

43|per layer × ≤6.6 µs).

139|- **Arbitrary weights and other captured-input assumptions.** None beyond the slot contract. `weights[wbase + j]` is used once, positionally against `y[ybase + 768j]`, with no normalisation, clamping, reordering, sign or sum-to-2.5 assumption and no value-based branch (`block-0.metal:29-41`): negative, zero, very large or very small finite weights take the same seven rounded operations as the captured routing weights, so midpoint sums and the `shared ≈ −acc` cancellation case (where the reported ULP gap magnifies) reproduce the reference bit for bit by construction rather than by sampling — including the separate `bfloat(acc)` round the retired round-1 merge would have skipped. The only hard-coded constants are the slot's fixed dimensions (768 columns, 4 experts, 3,072 = 4×768), and `float(y[…])` is the exact bf16→f32 widening the reference's `copy_v` performs.
140|
141|## Decision
142|
143|Best: `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1` (builder-3-a: thread-per-output with volatile-barrier stepwise sum). Why: passes G1, G2 (differ 0 at all six sizes) and its boundary check, and beats the compiled reference at all three row counts — chained 31.8 / 33.6 / 39.5 µs/layer vs compiled 35.4 / 38.2 / 43.4. Attempt-2 also passes all gates (45.2 / 37.6 / 33.8 vs 47.3 / 55.6 / 43.0) and is fastest at 32 rows, but attempt-1 wins at 1 and 8 rows, is simplest (no threadgroup memory, fully independent threads), and its margins are consistent (3.6 / 4.6 / 3.9 µs/layer) where attempt-2's 1-row margin (2.1 µs) sits inside the compiled figure's run-to-run variance (35.4–47.3). No hardening: both builders name no correctness change; further work would shave the chained floor, which ineff-baseline-combine-2 predicts no kernel-body change can do. G3 should show: a faster step at all three concurrencies. Piece basis (compiled − candidate × 20): −0.07 / −0.09 / −0.08 ms/step against the compiled reference; G3 decides against the unchanged model (round-1 combine alone saved 0.51 / 0.71 / 0.39 ms in vLLM with an inexact kernel of the same shape).

1|# Territory: grader — what changed in round 3 (ADR 0011, ADR 0013)
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-grader
4|- **Status:** done
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T17:39:20Z
7|- **Next:** none — checklist complete (6 pieces), 0 inefficiencies posted (grader runs no decode-step kernels); notes for baseline-*/g3 held in entry until their entries land; no notes to answer
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|Rounds 1 and 2's entries ([`muse-spark/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../exploration/territory-grader.md) and [`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md), frozen) mapped the grader through ADR 0010: bit-exact G2 at six sizes, chained piece timing at decode sizes only, median-vs-median `beats_compiled`, and the paired sign-test `--baseline` bar. Round 3 changes the judgment ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)): the piece timing runs at all six sizes with paired per-size verdicts, `beats_compiled` needs one phase faster and neither slower, and a spec may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference via `max_rows`. G3 moves to vLLM-only two-phase judgment (decode step, prompt time, whole-request time), and the lead's ready check ([`bench/grader/check_ready.py`](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py), [ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)) runs that same G3 inside the round. This entry writes only the delta. G1/G2 mechanics, the spec language, `capture`, and `gpu_lock` are cited to rounds 1–2, not re-described.
12|
13|## Checklist
14|
15|### 1. `check_candidate.py` — paired per-size verdicts and the two-phase judgment (check_candidate.py:51-58, 224-264, 345-378)
16|
17|- **Callers:** builders: `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt> <slot> [--out FILE]` ([check_candidate.py:15](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); no `--baseline` this round — no slot has one (round-3 README *Starting point*). Holds the GPU lock for the whole run ([check_candidate.py:294](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). One grader run is one attempt (ADR 0013); builders keep `grade.json` in the attempt folder.
18|- **Callees:** unchanged: `slots.build`/`load_inputs`/`capture_prefill`/`load_model`; `mx.eval` for correctness and timing; `mx.compile(ref)` for the compiled bar only.
19|- **Data:** `ROWS = (1, 8, 32)`, `PHASES = {"decode": "rows ", "prefill": "prefill rows "}` ([check_candidate.py:51-52](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); `REPEATS = 30`, `WINS_NEEDED = 22` computed by the same one-sided sign test at p < 0.01 as round 2 ([check_candidate.py:53-58](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).
20|- **What is new — paired timing at all six sizes:** timing runs only if G2 passes ([check_candidate.py:345](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), over the same six size inputs as correctness (decode `load_inputs` + prefill `capture_prefill`, [check_candidate.py:308-312,349](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per size and part, `paired_times` runs candidate and compiled (plus baseline when given) in rotating order within each of 30 repeats, each repeat a full chained 20-layer eval ([check_candidate.py:224-236](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per-part times are summed per repeat before wins are counted ([check_candidate.py:364-366](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), so for `routing+combine` the verdict is on summed time, as in round 2. The plain `reference` is still timed by unpaired median `timed()` ([check_candidate.py:360](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) — informational only, no verdict against it.
21|- **What is new — `compare`/`judge`:** per size, the candidate is `faster` with ≥22 wins, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same` ([check_candidate.py:239-245](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per phase: `faster` iff every size is, `slower` iff any size is, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` (and `beats_baseline`, same rule) is true iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower` ([check_candidate.py:248-264,377-378](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Consequences: two `faster` + one `same` in a phase is `not slower`, not `faster` — a single noisy size now blocks the bar instead of passing it (round 2's median-only rule passed on noise up to 5%, [ADR 0011:26](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); a `same` everywhere attempt never beats.
22|- **Invariants:** verdict JSON gains per-size `wins_vs_compiled`/`vs_compiled` (and baseline twins) plus `phases_vs_compiled`/`beats_compiled` ([check_candidate.py:368-378](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:207). On G2 failure there is still no timing at all.
23|
24|### 2. `slots.py` `build` — the `max_rows` hand-off (slots.py:304-337)
25|
26|- **Callers:** `check_candidate.load` and `time_candidates.Variants`/`implementations`, via `slots.build(spec, sources, slot)` — so the hand-off applies identically in the piece timing, G2, G3 and the ready check.
27|- **What it does:** with `"max_rows"` in the spec (per part for `routing+combine`, brief:174), `run()` sends inputs with `rows > max_rows` to the slot's reference under `mx.compile` instead of the kernels ([slots.py:333-337](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). `rows` is read from the first slot input's `shape[0]` ([slots.py:334](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Validation: int ≥ 1, bools rejected ([slots.py:327-331](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); `compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])` is built once per `build` call.
28|- **Grading:** "bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes" (brief:173). G2 checks `run()`, so sizes above `max_rows` exercise the compiled reference through the attempt's own dispatch; the compiled reference of each slot was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes on 2026-11-04 (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`, [ADR 0011:34](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). Timing above `max_rows` runs the bar's own code, so it reads `same` by construction, never better ([ADR 0011:35](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)) — the claim for such an attempt is "faster decode, unchanged prefill" ([ADR 0011:48](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)).
29|- **The experts switch at 60 rows:** from 60 rows MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`) with different rounding ([slots.py:219-220](../../../bench/grader/slots.py); brief:187). Kernels running at rows ≥ 60 must match the large kernel's rounding; `max_rows` ≤ 59 keeps decode-built kernels on the `gather_qvm` side only. The boundary agent checks the hand-off sits on the right side of 60 for experts ([ADR 0011:47](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). Round 2's checked hand-off copy used `max_rows` 59 (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).
30|- **What the grader cannot see here:** any `max_rows` in 32..126 behaves identically at all six G2 sizes and all six timing sizes (tested sizes on each side are 32 and 127) — the grader cannot tell 59 (right side of 60) from 100 (wrong side). §4's `check_sizes.py` (59/60/61) is what distinguishes them; see *What the grader still cannot see* item 1.
31|
32|### 3. `capture_prefill`'s `tokens` parameter and `check_sizes.py` — G2 between the six sizes (slots.py:214-255; check_sizes.py)
33|
34|- **New to these entries** (`check_sizes.py` arrived with Claude's "Measure round 2" commit `f679d23`, after round-2 exploration; the `tokens` parameter serves it). `capture_prefill(model, requests, with_weights, tokens)` with `tokens=N` records the first N tokens of a one-request prefill — N rows per layer ([slots.py:214-255](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)).
35|- **What it does:** `check_sizes.py <out.json> SLOT=FOLDER...` applies `check_candidate`'s checks and pass rule to every layer's slot inputs at `SIZES = (2,3,5,15,16,17,31,33,40,59,60,61,64,65,100,128,129,200,256,257,500,768,769,1024,1500)` ([check_sizes.py:26-27](../../../bench/grader/check_sizes.py)) — either side of the 16-row sort switch and the 60-row MLX switch, and inside each row-count regime an attempt names ([check_sizes.py:1-13](../../../bench/grader/check_sizes.py)). It loads the attempt's `run()` functions, so `max_rows` dispatch is exercised: sizes above `max_rows` test the hand-off path. GPU job under the lock ([check_sizes.py:38](../../../bench/grader/check_sizes.py)); prints per-size pass/FAIL and writes the report JSON.
36|- **Status:** boundary tooling, not a gate — G1/G2 still test exactly the six sizes. It closes round 2's *can't see* item 1 (branch-on-rows kernels exact at six sizes, wrong between) where the boundary agent runs it, and it is the tool that verifies a hand-off's side of 60.
37|
38|### 4. `time_candidates.py` — two-phase vLLM G3 (time_candidates.py:51-55, 163-201, 204-265)
39|
40|- **Callers:** Claude after the round; inside the round, only `check_ready.py` calls it (in-process, pinned argv). Plain-MLX mode still runs token checks and timing for diagnosis, but the G3 verdict reads vLLM runs only ([time_candidates.py:170](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)).
41|- **Protocol:** `G3_SETTINGS = "1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024"`, `G3_REPEATS = 5`, 256 output tokens ([time_candidates.py:51-55,217](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)); vLLM with 512 MiB KV cache, 1 GiB when a prompt length exceeds 128 ([time_candidates.py:247-257](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)).
42|- **What it times** (`MEASURES`, [time_candidates.py:54](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)): `decode` = `period_median_ms`, the steady decode-step period; `prompt` = `prompt_ms`, first forward pass to the first step with no prompt tokens left — "until every prompt was processed" ([repeat_fixes.py:277-282](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)); `request` = `wall_ms`, the whole run's wall time. Variants: `base`, `compiled-<slot>`, `muse-<slot>`, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` with several slots ([time_candidates.py:111-132](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)) — a combination is measured as one, never summed.
43|- **The pass rule** (`against`/`g3`, [time_candidates.py:163-201](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)): per setting and measure, `faster`/`slower` mean the two 5-repeat ranges don't overlap, else `same`. Per measure: `faster` iff every setting is, `slower` iff any is, else `not slower`. A `muse-*` variant passes against a bar iff decode or prompt is `faster` and none of the three is `slower`; `g3` needs that against both `base` and its `compiled-*` counterpart. A `muse-*` variant without its compiled counterpart is not judged ([time_candidates.py:179-181](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)). Verdict to `g3-vllm.json`.
44|- **Why 5 repeats:** with 3, two identical engines' ranges miss per direction with p = 1/20, and 8 "never slower" checks per phase fail an unchanged phase ~1/3 of the time; with 5 it is 1/252 per check, ~3% over 8 ([ADR 0011:40](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). The motivating case: a hand-off copy at `max_rows` 59 read `slower` on prompt time at 32×1,024 by 0.5% (ranges 16 ms apart) although above 59 rows it *is* the compiled reference. Residual ~3% false-`slower` risk per phase stands.
45|- **Token checks:** `rf.vllm_checks` — greedy tokens (24, temperature 0) at 1 and 32 requests of 128-token prompts, plus one steady decode step's kernel count, per variant ([repeat_fixes.py:175-176](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)).
46|
47|### 5. `check_ready.py` — the in-round ready check (whole file)
48|
49|- **Callers:** the lead only, at most twice per round (ADR 0013, skill v8). `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_ready.py <new out folder> SLOT=FOLDER...`, or `--audit <out folder>` ([check_ready.py:24-25](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
50|- **What it runs:** `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3 protocol fixed in code — four workloads, 5 repeats, 256 tokens, every submitted slot in one call so the combination is measured as `muse-all` ([check_ready.py:48-56,81-86](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). No flag changes the protocol; `check_protocol` stops before any GPU work if `time_candidates.py`'s G3 constants changed ([check_ready.py:63-70](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). The out folder must be new ([check_ready.py:76-78](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Cost: ~10–15 min per slot, ~21 min for two, blocking builders' grader runs (ADR 0013).
51|- **What it audits** (the log, never the verdict file, [check_ready.py:103-150](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)): (1) exactly one `ready-check` marker with the protocol; (2) every timed run is vLLM at a G3 workload with 256 tokens and all three measurements present; (3) the variants are exactly `base`, `compiled-<slot>`/`muse-<slot>` per slot, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` with >1 slot, with repeats 0–4 at each workload; (4) every non-base variant keeps the unchanged model's greedy tokens at 1 and 32 requests — and a `compiled-*` variant that changes tokens is "no bar", invalidating the run ([check_ready.py:131-140](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)); (5) `g3-vllm.json` equals the G3 verdict recomputed from the log ([check_ready.py:142-148](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
52|- **What it writes:** `ready-verdict.json` — per `muse-*` variant its pass (G3 and same tokens), `vs` per bar, `phases` per bar, plus per-variant/workload/measurement median/min/max/n, `same_tokens`, `pass`, `judged`, `problems` ([check_ready.py:152-174](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Exit 0: every `muse-*` passes; 1: a variant fails — the verdict stands; 2: the run stopped or broke the protocol — no verdict, may rerun in a new folder ([check_ready.py:20-22,205-213](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
53|- **`--audit`:** re-checks a finished folder without the GPU; compares `pass`, `judged`, `variants`, `medians`, `same_tokens` against the saved `ready-verdict.json`, writes nothing, exits 2 on disagreement ([check_ready.py:195-203](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Used by the swarm's checker and by Claude after the round. Tested against 13 gaming tricks plus the control (`bench/grader/test_check_ready.py`, ADR 0013); verified live on round 2's submission (`results/runs/2026-11-04-ready-check/`, exit 1: routing fails on prompt time, combine on the decode step, the pair on all three).
54|- **Invariants:** only a passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's post-round G3 stays the authority (ADR 0013).
55|
56|### 6. Verdict shape delta (check_candidate.py:296-302, 336-378)
57|
58|`{slot, g1, g2, beats_compiled, correctness: {"<part> <kind> <rows>": {...}}, timing_us_per_layer: {"rows N"/"prefill rows N": {reference, candidate, compiled, wins_vs_compiled, vs_compiled}}, phases_vs_compiled}` plus, with `--baseline`, `{baseline, beats_baseline, wins_needed, phases_vs_baseline}`. Size labels carry the phase prefix (`rows 32` vs `prefill rows 127`), which is what `judge()` splits on.
59|
60|## What the grader still cannot see
61|
62|Round 2's list stands except item 3 (prefill speed — now timed) and item 5c (median-only `beats_compiled` — now a sign test at every size). What is new or still open:
63|
64|1. **`max_rows` between the tested sizes.** Any value in 32..126 is identical at all six G2/timing sizes; the grader cannot see which side of 60 an experts hand-off sits on. `check_sizes.py` (59/60/61) closes it where the boundary agent runs it — the piece verdict never does.
65|2. **Kernel speed at 33–126 rows is unmeasured by the piece timing** (decode sizes stop at 32, prefill starts at 127). With `max_rows` > 32 the kernels run there in real serving (vLLM chunked prefills), and only G3's prompt time at its four workloads can show it — and only if a chunk lands there. Hypotheses with `max_rows` above 32 carry this as **Unverified**.

## The slots

Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.

The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.

### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights

| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
|---|---|---|---|
| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |

Reference:

```python
scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
```

The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.

### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert

| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
|---|---|---|---|
| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |

Reference:

```python
out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
```

Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.

### `routing+combine`

Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.

- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
- **`max_rows`** (optional, an integer of at least 1): inputs with more rows than this skip your kernels and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. Use it to keep prefill-sized inputs on MLX's own code when your kernels are built for decode sizes; MLX switches its own experts kernel at 60 rows. The hand-off is graded like the rest: bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes.
- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot, `max_rows` included: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.
- **Template values** are one of those dtypes, an integer or a boolean.

## How each attempt is judged

The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.

1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.

   At every size:
   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.

   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.

   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.

   **From round 3, the same G3 runs inside the round too:** the lead's **ready check**, `bench/grader/check_ready.py`, with every candidate in one call. It also requires the same greedy tokens, and audits its own log. Only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's G3 after the round decides. The skill says when the lead runs it ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)).

**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same` or `slower`); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.

**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size is, `slower` when any size is, and `not slower` otherwise.
- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.

It is a guide; the ready check in the round, and Claude's G3 after it, decide.

Gate/up's `q` value is consumed by the store `tg_up[b*32 + lane] = (bfloat)q[lane]` (B0:57) before the barrier at B0:73; the silu loop (B0:77–85) reads only `tg_gate`/`tg_up`/`tg_h` and never touches `q` (its local `bfloat p` at B0:83 shadows the outer array inside the loop body and writes nothing to either accumulator); and `qvm_down_pair` re-zeroes both of its accumulators on entry, `p0[j] = p1[j] = 0.0f` for all `j` (B1:152–155), exactly as `qvm_gate_up_pair` does (B1:85–88), before any accumulate, `simd_sum` (B1:187–194) or store reads `q`. So down's `q` at the `y` store (B0:101) is a function only of `tg_h` and the down weights, never of the up values the same storage held before the barriers. Coverage is complete: both helpers touch only indices `2i`/`2i+1` for `i < 16` and the stores read `[lane]`, all inside the zeroed 0–31 (B1:85–88,152–155,176–185). Idle simdgroups 12–15 in decode never call either pair helper and never store (every store sits inside the `simd < 12` guards, B0:51,95), so their never-initialised `p`/`q` is never read; in the prefill branch `p`/`q` are not used at all (`qmm_accum` keeps a scalar local `acc`, B1:219), so prefill threads' uninitialised accumulators are likewise never read.
