110|- **Don't read `.env`** or any credentials file.
111|- One commit per attempt, after you've run the grader on it, so the history shows every attempt in order.
112|
113|## Your files
114|
115|```
116|muse-spark/
117|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
118|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
119|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
120|    spec.json                                the launch spec
121|    notes.md                                 optional: what you tried and why
122|  summary.md                                 your final attempt per slot
123|```
124|
125|`<slot-folder>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing-combine` or `experts`. Grade an attempt with:
126|
127|```bash
128|.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N> <slot>
129|```
130|
131|where `<slot>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing+combine` or `experts`.
132|
133|**The targets JSON** at the end of `strategy.md`:
134|
135|```json
136|{
137|  "targets": [
138|    {"slot": "routing+combine", "why": "...", "expected_saving_ms": {"rows_1": 0.0, "rows_32": 0.0}, "design": "..."}
139|  ]
140|}
141|```
142|
143|List one or two targets, in the order you work on them.
144|
145|**The launch spec** (`spec.json`):
146|
147|```json
148|{
149|  "kernels": [
150|    {
151|      "name": "fused_routing",
152|      "source_block": 0,
153|      "header_block": null,
154|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
155|      "outputs": [
156|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
157|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
158|      ],
159|      "grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1],
160|      "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
161|      "template": {"T": "bfloat16"},
162|      "init_value": null,
163|      "atomic_outputs": false
164|    }
165|  ],
166|  "slot_outputs": {"inds": "inds", "weights": "weights"}
167|}
168|```
169|
170|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
171|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
172|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
173|- **`max_rows`** (optional, an integer of at least 1): inputs with more rows than this skip your kernels and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. Use it to keep prefill-sized inputs on MLX's own code when your kernels are built for decode sizes; MLX switches its own experts kernel at 60 rows. The hand-off is graded like the rest: bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes.
174|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot, `max_rows` included: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
175|- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
176|- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.
177|- **Template values** are one of those dtypes, an integer or a boolean.
178|- **`grid`** counts threads, not threadgroups, as in `mx.fast.metal_kernel`.
179|
180|## How each attempt is judged
181|
182|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
183|
184|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
185|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
186|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
187|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
188|
189|   At every size:
190|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
191|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
192|
193|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
194|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
195|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
196|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
197|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
198|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
199|
200|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
201|
202|   **From round 3, the same G3 runs inside the round too:** the lead's **ready check**, `bench/grader/check_ready.py`, with every candidate in one call. It also requires the same greedy tokens, and audits its own log. Only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's G3 after the round decides. The skill says when the lead runs it ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)).
203|
204|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
205|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
206|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
207|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same` or `slower`); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
208|
209|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
210|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
211|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
212|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size is, `slower` when any size is, and `not slower` otherwise.
213|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
214|
215|It is a guide; the ready check in the round, and Claude's G3 after it, decide.
216|
217|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and has `beats_compiled` true, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

Read text file `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`.
1|# Territory: quantized-kernels (round 2 — prefill path)
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
4|- **Status:** done
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T03:24:31Z
7|- **Next:** none — prefill checklist filled (§A–§H), 2 inefficiencies posted, note left on `territory-baseline-experts`
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|This territory is MLX's `mx.gather_qmm` Metal kernels behind the `experts`
12|slot (`quantized.h`, `quantized_utils.h`, `utils.h` in the installed
13|0.32.4 headers, dispatch in MLX v0.32.4 `quantized.cpp`). Round 1 mapped
14|it as decode-only: `affine_gather_qvm` runs at every decode size and
15|`affine_gather_qmm_rhs` was listed as never run
16|([`muse-spark/exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md`](../../exploration/territory-quantized-kernels.md)
17|§A/§C, frozen). Round 2 reopens it because the new G2 is bit-exact at
18|prefill sizes too: from 60 rows the reference switches to
19|`gather_qmm_rhs`, whose rounding is now on the correctness path at
20|prefill 127/1,016/2,048 rows. This entry writes only what is new: the
21|prefill dispatch, the `qmm_rhs` arithmetic, and exactly how it diverges
22|from `qvm`. Decode facts that still hold are cited, not rewritten.
23|
24|## The checklist
25|
26|### A. Dispatch — `GatherQMM::eval_gpu` (which kernel runs at each size)
27|
28|- **Callers:** `ref_experts` (`bench/grader/slots.py:55-82`) and the
29|  served twin `SwitchGLU.__call__`
30|  (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:176-199`) both call
31|  `mx.gather_qmm(..., transpose=False, group_size=32, bits=4,
32|  mode="affine", sorted_indices=do_sort)` three times per layer (gate,
33|  up, down), with `do_sort = inds.size >= 64` ⇔ rows ≥ 16
34|  (`slots.py:62`, `switch_layers.py:181`). MLX is 0.32.4
35|  (`.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; print(mx.__version__)"`).
36|  Served weights are `[E, in, out]` via `TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear`
37|  (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:142-184`), hence
38|  `transpose=False`; the `transpose=True` twin in `switch_layers.py:75-90`
39|  is not the served path.
40|- **Callees:** `GatherQMM::eval_gpu`
41|  ([quantized.cpp v0.32.4:1980-2094](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1980-L2094)).
42|  It shapes `K = x.shape(-1)`, `M = x.shape(-2)`,
43|  `N = out.shape(-1)`, `B = out.size()/M/N`,
44|  `E = w.size()/w.shape(-1)/w.shape(-2) = 60`,
45|  `vector_limit = 4` for `transpose=False` (`:2000-2005`). Branch order:
46|  (1) rhs fast path iff `M==1 && B>=16 && right_sorted_ && B/E>=4`
47|  (`:2012-2031`); (2) else `gather_qmm` iff `M >= vector_limit`
48|  (`:2034-2054`); (3) else `gather_qmv` iff `transpose_` (`:2056-2075`);
49|  (4) else `gather_qvm` (`:2077-2094`). With `M=1` always (below),
50|  branch (2) never fires in this model.
51|- **Data / shapes at every grader size.** `x` reaching `gather_qmm` is
52|  `[B, 1, K]` with `B = rows*4`: `xx = expand_dims(x, (-2,-3))` then,
53|  when sorting, `_gather_sort` gathers to one row per pair
54|  (`slots.py:61-65`, `switch_layers.py:12-17`); hence `M = 1` and the
55|  `M` argument later passed to `gather_qmm_rhs` is `x.size()/K = B`
56|  (`:2013-2027`). Gate/up: `K=768, N=384`; down (input is the
57|  bfloat16 `silu*up` hidden): `K=384, N=768`.
58|
59|  | rows | B = rows·4 | B/E | sorted (`inds.size≥64`) | MLX kernel |
60|  |---|---|---|---|---|
61|  | 1 (decode) | 4 | 0.07 | no | `gather_qvm` |
62|  | 8 (decode) | 32 | 0.53 | no | `gather_qvm` |
63|  | 32 (decode) | 128 | 2.13 | yes | `gather_qvm` (sorted, still `B/E<4`) |
64|  | 127 (prefill) | 508 | 8.47 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
65|  | 1,016 (prefill) | 4,064 | 67.73 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
66|  | 2,048 (prefill) | 8,192 | 136.53 | yes | `gather_qmm_rhs` |
67|
68|  The switch is `rows >= 60` (`B >= 240 ⇔ B/E >= 4`; `B>=16` already
69|  holds from 4 rows). Two thresholds must not be conflated: sorting
70|  starts at 16 rows, the kernel switch at 60. The grader tests 32 and
71|  127, only bracketing 60; the exact threshold comes from this source,
72|  not from grader probing (cf. `territory-grader.md` *What the grader
73|  still cannot see* §1).
74|- **Neighbours:** before: router `inds` + `_gather_sort` (switch-layers
75|  territory); the sort is what sets `right_sorted_`. Between gate/up
76|  and down: compiled `swiglu` on bfloat16 values (other-kernels).
77|  After: `_scatter_unsort` back to positional `[rows, 4, 768]`, then
78|  combine. A replacement slot kernel sees only positional `inds`
79|  (any order, duplicates allowed) — the reference's sort is internal
80|  and invisible in `y` except through the bits.
81|- **Cost:** the dispatch itself launches nothing. Kernel counts and
82|  times per branch are in §C/§F. Prefill sizes are correctness-only in
83|  the grader (no timing; `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`),
84|  so every prefill cost below is arithmetic, not a measured time.
85|- **Invariants:** `right_sorted_` is the Python `sorted_indices`
86|  argument trusted as-is; `gather_qmm_rhs` (§C) is only correct if
87|  `rhs_indices` really is sorted ascending by expert. `M` in the rhs
88|  call means total pairs `B`, not the `M=1` matrix height — the rhs
89|  kernel re-derives row tiles from `offsets` (§D).
90|
91|### B. Host wrapper — `gather_qmm_rhs` (legacy path, the one this GPU runs)
92|
93|- **Callers:** only §A branch (1) (and the `GatherQQMM` twin at
94|  `quantized.cpp:2233-2251`, not this model).
95|- **Callees:** [gather_qmm_rhs v0.32.4:1676-1830](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/quantized.cpp#L1676-L1830).
96|  First gate: `is_nax_available() && (enable_tf32 || dtype != float32)`
97|  diverts to `gather_qmm_rhs_nax` (`:1692-1714`). On this machine that
98|  is false: device is Apple M1 Pro `applegpu_g13s`
99|  (`mx.device_info()`), architecture generation 13 < 17, and NAX also
100|  needs macOS 26.2
101|  ([device.cpp v0.32.4:978-995](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/device.cpp#L978-L995)).
102|  So the legacy tiling below is the prefill path here; the NAX variant
103|  (`bm=32/64, bn=bk=64` in the same function, NAX MMA in
104|  `quantized_nax.h`) never runs on the grader GPU. Legacy tiles
105|  (`:1748-1749`): `bm=16, bn=32, bk=32`, `wm=1, wn=2`;
106|  `align_N = (N%32==0)`, `align_K = (K%32==0)` — both true for
107|  384/768, passed as function constants 201/202. Then
108|  `offsets = gather_mm_offsets(indices, E, M=B, ...)` (`:1795`), one
109|  `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` launch with
110|  `group_dims = (32, wn, wm) = 64` threads and
111|  `grid_dims = ((N+31)/32, min(B, ceil(B/16)+E-1), 1)` (`:1817-1819`).
112|- **Data:** `broadcast_with_indices` (`:1721-1733`) copies `x` to
113|  `[B, 1, K]` only if `x.size()/x.shape(-2)/x.shape(-1) != B`; on the
114|  sorted path `x` already has `B` rows (the sort gathered it), so this
115|  is a no-op apart from `ensure_row_contiguous` flag checks, as are
116|  the `w`/`scales`/`biases` normalisations (already contiguous).
117|  `offsets` is `int32[E=60]` (240 B), the per-expert start rows in
118|  sorted order, built by one tiny kernel launch
119|  (`gather_mm_offsets`, host side at
120|  [matmul.cpp v0.32.4:2247-2265](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.4/mlx/backend/metal/matmul.cpp#L2247-L2265):
121|  `dispatch_threads(60)`, one threadgroup). Inputs to the Metal kernel,
122|  in buffer order: `x` bfloat16 `[B, K]`, `w` uint32, `scales`/
123|  `biases` bfloat16, `offsets` int32, out `y` bfloat16 `[B, N]`, then
124|  `M=B, N, K, num_groups=60` as constants (`:1821-1835`).
125|- **Neighbours:** same slot edges as §A. The three products in one
126|  layer share the same sorted `idx`, hence the same `offsets` — yet
127|  each of the three calls recomputes it (see
128|  `ineff-quantized-kernels-2`).
129|- **Cost (arithmetic, per layer):** 3 offsets kernels + 3 main kernels
130|  per prefill layer-call (60 + 60 per 20-layer prefill forward),
131|  against 0 + 3 on the decode `qvm` path. Main-kernel dispatched
132|  threadgroups (64 threads each): gate/up `12 × grid_y`, down
133|  `24 × grid_y` with `grid_y = min(B, ceil(B/16)+59)` = 91 / 313 / 571
134|  at B = 508 / 4,064 / 8,192 → gate/up 1,092 / 3,756 / 6,852 and down
135|  2,184 / 7,512 / 13,704 threadgroups per call. Useful row tiles are
136|  fewer (§C, `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`).
137|- **Invariants:** `grid_y` over-provisions by up to `E-1 = 59` tiles:
138|  `ceil(B/16) + E - 1` is the worst case (every expert contributing a
139|  partial tile). Threadgroups whose tile index exceeds the real tile
140|  count return early inside the kernel (§C) — they are launched,
141|  scheduled, and discarded, never incorrect.
142|
143|### C. Metal kernel — `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` + `schedule_row_tile`
144|
145|- **Callers:** §B only. Instantiated for this model as
146|  `affine_gather_qmm_rhs<bfloat16, group_size=32, bits=4, BM=16,
147|  BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2, transpose=false>`
148|  (`quantized.h:2570-2593`).
149|- **Callees:** `schedule_row_tile<BM=16>` (`utils.h:501-542`) maps
150|  `tid.y` to `(y_row, group, tgp_bm)`: it scans experts in lane-parallel
151|  chunks of 32, prefix-summing `ceil((end-start)/16)` per expert from
152|  `offsets`, and returns the expert owning tile `tid.y`, its first
153|  row, and `tgp_bm = min(16, end - row)` valid rows (`utils.h:524-537`).
154|  If no expert owns the tile it returns false and the whole
155|  threadgroup exits (`quantized.h:2637-2640`). Then
156|  `QuantizedBlockLoader` (§D) fills threadgroup `Ws`, `BlockLoader`
157|  fills `Xs` (§E), and `gemm_loop_aligned` /
158|  `gemm_loop_unaligned<...>` (`quantized_utils.h:6-90`) drive
159|  `BlockMMA::mma` over `K_it = K/BK` tiles (24 gate/up, 12 down),
160|  with an extra `gemm_loop_finalize` only when `!align_K` — never
161|  here, since `K % 32 == 0` (`quantized.h:2631, 2676-2717`).
162|- **Data:** threadgroup memory `Xs[16 × 40]` + `Ws[32 × 40]` bfloat16
163|  = 1,280 B + 2,560 B = 3,840 B (`BK_padded = BN_padded = 32 + 16/2 =
164|  40`, `quantized.h:2596-2597, 2623-2624`; padding is the usual
165|  16-byte bank-conflict pad). Weight addressing for
166|  `transpose=false`: `wl += group * stride_w` with
167|  `stride_w = K * N_w`, `N_w = N/2` bytes-worth per row — i.e. the
168|  `[E, K, N]`-quantized expert block selected by `group`
169|  (`:2627-2633, 2655-2674`). `x` rows are the sorted pair rows
170|  `y_row .. y_row+tgp_bm-1` of the already-gathered `[B, K]` matrix;
171|  `y` writes go to those same sorted rows, unsorted later by the
172|  caller. Per-output values never mix rows: padded rows (§E) occupy
173|  separate accumulator rows and are discarded by
174|  `store_result_safe` (`:2694`).
175|- **Neighbours:** consumes the sorter's output order directly; this
176|  is the only gather kernel whose addressing depends on pair order
177|  (all others index per pair via `adjust_matrix_offsets`,
178|  `quantized.h:1636-1688`). Its output rows are in sorted-pair order,
179|  so `_scatter_unsort` after the down product is load-bearing for
180|  position, not for bits.
181|- **Cost (arithmetic):** balanced-expert model (counts near the
182|  uniform mean `B/60`; grader prompts are random tokens, so this is
183|  the expected case, not a bound): useful row tiles
184|  `T = Σ_e ceil(cnt_e/16)` ≈ 60 / 300 / 540 at B = 508 / 4,064 /
185|  8,192, against dispatched `grid_y` 91 / 313 / 571 (§B). Weight
186|  bytes read per product per layer = `T × 184,320 B` (per-expert
187|  147,456 B weights + 36,864 B scales/biases; §F) = 11.06 / 55.30 /
188|  99.53 MB, i.e. 1× / 5× / 9× the 11.06 MB distinct-expert floor —
189|  each extra row tile of an expert re-reads and re-dequantizes its
190|  full weights. The per-pair `qvm` path at the same `B` would read
191|  `B × 184,320 B` = 93.6 MB / 749 MB / 1.51 GB per product, so `rhs`
192|  is 8.5× / 13.5× / 15.2× leaner on weight traffic — grouping works;
193|  its waste is the tile quantization in `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`,
194|  not the grouping idea.
195|- **Invariants:** correctness rests on sorted `rhs_indices` +
196|  exact `offsets`; an unsorted input silently computes tiles from
197|  mixed experts (dispatch trusts `right_sorted_`, §A). `BM=16`
198|  grouping changes only which rows share a weight-tile load — never
199|  a valid row's arithmetic (§E) — so a bit-exact replacement may
200|  regroup rows freely, including not grouping at all, as long as
201|  each row's own accumulation matches §D+§E.
202|
203|### D. Dequantization — `QuantizedBlockLoader` + `dequantize` (rounding point 1)
204|
205|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` with
206|  `QuantizedBlockLoader<T=bfloat16, BROWS=BK=32, BCOLS=BN=32,
207|  dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=0, tgp_size=64, group_size=32, bits=4>`
208|  (`quantized.h:2613-2621`); same loader family as `qmm_n`/`qmm_t`
209|  (§G).
210|- **Callees:** `load_unsafe`/`load_safe` (`quantized.h:736-770`) call
211|  `dequantize<T, pack_factor=2, bits=4>` (`quantized.h:557-663`,
212|  bits=4 at `:617-623`) per packed byte: with `s = float(scale)`,
213|  `b = float(bias)` it writes
214|  `w_local[2i] = (bfloat16)(s * (w[i] & 0x0f) + b)` and
215|  `w_local[2i+1] = (bfloat16)((s/16) * (w[i] & 0xf0) + b)` into
216|  threadgroup `Ws`. Scales: one `scale`/`bias` pair per thread from
217|  `scales + bi * N/32` (`:733-734`); `group_steps = 32/32 = 1`, so
218|  `next()` advances `scales/biases` by `32*N/32 = N` per K tile
219|  (`:772-790`) — exactly one scale group per `BN=32` output tile and
220|  per `BK=32` row of `K`, matching the `[E, K, N/32]` layout.
221|- **Data:** packed uint32 weights are viewed as bytes (`(device
222|  uint8_t*)w`); each byte yields 2 outputs (low/high nibble), each
223|  `BK×BN = 1,024`-element weight tile dequantized once per
224|  (row tile, K tile) visit into `Ws`, then read by the MMA (§E).
225|  `x` tiles by contrast are copied verbatim (bfloat16 → bfloat16,
226|  exact) by `BlockLoader` (`steel/gemm/loader.h:74-80`).
227|- **Neighbours:** this is the first of the two divergence points
228|  vs `qvm` (§F): the dequantized weight is **rounded to bfloat16
229|  before any multiply**. In `qvm` the same `scale*q + bias` value
230|  stays in float32 registers through the product.
231|- **Cost:** dequant element-ops per product per layer =
232|  `T × K × N` = `T × 294,912` (both products have `K·N = 294,912`):
233|  17.7M / 88.5M / 159.2M at the three prefill sizes (balanced `T`
234|  from §C), each a float mul+add, a float→bfloat round, and a
235|  threadgroup store+reload. This recompute-per-row-tile is the
236|  loader's design (no dequantized-weight cache exists; the full
237|  dequantized expert is 294,912 × 2 B = 590 KB, far above the
238|  32 KB threadgroup limit, so cross-tile reuse would need a device
239|  buffer and an extra kernel — not a free fix).
240|- **Invariants:** `scale`/`bias` themselves are bfloat16 values
241|  upcast to float exactly (bfloat→float is exact), identical to
242|  `qvm`'s inputs; the *only* added rounding is
243|  `static_cast<bfloat16>(s*q + b)`. Relative error up to half a
244|  bfloat ULP (≈2⁻⁹ ≈ 0.2%) per weight element, deterministic per
245|  `(expert, k, n)` — the same rounded weight is reused for all
246|  ≤16 rows of the tile, so errors are correlated across rows
247|  sharing an expert, unlike per-pair float weights.
248|
249|### E. Accumulation — `BlockLoader` + `BlockMMA` (rounding point 2)
250|
251|- **Callers:** `affine_gather_qmm_rhs` instantiates
252|  `BlockMMA<bfloat16, bfloat16, BM=16, BN=32, BK=32, WM=1, WN=2,
253|  false, transpose=false, ...>` (`quantized.h:2599-2610`) and
254|  `BlockLoader<bfloat16, BM=16, BK=32, dst_ld=40, reduction_dim=1,
255|  tgp_size=64>` for `x` (`:2611-2612`).
256|- **Callees:** `BlockMMA` (`steel/gemm/mma.h:439-537`) with
257|  `AccumType = float` by default (`mma.h:451`): accumulator
258|  fragments `Ctile` are `float` 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` tiles
259|  (`TM = 16/(8·1) = 2`, `TN = 32/(8·2) = 2` frags per simdgroup).
260|  `mma()` (`mma.h:513-537`) steps `kk` over `BK` in 8-wide frags
261|  (4 steps per tile), each `tile_matmad` issuing
262|  `simdgroup_multiply_accumulate` (`mma.h:181-206, 406-427`).
263|  Operand fragments are loaded from threadgroup bfloat16 and
264|  widened to float (`BaseMMAFrag::load` casts, `mma.h:57-67`), so
265|  the multiply is float×float with float accumulate — but the
266|  weight operand is the already-bfloat-rounded value of §D, and
267|  the 8-term dot inside each frag is the hardware's tree order,
268|  not a serial FMA chain. `gemm_loop_*` then adds tile results
269|  sequentially over the 24/12 K tiles. Store:
270|  `store_result`/`store_result_safe` cast float → bfloat16 once
271|  (`mma.h:100-112, 540-592`; `quantized.h:2683, 2694`) — the same
272|  single final rounding as `qvm`.
273|- **Data:** `Xs` holds `16×32` bfloat16 activations per K tile
274|  (rows zero-padded by `load_safe` when `tgp_bm < 16`,
275|  `loader.h:83-128`); `Ws` holds the §D dequantized tile. Partial-row
276|  tiles take the `gemm_loop_unaligned<false, true, ...>` branch
277|  (`quantized.h:2687-2695`) — full MMA work on padded rows, results
278|  discarded.
279|- **Neighbours:** identical bfloat16 store boundary as `qvm`, so
280|  the downstream `swiglu` (gate/up) and down product see the same
281|  *kind* of rounding point — only the float value arriving at the
282|  cast differs.
283|- **Cost:** per product, MMA flops are `2·B_padded·K·N` with
284|  `B_padded = T·16` = 960 / 4,800 / 8,640 vs useful `B` = 508 /
285|  4,064 / 8,192 (padded fractions in `ineff-quantized-kernels-1`).
286|  At 5.2 TFLOPS peak (`claude/GLOSSARY.md:14`) the useful MMA
287|  floors at `2·B·K·N/5.2 TFLOPS` = 57.6 / 461.0 / 929.2 µs per
288|  layer-product (B = 508 / 4,064 / 8,192) if it ran at peak — it
289|  cannot, at `BM=16` tiles with two barriers per 32-K step
290|  (`quantized_utils.h:14-29`), so the path is
291|  overhead/latency-bound, not compute-bound; no measured prefill
292|  time exists to check this against (§A).
293|- **Invariants:** per-output accumulation grouping is
294|  **[contiguous 8-wide frag dots] sequentially over BK=32 tiles**,
295|  in increasing K. This is the second divergence from `qvm` (§F):
296|  even with bit-identical weight operands, regrouping a 768-term
297|  float sum this way rounds differently on generic data. Reproducing
298|  it with scalar FMAs is not bit-safe; reproducing it requires the
299|  same 8×8 `simdgroup_matrix` fragmentation (same `BK`, same
300|  frag step order) or a proof the hardware order coincides — none
301|  exists in the sources. Warp tiling `WM/WN` only partitions frags
302|  across simdgroups; it does not change a single output's add order.
303|
304|### F. Comparator — `qvm_impl` + `qouter` (what decode runs; delta only)
305|
306|Round 1 §A mapped this kernel fully; only the contrast is new.
307|
308|- **Callers/Callees:** `gather_qvm` host (`quantized.cpp:1462-1529`)
309|  → `affine_gather_qvm` (`quantized.h:2355-2416`) → `qvm_impl`
310|  (`quantized.h:1222-1330`): grid `(1, (N+63)/64, B)` threadgroups of
311|  64 threads; gate/up `(1, 6, B)`, down `(1, 12, B)`. Each lane owns
312|  one strided `K` element per 32-step (`x += block_size` with
313|  `block_size = 32`, `:1275-1287`) and accumulates 32 outputs in
314|  float registers via `qouter` (`quantized.h:452-553`, bits=4 at
315|  `:503-509`): `result += x * (scale*q + bias)` with
316|  `scale`/`bias`/`x` all float, **no bfloat16 rounding of the
317|  weight**, serial per-lane adds in strided-K order
318|  (`k = lane, lane+32, ...`), then one `simd_sum` tree over the 32
319|  lane partials (`:1317-1321`) and a single float→bfloat16 store
320|  (`:1324-1329`).
321|- **The two divergences, side by side:**
322|
323|  | aspect | `gather_qvm` (decode, rows < 60) | `gather_qmm_rhs` (prefill, rows ≥ 60) |
324|  |---|---|---|
325|  | weight value | `float(scale)·q + float(bias)` kept in float32 | same value rounded to bfloat16 in threadgroup (§D) |
326|  | K grouping | strided lanes: lane `l` sums `k≡l (mod 32)` serially, then `simd_sum` tree | contiguous: 8-wide frag dots, sequential over BK=32 tiles (§E) |
327|  | rows sharing work | none: one grid slice per pair | ≤16 sorted rows share each weight tile |
328|  | final rounding | float → bfloat16 once after `simd_sum` | float → bfloat16 once after MMA — identical point |
329|
330|  Either divergence alone breaks bit-equality (measured: 62.4–62.6%
331|  of experts outputs differ at all three prefill sizes, max
332|  43/65/110.5 ULP, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-experts.json`;
333|  full statement in `ineff-baseline-experts-1`). A single arithmetic

335|  `float(scale·q+bias)` not representable in bfloat16 and any
336|  `x ≠ 0` — the two references already disagree on that product
337|  before accumulation even starts. **Conclusion for builders: a
338|  size branch is required** — `qvm` arithmetic below 60 rows,
339|  `qmm_rhs` arithmetic (bfloat-rounded dequant tiles + 8-wide frag
340|  accumulation) at/above 60 rows — or a proof of coincidence that
341|  the 62% differ rate rules out empirically. The branch threshold
342|  must be the dispatch rule `rows >= 60` (pairs `>= 240`, `E=60`),

344|  real model still run `qvm` (§A). Row *grouping* inside the
345|  prefill branch is free (§C invariant); per-row accumulation is
346|  not.
347|- **Cost:** decode cost is round 1's confirmed entry

349|  round-2 restatement `ineff-baseline-experts-3`): 51 MB read in

351|  (62 GB/s, 31% of peak). Not re-posted here.
352|- **Invariants:** both paths accumulate in float32 and round to
353|  bfloat16 exactly once per product; `silu(gate)·up` is computed on
354|  those bfloat16 values and rounded again before down (brief:
355|  `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`). Any candidate must keep all

359|  `muse-spark/implementation/hyp-1-fused-experts.md:103-108`).

1|# attempt-7 (round 2): hardening — interleaved down, shared second accumulator (builder-1-g)
2|
3|Hardening attempt for `hyp-1-experts-exact` (slot `experts`, baseline
4|`none`). Builds on the best attempt
5|`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-5` (fused single kernel,
6|512 threads/pair, interleaved gate/up + parallel block stores, G2 pass
7|all six, 92.1 / 162.0 / 534.8 µs/layer chained vs compiled
8|75.9 / 234.6 / 798.2 — loses only at 1 row by 16.2 µs) with the
9|down-interleave `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-6` tried
10|(one simdgroup, two down blocks, merged K loop), made to compile
11|within the pipeline threadgroup limit. Attempt-6 failed G1:
12|`Thread group size (512) is greater than the maximum allowed
13|threads per threadgroup (448)` — its compiled pipeline's
14|`maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` fell to 448 for the identical
15|512-thread launch.
16|
17|## The one main change
18|
19|Attempt-6's merged down loop, with the second accumulator's storage
20|shared so the kernel compiles at 512 threads. Everything else is
21|copied from attempt-5/6, not redesigned (`spec.json` byte-identical
22|to attempt-5/6; `block-1.metal` helpers `qvm_block`,
23|`qvm_gate_up_pair`, `qvm_down_pair`, `qmm_accum` bodies byte-identical
24|to attempt-6 by diff; `block-0.metal` gate/up, silu and prefill
25|branches otherwise byte-identical):
26|
27|- **Before (attempt-5):** down ran 24 blocks of 32 outputs in 2
28|  sequential waves of 16 simdgroups (`b = v*16 + simd`, `b < 24`):
29|  wave 0 computed blocks 0–15, wave 1 blocks 16–23 (simdgroups
30|  8–15 idle), each block a separate `qvm_block` call — 12 strided
31|  K steps per lane (`k = lane, lane+32, …, lane+352` over `K=384`),
32|  then `simd_sum` and the parallel store
33|  `y[pair*768 + b*32 + lane] = (bfloat)p[lane]`. The second wave's
34|  first load waited for the first wave's last accumulate.
35|- **Attempt-6's down change (kept):** one simdgroup computes two
36|  down blocks in one merged K loop (`qvm_down_pair`, block-1).
37|  Simdgroup `s < 12` owns the consecutive pair `b0 = 2s`,
38|  `b1 = 2s+1` (12 pairs, one wave; simdgroups 12–15 idle, as in
39|  gate/up). For each strided `k` both blocks' loads are issued
40|  before either accumulates — block 0's scale/bias and 4 weight
41|  words, then block 1's scale/bias and 4 weight words (plus the
42|  shared `tg_h[k]`, read once) — and only then do the two
43|  accumulation passes run, block 0's 32 terms then block 1's, into
44|  separate accumulators. The 24 down blocks therefore run as 12
45|  interleaved pairs instead of 2 sequential waves.
46|- **This attempt's fix vs attempt-6:** attempt-6 declared three
47|  distinct 32-float thread arrays — kernel-scope `p[32]`, a
48|  gate/up-scoped `pu[32]` and a down-scoped `q[32]` — and the
49|  compiler charged all three against the per-threadgroup budget
50|  (`maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` 448 < 512) even though `pu` and
51|  `q` are live in disjoint phases. Attempt-7 hoists the second
52|  accumulator to kernel scope: `float p[32]; float q[32];` beside
53|  the existing buffers in `block-0`, and passes the same `q` as
54|  gate/up's second accumulator (`qvm_gate_up_pair(..., p, q)`) and
55|  as down's second accumulator (`qvm_down_pair(..., p, q)`),
56|  deleting both scoped declarations. The kernel again has two
57|  distinct 32-float thread arrays, exactly attempt-5's footprint,
58|  at unchanged 512 threads.
59|
60|Everything else is kept identical, as the task requires:
61|
62|- **Per-block bits unchanged.** In `qvm_down_pair` each block's adds
63|  run in exactly `qvm_block`'s order: the same strided `k` sequence,
64|  the same float32 dequant terms
65|  `x * (s0 * (by & 0x0f) + bias)` / `x * (s1 * (by & 0xf0) + bias)`
66|  with `s1 = scale/16`, in the same per-output sequence; the two
67|  accumulators are independent, so interleaving cannot reorder
68|  either block's own adds. Each accumulator then gets the identical
69|  `#pragma clang loop unroll(full)` `simd_sum` tree as `qvm_block`.
70|  The `(bfloat)` rounding at the store is unchanged.
71|- **Sharing is a pure storage rename.** Gate/up and down run in
72|  disjoint phases separated by two `threadgroup_barrier`s (after
73|  gate/up and after silu): gate/up's `q` values are stored to
74|  `tg_up` before the first barrier, silu consumes only
75|  `tg_gate`/`tg_up`/`tg_h`, and `qvm_down_pair` re-zeroes both
76|  `p[0..31]` and `q[0..31]` on entry (as `qvm_gate_up_pair` does),
77|  so no value can leak across the barrier through the shared array.
78|  Peak live floats per phase is unchanged (64 in gate/up, 64 in
79|  down); only the distinct-array count charged by the compiler
80|  drops from three to two.
81|- **Parallel lane stores kept.** After the two `simd_sum`s every
82|  lane holds both blocks' full reduced 32-vectors, so lane `j`
83|  stores element `j` of each block — one store per lane per block:
84|  `y[pair*768 + b0*32 + lane] = (bfloat)p[lane]`,
85|  `y[pair*768 + b1*32 + lane] = (bfloat)q[lane]`.
86|- **Gate/up interleave, silu, prefill scalar branch, grids and
87|  rounding points identical.** Gate/up still calls
88|  `qvm_gate_up_pair` with attempt-5's parallel `tg_gate`/`tg_up`
89|  stores; the full-bfloat16 silu-mul is byte-identical; the
90|  `rows >= 60` prefill branch still uses the scalar `qmm_accum`
91|  (bfloat16-rounded dequant, contiguous `BK=32` order) for gate,
92|  up and down, with the same `x_shape[0] >= 60` dispatch
93|  threshold; `spec.json` (one kernel, `rows*2048` threads =
94|  `rows*4` groups of 512) is byte-identical. No kernel split, no
95|  new device-memory intermediate, same four bfloat16 rounding
96|  points and positional `y[r,j]`.
97|
98|## Which inefficiency it removes, and how
99|
100|- `ineff-baseline-experts-2` (chained 1-row latency): attempt-5's
101|  miss analysis left the still-sequential down chain as the
102|  largest named remainder at 1 row — 12 strided steps × 2 waves
103|  behind the silu barrier, plus the `tg_x` load, silu, barriers
104|  and chained fixed cost. Attempts 1–3 showed threadgroup count
105|  past 4 is not the lever and attempt-4/5 showed overlapping the
106|  per-block serial K chain is. The down product was the last
107|  product still running its blocks in fully sequential waves with
108|  only one block's loads in flight per simdgroup; merging two
109|  blocks per simdgroup puts both blocks' loads (8 weight words +
110|  2 scales/biases per step) in flight in every step, so each
111|  block's load latency has the other block's loads/compute to
112|  hide behind, without touching any block's `simd_sum` order.
113|  The shared-`q` fix is what lets this merged loop launch at all:
114|  attempt-6 proved the three-array form exceeds the pipeline
115|  threadgroup budget at 512 threads.
116|- `ineff-baseline-experts-1` (prefill G2 gate): already removed by
117|  attempt-5's branch; kept by reusing its scalar `qmm_accum`
118|  verbatim — the interleave does not touch prefill arithmetic.
119|- `ineff-baseline-experts-3` (per-pair re-reads): deliberately
120|  kept, as in attempts 1–6 — weight bytes per pair stay 552,960 B;
121|  the interleave changes load scheduling, not bytes.
122|

125|512 threads/group ≤ 1,024 (`spec.json` identical to attempt-5/6).
126|Threadgroup memory unchanged: `tg_x[768] + tg_gate[384] +
127|tg_up[384] + tg_h[384]` bfloat16 = **3,840 B** of 32,768 B,
128|rows-independent. Distinct thread arrays are two 32-float
129|accumulators (`p`, shared `q`) — attempt-5's count, one fewer than
130|attempt-6's three. Grid scales as `rows*4` groups, so the kernel
131|is valid at every `rows ≥ 1`, on both sides of 60. Decode coverage:
132|12 simdgroups × 2 blocks × 32 lanes = 768 outputs per pair, each
133|written exactly once, as before.
134|
135|## Predicted µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (chained, grader timing)
136|
137|Attempt-5 (other run): 92.1 / 162.0 / 534.8 µs/layer vs compiled
138|75.9 / 234.6 / 798.2 and reference 95.7 / 232.4 / 802.3. Attempt-6
139|predicted 85 / 156 / 540 but never launched, so that prediction is
140|untested, not missed. Baseline `none`, so no
141|`wins_vs_baseline` / `beats_baseline`. Weight bytes per layer
142|(552,960 B/pair): 2.21 / 17.69 / 70.78 MB at 4 / 32 / 128 pairs;
143|bandwidth floors at 200 GB/s: 11.1 / 88.5 / 353.9 µs.
144|Attempt-5 effective: 24.0 / 109.2 / 132.3 GB/s.
145|
146|Down arithmetic: `K = 384` → 12 strided steps per lane per block.
147|Attempt-5 pays 2 waves × 12 steps sequentially after the silu
148|barrier; this attempt pays 12 merged steps. A merged step issues
149|twice the loads (8 weight words, 2 scales) for twice the
150|accumulate work, so it costs more than a single-block step but
151|less than two — the gate/up precedent (attempt-4) hid ≈ 20% of
152|the merged chain's exposed latency at 1 row.
153|
154|- **1 row: 85.** Latency-bound (floor 11.1 µs). The down phase
155|  sits alone behind the silu barrier; at attempt-5's 92.1 µs the
156|  product chains (gate/up merged 24 steps + down 2×12 steps)
157|  dominate, so the down waves are roughly a third of the layer
158|  (≈ 30 µs). Collapsing 24 sequential steps into 12 merged ones
159|  at ≈ 1.3× the per-step cost (8 loads share the `tg_h[k]` read
160|  and the loop control) cuts the down phase to ≈ 23 µs, saving
161|  ≈ 7 µs → 92.1 − 7 ≈ **85 µs**. Still above compiled 75.9 — the
162|  `tg_x` load, silu, barriers and chained launch/link cost
163|  remain untouched — but it should roughly halve the 16.2 µs gap.
164|  The shared `q` itself is arithmetic-neutral; its only timing
165|  effect is restoring a legal 512-thread pipeline.
166|- **8 rows: 156.** 32 groups per call partly hide one group's
167|  down tail behind other groups' K loops (attempt-5 already at
168|  109.2 GB/s), so only part of the 1-row saving survives:
169|  162.0 − 6 ≈ **156 µs**, keeping the win over compiled 234.6.
170|- **32 rows: 540.** Streaming-bound (attempt-5: 132.3 GB/s).
171|  Group parallelism already hides load latency, so the merged
172|  loop buys nothing; the peak live accumulator count is the same
173|  64 floats gate/up already held in attempt-5, so no new spill
174|  tax is expected beyond attempt-6's identical merged step:
175|  534.8 + 5 ≈ **540 µs**, keeping the win over compiled 798.2.

178|3,840 B threadgroup memory) and the only change from attempt-5's

218|parallelism already hides load latency (32 rows, +4.9% GB/s,

220|8 rows, but it does not move the latency-bound 1-row size.

222|## Miss analysis (prediction 85 / 156 / 540, measured 93.8 / 160.1 / 510.1)
223|
224|Misses are +10.4% / +2.6% / −5.5% — all inside the 20% bar, so
225|no formal miss, but the size pattern was inverted versus the
226|prediction (saving predicted largest at 1 row, actually largest
227|at 32 rows) and that needs explaining:
228|
229|1. **The compilation fix worked exactly as predicted, the
230|   latency saving did not.** G1 passes at 512 threads with the
231|   same 3,840 B of threadgroup memory, confirming attempt-6's
232|   failure was the third distinct accumulator array, not
233|   threadgroup memory or the merged loop itself: two distinct
234|   arrays (`p`, shared `q`) fit, three do not. That part of the
235|   prediction (pure rename, identical bits) is confirmed by
236|   G2's differ 0 at all six sizes.
237|2. **At 1 row the down waves were not a third of the layer's
238|   latency in the way the arithmetic assumed.** The prediction
239|   priced the down phase at ≈ 30 µs and the merged step at
240|   1.3× a single-block step. Measured 93.8 ≈ attempt-5's 92.1
241|   says the merged step costs closer to 2× at this size: with
242|   only 4 threadgroups (one per pair) on 16 cores, the down
243|   phase's latency was already hidden *across* simdgroups —
244|   attempt-5's wave 0 runs 16 blocks concurrently per group,
245|   attempt-7 runs 12 simdgroups each serially merging two
246|   blocks, so concurrent in-flight loads per group fall
247|   (48 vs 64 simdgroup-block chains per call at 1 row) while
248|   each chain's step doubles its loads. The gate/up precedent
249|   hid ≈ 20% because gate and up *share* the `tg_x[k]` read and
250|   both blocks' loads were previously fully sequential phases;
251|   down's two blocks share only `tg_h[k]` and already overlapped
252|   across the 16-simdgroup wave. The remaining ≈ 19 µs gap to
253|   compiled (93.8 vs 74.8) is therefore still the `tg_x` load,
254|   silu, the two barriers and the chained launch/link cost —
255|   none of which this change touches.
256|3. **At 32 rows the merged loop pays for a different reason.**
257|   One wave instead of two removes a wave-quantization tail
258|   (wave 1 ran 8 of 16 simdgroups) on every pair and halves the
259|   down loop's barrier-free step count, which at 128 groups
260|   shows up as throughput: 138.8 vs 132.3 GB/s. The predicted
261|   +5 µs register tax did not appear (measured −24.7 µs vs

263|   live accumulators never exceed gate/up's 64 floats, so there
264|   is no new spill, and claim 2's cross-simdgroup overlap loss
265|   is hidden by group parallelism at this size.
266|
267|Lesson for `ineff-baseline-experts-2`: a merged pair helps only
268|where the two blocks were previously *phases* (gate then up,
269|fully sequential, shared activation read); where the blocks
270|already ran as concurrent simdgroups in one wave (down's 24
271|blocks), merging trades cross-simdgroup parallelism for
272|in-step parallelism and is latency-neutral at 4 groups — the
273|1-row remainder is fixed cost and the serial gate/up chain,
274|not the down wave count. Register headroom at 512 threads is
275|exactly two 32-float accumulators; a third distinct array,
276|however short-lived, fails G1.
277|
278|## Next change
279|
280|Leave the down interleave in (it is the best 32-row time and
281|G2-exact) and attack the actual 1-row remainder named above:
282|the `tg_x` load + silu + barrier chain and the chained fixed
283|cost. Concretely, overlap the down product's first K steps with
284|the silu tail (down blocks whose `tg_h` slice is already

286|but any such change must keep the full-bfloat16 silu bits and
287|every accumulation order, and must not add a third accumulator

1|"""The parts of MobileMoE-S's MoE block that a Muse Spark kernel may replace.
2|
3|Each slot has a reference (the port's own code, split as in breakdown.py),
4|named inputs and outputs (claude/muse-agent-brief.md), and a way to install
5|an implementation into MoE.__call__ for every layer. build() turns a launch
6|spec (data, never code) into mx.fast.metal_kernel calls.
7|
8|Record the grader's inputs from a real decode step (plain MLX, no API):
9|
10|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/slots.py capture
11|"""

17|import numpy as np

22|DTYPES = {

24|    "bfloat16": mx.bfloat16,
25|    "float16": mx.float16,

32|}

44|def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
45|    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
46|    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
47|    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
48|    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE

57|    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
58|    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort

64|    if do_sort:

69|            a,

304|def build(spec, sources, slot):
305|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks.
306|
307|    With "max_rows" in the spec, inputs with more rows than that run the slot's
308|    reference under mx.compile instead of the kernels, so an attempt can keep
309|    prompt-sized inputs on MLX's own code (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
310|    """
311|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
312|    kernels = []
313|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
314|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
315|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
316|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
317|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
318|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
319|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
320|            header=header,
321|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
322|        )
323|        kernels.append((k, fn))
324|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
325|    if missing:
326|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
327|    max_rows = spec.get("max_rows")
328|    if max_rows is not None:
329|        if isinstance(max_rows, bool) or not isinstance(max_rows, int) or max_rows < 1:
330|            raise ValueError(f"bad max_rows {max_rows!r}")
331|        compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])
332|
333|    def run(**inputs):
334|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
335|        if max_rows is not None and rows > max_rows:  # the compiled reference takes over
336|            out = compiled(*[inputs[n] for n in slot_in])
337|            return dict(zip(slot_out, out if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out]))
338|        env = dict(inputs)
339|        for k, fn in kernels:
340|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
341|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
342|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
343|            outs = fn(
344|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
345|                template=[
346|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
347|                ],
348|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
349|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
350|                output_shapes=[
351|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
352|                ],
353|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
354|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
355|            )
356|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
357|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
358|
359|    return run

1|"""Grade one kernel attempt: compile it, test it on captured inputs, time it.
2|
3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step
5|(1, 8 and 32 rows), and on every layer's inputs in a prefill, recorded as
6|it runs (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows): every output must be identical to the
7|reference's, bit for bit, since only then are the model's tokens identical
8|(claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md). The timing runs at the same six
9|sizes and chains the 20 layers, so each call waits for the one before, as in
10|the model. The grader prints its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when
11|given. It writes into an attempt folder only when --out points there, as
12|the Muse agent's builders do with grade.json; load() reads only spec.json and
13|the block-N.metal files.
14|
15|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt folder> <slot> [--out FILE]
16|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]
17|
18|The candidate and the compiled reference are timed in alternating repeats, so
19|drift in the GPU's clocks reaches both alike. At each size the candidate is
20|"faster" when it wins at least WINS_NEEDED of the REPEATS paired repeats (a
21|one-sided sign test at p < 0.01), "slower" when it loses that many, and
22|"same" otherwise; the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5% between
23|medians, so comparing medians alone would pass on noise. `beats_compiled`
24|needs both phases, decode and prefill: faster at every size of one, slower
25|at none of the other (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
26|
27|--baseline times an earlier, already graded attempt in the same run and adds
28|`beats_baseline`, judged the same way. From round 2 on, the bar is the
29|previous round's final attempt for the slot
30|(claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md). FOLDER alone is an attempt
31|for the same slot. For routing+combine, give either one routing+combine
32|attempt or `routing=FOLDER` and `combine=FOLDER`.

234|            calls[j]()
235|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
236|    return times
237|
238|
239|def compare(wins):
240|    """One size's verdict from the candidate's wins in REPEATS paired repeats."""
241|    if wins >= WINS_NEEDED:
242|        return "faster"
243|    if REPEATS - wins >= WINS_NEEDED:
244|        return "slower"
245|    return "same"
246|
247|
248|def judge(verdicts):
249|    """Each phase's verdict from its sizes' verdicts, and whether the candidate
250|    beats the bar: faster at every size of one phase, slower at no size of the other.
251|
252|    A phase is "faster" when every size is, "slower" when any size is, and
253|    "not slower" otherwise.
254|    """
255|    phases = {}
256|    for phase, prefix in PHASES.items():
257|        sizes = [v for size, v in verdicts.items() if size.startswith(prefix)]
258|        phases[phase] = (
259|            "faster" if all(v == "faster" for v in sizes)
260|            else "slower" if "slower" in sizes
261|            else "not slower"
262|        )
263|    beats = "faster" in phases.values() and "slower" not in phases.values()
264|    return phases, beats
265|
266|
267|def short_error(e):
268|    """The exception, keeping only the compiler's error lines from Metal builds."""
269|    text = "".join(traceback.format_exception_only(type(e), e)).strip()
270|    lines = text.splitlines()
271|    if len(lines) > 1 and "Unable to build metal library" in lines[0]:
272|        keep = [lines[0]]
273|        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
274|            if "error:" in line:
275|                keep += lines[i : i + 3]
276|        text = "\n".join(keep)
277|    return text[:4000]
278|
279|
280|def main():
281|    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
282|    ap.add_argument("attempt", type=Path)
283|    ap.add_argument("slot", choices=tuple(slots.SLOTS))
284|    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="also write the verdict here")
285|    ap.add_argument(
286|        "--baseline",
287|        action="append",
288|        default=[],
289|        metavar="[SLOT=]FOLDER",
290|        help="an earlier attempt to time in the same run (repeat for routing+combine)",
291|    )
292|    args = ap.parse_args()
293|    attempt, slot = args.attempt, args.slot
294|    gpu_lock.hold(f"check_candidate.py {attempt} {slot}")
295|    base = baselines(args.baseline, slot) if args.baseline else None
296|    result = {"slot": slot, "g1": False, "g2": False, "beats_compiled": False}
297|    if base:
298|        result |= {
299|            "baseline": args.baseline,
300|            "beats_baseline": False,
301|            "wins_needed": f"{WINS_NEEDED} of {REPEATS} paired repeats",
302|        }
303|    try:
304|        fns = load(attempt, slot)
305|        model = slots.load_model()
306|        weights = slots.model_expert_weights(model) if slot == "experts" else None
307|        stats = {}
308|        sizes = [("rows", lambda r=r: slots.load_inputs(r, weights)) for r in ROWS]
309|        sizes += [
310|            ("prefill rows", lambda r=r: slots.capture_prefill(model, r, weights))
311|            for r in slots.PROMPT_REQUESTS
312|        ]
313|        for kind, inputs in sizes:
314|            layers = inputs()
315|            size = f"{kind} {layers[0]['x'].shape[0]}"
316|            for part, fn in fns.items():
317|                check = {
318|                    "routing": check_routing,
319|                    "combine": check_combine,
320|                    "experts": check_experts,
321|                }[part]
322|                per_layer = [check(fn, layer) for layer in layers]
323|                errors = [s["error"] for s in per_layer if "error" in s]
324|                if errors:
325|                    stats[f"{part} {size}"] = {"error": errors[0]}
326|                    continue
327|                agg = {
328|                    k: (max if k.startswith("max") else sum)(s[k] for s in per_layer)
329|                    for k in per_layer[0]
330|                    if k != "example"
331|                }
332|                agg["pass"] = all(passes(part, s) for s in per_layer)
333|                examples = [
334|                    f"layer {i}, {s['example']}"
335|                    for i, s in enumerate(per_layer)
336|                    if "example" in s
337|                ]
338|                if examples:
339|                    agg["worst_example"] = examples[0]
340|                stats[f"{part} {size}"] = agg
341|            del layers
342|        result["g1"] = True
343|        result["correctness"] = stats
344|        result["g2"] = all(s.get("pass") for s in stats.values())
345|        if result["g2"]:
346|            timing = {}
347|            bars = ("compiled", "baseline") if base else ("compiled",)
348|            verdicts = {bar: {} for bar in bars}
349|            for kind, inputs in sizes:
350|                layers = inputs()
351|                size = f"{kind} {layers[0]['x'].shape[0]}"
352|                row = {"reference": 0.0}
353|                times = {name: [0.0] * REPEATS for name in ("candidate", *bars)}
354|                for part, fn in fns.items():
355|                    names = slots.SLOTS[part][0]
356|                    ref = slots.REFERENCE[part]
357|                    wrap = lambda f: lambda **kw: f(  # noqa: E731
358|                        *[kw[n] for n in names]
359|                    )
360|                    row["reference"] += timed(wrap(ref), layers, names)
361|                    together = {"candidate": fn, "compiled": wrap(mx.compile(ref))}
362|                    if base:
363|                        together["baseline"] = base[part]
364|                    paired = paired_times(list(together.values()), layers, names)
365|                    for name, t in zip(together, paired):
366|                        times[name] = [s + u for s, u in zip(times[name], t)]
367|                del layers
368|                row |= {name: statistics.median(t) for name, t in times.items()}
369|                for bar in bars:
370|                    wins = sum(c < b for c, b in zip(times["candidate"], times[bar]))
371|                    verdicts[bar][size] = compare(wins)
372|                    row |= {f"wins_vs_{bar}": wins, f"vs_{bar}": verdicts[bar][size]}
373|                timing[size] = {
374|                    k: round(v, 1) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in row.items()
375|                }
376|            result["timing_us_per_layer"] = timing
377|            for bar in bars:
378|                result[f"phases_vs_{bar}"], result[f"beats_{bar}"] = judge(verdicts[bar])
379|    except Exception as e:  # report the failure to the Muse agent as G1
380|        result["error"] = short_error(e)
381|    if args.out:
382|        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
383|        args.out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=1) + "\n")
384|    print(json.dumps(result))

9|## What it does

11|The `experts` slot of one MoE layer: for each row `r` and slot `j`,
12|`y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]`

16|with interleaved gate/up and interleaved down behind a `rows >= 60`
17|branch — a `qvm` replica below 60 rows, a scalar `qmm_accum`
18|(`bfloat16`-rounded dequant, contiguous `BK=32` order) at/above.

20|decode rows, and loses at 1 row and at every prefill size

13|## What happens
14|
15|At `rows >= 60` the slot kernel takes its prefill branch
16|(`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7/block-0.metal:22,59-72,103-112`),
17|one thread per output calling `qmm_accum`
18|(`block-1.metal:206-230`): a single thread walks all of K
19|(768 for gate/up, 384 for down) in `BK=32` contiguous
20|order, accumulating into one float `acc`. The arithmetic
21|is right — G2 passes with `differ 0` at all three prefill
22|sizes — but the issue pattern loses three ways at once:
23|
24|1. **A purely serial dependent chain per thread.** Each of
25|   the 884,736 iterations per pair (gate/up 384×768 each,
26|   down 768×384) does `acc += xv[k] * (bfloat)wq` on one
27|   accumulator: no second accumulator, no unrolling, so
28|   each iteration waits for the last — zero instruction
29|   overlap within a thread. Serial depth per thread (simd
30|   groups 0–7) is 768 (gate) + 768 (up) + 768 (down, two
31|   blocks) = 2,304 dependent iterations, plus silu. Gate
32|   and up run as fully sequential phases (384 of 512
33|   threads active in each, `block-0.metal:61-71`); down
34|   runs 2 waves (`:105-111`).
35|2. **Scalar redundant loads: ~7.1 MB issued per pair for
36|   553 KB of unique weight bytes (12.8×).** Per iteration
37|   each thread issues 1 W load + 1 S + 1 B device load +
38|   1 threadgroup `xv` load (`block-1.metal:223-226`), but
39|   8 lanes share each weight word (`word = wb + (lane >>
40|   3)`, `:217`) and all 32 lanes of a block share `S`,
41|   `B` and `xv[k]`. Issued per pair: W 884,736 words =
42|   3.54 MB vs 442,368 unique B (8×); S+B 884,736×2×2 B =
43|   3.54 MB vs 110,592 unique B (32×). All scalar,
44|   uncoalesced, per-thread.
45|3. **No cross-row reuse: per-pair grid at fan-ins of
46|   508–8,192 pairs.** Each pair streams its expert's full
47|   552,960 B independently, so unique-pair traffic is
48|   280.9 MB / 2,247 MB / 4,530 MB per layer at 127/1,016/
49|   2,048 rows, where MLX's grouped `gather_qmm_rhs` loads
50|   each appearing expert's tile once per `BM=16` row tile
51|   into threadgroup `Ws` and shares it across 16 rows
52|   (round-2 `territory-quantized-kernels.md` §C–§E,
53|   frozen), and issues 8×8×8 matrix instructions (~512
54|   MACs per simdgroup step vs this branch's 32 scalar
55|   MACs — a 16× ALU-issue gap per step).

2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-grader
4|- **Status:** done

7|- **Next:** none — checklist complete (6 pieces), 0 inefficiencies posted (grader runs no decode-step kernels); notes for baseline-*/g3 held in entry until their entries land; no notes to answer
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|Rounds 1 and 2's entries ([`muse-spark/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../exploration/territory-grader.md) and [`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md), frozen) mapped the grader through ADR 0010: bit-exact G2 at six sizes, chained piece timing at decode sizes only, median-vs-median `beats_compiled`, and the paired sign-test `--baseline` bar. Round 3 changes the judgment ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)): the piece timing runs at all six sizes with paired per-size verdicts, `beats_compiled` needs one phase faster and neither slower, and a spec may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference via `max_rows`. G3 moves to vLLM-only two-phase judgment (decode step, prompt time, whole-request time), and the lead's ready check ([`bench/grader/check_ready.py`](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py), [ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)) runs that same G3 inside the round. This entry writes only the delta. G1/G2 mechanics, the spec language, `capture`, and `gpu_lock` are cited to rounds 1–2, not re-described.
12|
13|## Checklist
14|
15|### 1. `check_candidate.py` — paired per-size verdicts and the two-phase judgment (check_candidate.py:51-58, 224-264, 345-378)
16|
17|- **Callers:** builders: `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt> <slot> [--out FILE]` ([check_candidate.py:15](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); no `--baseline` this round — no slot has one (round-3 README *Starting point*). Holds the GPU lock for the whole run ([check_candidate.py:294](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). One grader run is one attempt (ADR 0013); builders keep `grade.json` in the attempt folder.
18|- **Callees:** unchanged: `slots.build`/`load_inputs`/`capture_prefill`/`load_model`; `mx.eval` for correctness and timing; `mx.compile(ref)` for the compiled bar only.
19|- **Data:** `ROWS = (1, 8, 32)`, `PHASES = {"decode": "rows ", "prefill": "prefill rows "}` ([check_candidate.py:51-52](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); `REPEATS = 30`, `WINS_NEEDED = 22` computed by the same one-sided sign test at p < 0.01 as round 2 ([check_candidate.py:53-58](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).
20|- **What is new — paired timing at all six sizes:** timing runs only if G2 passes ([check_candidate.py:345](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), over the same six size inputs as correctness (decode `load_inputs` + prefill `capture_prefill`, [check_candidate.py:308-312,349](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per size and part, `paired_times` runs candidate and compiled (plus baseline when given) in rotating order within each of 30 repeats, each repeat a full chained 20-layer eval ([check_candidate.py:224-236](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per-part times are summed per repeat before wins are counted ([check_candidate.py:364-366](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), so for `routing+combine` the verdict is on summed time, as in round 2. The plain `reference` is still timed by unpaired median `timed()` ([check_candidate.py:360](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) — informational only, no verdict against it.
21|- **What is new — `compare`/`judge`:** per size, the candidate is `faster` with ≥22 wins, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same` ([check_candidate.py:239-245](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per phase: `faster` iff every size is, `slower` iff any size is, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` (and `beats_baseline`, same rule) is true iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower` ([check_candidate.py:248-264,377-378](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Consequences: two `faster` + one `same` in a phase is `not slower`, not `faster` — a single noisy size now blocks the bar instead of passing it (round 2's median-only rule passed on noise up to 5%, [ADR 0011:26](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); a `same` everywhere attempt never beats.
22|- **Invariants:** verdict JSON gains per-size `wins_vs_compiled`/`vs_compiled` (and baseline twins) plus `phases_vs_compiled`/`beats_compiled` ([check_candidate.py:368-378](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:207). On G2 failure there is still no timing at all.

24|### 2. `slots.py` `build` — the `max_rows` hand-off (slots.py:304-337)
25|
26|- **Callers:** `check_candidate.load` and `time_candidates.Variants`/`implementations`, via `slots.build(spec, sources, slot)` — so the hand-off applies identically in the piece timing, G2, G3 and the ready check.
27|- **What it does:** with `"max_rows"` in the spec (per part for `routing+combine`, brief:174), `run()` sends inputs with `rows > max_rows` to the slot's reference under `mx.compile` instead of the kernels ([slots.py:333-337](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). `rows` is read from the first slot input's `shape[0]` ([slots.py:334](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Validation: int ≥ 1, bools rejected ([slots.py:327-331](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); `compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])` is built once per `build` call.
28|- **Grading:** "bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes" (brief:173). G2 checks `run()`, so sizes above `max_rows` exercise the compiled reference through the attempt's own dispatch; the compiled reference of each slot was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes on 2026-11-04 (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`, [ADR 0011:34](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). Timing above `max_rows` runs the bar's own code, so it reads `same` by construction, never better ([ADR 0011:35](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)) — the claim for such an attempt is "faster decode, unchanged prefill" ([ADR 0011:48](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)).
29|- **The experts switch at 60 rows:** from 60 rows MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`) with different rounding ([slots.py:219-220](../../../bench/grader/slots.py); brief:187). Kernels running at rows ≥ 60 must match the large kernel's rounding; `max_rows` ≤ 59 keeps decode-built kernels on the `gather_qvm` side only. The boundary agent checks the hand-off sits on the right side of 60 for experts ([ADR 0011:47](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). Round 2's checked hand-off copy used `max_rows` 59 (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).
30|- **What the grader cannot see here:** any `max_rows` in 32..126 behaves identically at all six G2 sizes and all six timing sizes (tested sizes on each side are 32 and 127) — the grader cannot tell 59 (right side of 60) from 100 (wrong side). §4's `check_sizes.py` (59/60/61) is what distinguishes them; see *What the grader still cannot see* item 1.

40|- **Callers:** Claude after the round; inside the round, only `check_ready.py` calls it (in-process, pinned argv). Plain-MLX mode still runs token checks and timing for diagnosis, but the G3 verdict reads vLLM runs only ([time_candidates.py:170](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)).
41|- **Protocol:** `G3_SETTINGS = "1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024"`, `G3_REPEATS = 5`, 256 output tokens ([time_candidates.py:51-55,217](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)); vLLM with 512 MiB KV cache, 1 GiB when a prompt length exceeds 128 ([time_candidates.py:247-257](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)).
42|- **What it times** (`MEASURES`, [time_candidates.py:54](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)): `decode` = `period_median_ms`, the steady decode-step period; `prompt` = `prompt_ms`, first forward pass to the first step with no prompt tokens left — "until every prompt was processed" ([repeat_fixes.py:277-282](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)); `request` = `wall_ms`, the whole run's wall time. Variants: `base`, `compiled-<slot>`, `muse-<slot>`, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` with several slots ([time_candidates.py:111-132](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)) — a combination is measured as one, never summed.
43|- **The pass rule** (`against`/`g3`, [time_candidates.py:163-201](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)): per setting and measure, `faster`/`slower` mean the two 5-repeat ranges don't overlap, else `same`. Per measure: `faster` iff every setting is, `slower` iff any is, else `not slower`. A `muse-*` variant passes against a bar iff decode or prompt is `faster` and none of the three is `slower`; `g3` needs that against both `base` and its `compiled-*` counterpart. A `muse-*` variant without its compiled counterpart is not judged ([time_candidates.py:179-181](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)). Verdict to `g3-vllm.json`.
44|- **Why 5 repeats:** with 3, two identical engines' ranges miss per direction with p = 1/20, and 8 "never slower" checks per phase fail an unchanged phase ~1/3 of the time; with 5 it is 1/252 per check, ~3% over 8 ([ADR 0011:40](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). The motivating case: a hand-off copy at `max_rows` 59 read `slower` on prompt time at 32×1,024 by 0.5% (ranges 16 ms apart) although above 59 rows it *is* the compiled reference. Residual ~3% false-`slower` risk per phase stands.
45|- **Token checks:** `rf.vllm_checks` — greedy tokens (24, temperature 0) at 1 and 32 requests of 128-token prompts, plus one steady decode step's kernel count, per variant ([repeat_fixes.py:175-176](../../../bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py)).
46|
47|### 5. `check_ready.py` — the in-round ready check (whole file)
48|
49|- **Callers:** the lead only, at most twice per round (ADR 0013, skill v8). `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_ready.py <new out folder> SLOT=FOLDER...`, or `--audit <out folder>` ([check_ready.py:24-25](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
50|- **What it runs:** `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3 protocol fixed in code — four workloads, 5 repeats, 256 tokens, every submitted slot in one call so the combination is measured as `muse-all` ([check_ready.py:48-56,81-86](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). No flag changes the protocol; `check_protocol` stops before any GPU work if `time_candidates.py`'s G3 constants changed ([check_ready.py:63-70](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). The out folder must be new ([check_ready.py:76-78](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Cost: ~10–15 min per slot, ~21 min for two, blocking builders' grader runs (ADR 0013).
51|- **What it audits** (the log, never the verdict file, [check_ready.py:103-150](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)): (1) exactly one `ready-check` marker with the protocol; (2) every timed run is vLLM at a G3 workload with 256 tokens and all three measurements present; (3) the variants are exactly `base`, `compiled-<slot>`/`muse-<slot>` per slot, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` with >1 slot, with repeats 0–4 at each workload; (4) every non-base variant keeps the unchanged model's greedy tokens at 1 and 32 requests — and a `compiled-*` variant that changes tokens is "no bar", invalidating the run ([check_ready.py:131-140](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)); (5) `g3-vllm.json` equals the G3 verdict recomputed from the log ([check_ready.py:142-148](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
52|- **What it writes:** `ready-verdict.json` — per `muse-*` variant its pass (G3 and same tokens), `vs` per bar, `phases` per bar, plus per-variant/workload/measurement median/min/max/n, `same_tokens`, `pass`, `judged`, `problems` ([check_ready.py:152-174](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Exit 0: every `muse-*` passes; 1: a variant fails — the verdict stands; 2: the run stopped or broke the protocol — no verdict, may rerun in a new folder ([check_ready.py:20-22,205-213](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).
53|- **`--audit`:** re-checks a finished folder without the GPU; compares `pass`, `judged`, `variants`, `medians`, `same_tokens` against the saved `ready-verdict.json`, writes nothing, exits 2 on disagreement ([check_ready.py:195-203](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). Used by the swarm's checker and by Claude after the round. Tested against 13 gaming tricks plus the control (`bench/grader/test_check_ready.py`, ADR 0013); verified live on round 2's submission (`results/runs/2026-11-04-ready-check/`, exit 1: routing fails on prompt time, combine on the decode step, the pair on all three).
54|- **Invariants:** only a passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's post-round G3 stays the authority (ADR 0013).
55|
56|### 6. Verdict shape delta (check_candidate.py:296-302, 336-378)
57|
58|`{slot, g1, g2, beats_compiled, correctness: {"<part> <kind> <rows>": {...}}, timing_us_per_layer: {"rows N"/"prefill rows N": {reference, candidate, compiled, wins_vs_compiled, vs_compiled}}, phases_vs_compiled}` plus, with `--baseline`, `{baseline, beats_baseline, wins_needed, phases_vs_baseline}`. Size labels carry the phase prefix (`rows 32` vs `prefill rows 127`), which is what `judge()` splits on.
59|
60|## What the grader still cannot see
61|
62|Round 2's list stands except item 3 (prefill speed — now timed) and item 5c (median-only `beats_compiled` — now a sign test at every size). What is new or still open:
63|
64|1. **`max_rows` between the tested sizes.** Any value in 32..126 is identical at all six G2/timing sizes; the grader cannot see which side of 60 an experts hand-off sits on. `check_sizes.py` (59/60/61) closes it where the boundary agent runs it — the piece verdict never does.
65|2. **Kernel speed at 33–126 rows is unmeasured by the piece timing** (decode sizes stop at 32, prefill starts at 127). With `max_rows` > 32 the kernels run there in real serving (vLLM chunked prefills), and only G3's prompt time at its four workloads can show it — and only if a chunk lands there. Hypotheses with `max_rows` above 32 carry this as **Unverified**.
66|3. **Sizes above 2,048 rows** are tested nowhere (G2 stops at 2,048, `check_sizes` at 1,500); real prefill chunks reach 2,048 under `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`, so this is the top edge, not a gap in practice.
67|4. **Prefill beyond the first chunk** of 128-token seeded-random prompts, other prompt lengths, real-token distributions, mixed prefill+decode batches — unchanged from round 2. `check_sizes` varies the first chunk's length but nothing else.
68|5. **Hand-off exactness above `max_rows` at untested sizes** rests on compiled==reference there, shown at the six sizes (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`) plus the hand-off path at `SIZES` wherever `check_sizes` runs the attempt.
69|6. **Whole-request noise at 1 request:** repeats spread 6–41%, so G3/ready-check there mostly say `same` — which passes "never slower" without showing a gain ([ADR 0011:52](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A real small gain hidden by noise is lost too, because a verdict stands (ADR 0013).
70|7. **A log invented whole** passes the audit; only Claude's independent G3 catches it ([ADR 0013:69-72](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)). Old logs without marker/token count are refused, not evidence.
71|8. **Threadgroup memory** still unchecked (only the ≤1024-thread product, [slots.py:341-342](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); Metal rejects oversize kernels as opaque G1 exceptions.
72|9. **Link-kernel caveats carried over** (round-2 item 5a/b/d): 20 link kernels' additive cost in every timed eval; the 10% chain-fidelity figure unverified by the grader; host wall time with CPU dispatch inside; clocks unpinned.
73|10. **Plain-MLX behaviour is no longer gated** — G3 and the ready check judge vLLM runs only (`time_candidates plain` remains for diagnosis). Round 2's plain-vs-vLLM divergences (combine at 32, all-three at 8) are now visible in-round only through the ready check's vLLM lens.

Summarizing performance predictions for decode kernels across six sizes with arithmetic versus baseline and noting missing max_rows and unverified items.

Extending predictions with early-exit and copy overheads for decode and prefill while weighing small margins against win-rate risk.
