tool_calls.args:
{"content":"# attempt-3 (round 3): grouped/tiled prefill replica (builder-2-c)

Hypothesis `hyp-2-experts-prefill`, slot `experts`, baseline `none`,
starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7`
(G1+G2 pass, slower at 1 row and at every prefill size).
Direction (c): grouped/tiled replica of `gather_qmm_rhs` issue.

## The one main change

Four kernels replace the single fused kernel. The decode path is
starting-point code; the `rows >= 60` prefill branch is replaced by a
grouped, fused, MMA-tiled path in the shape of MLX's `gather_qmm_rhs`.

- **Decode kernel** (`block-0.metal` + `block-1.metal`): attempt-7's
  body with one added line (`if (prefill) return;` above the dispatch)
  and the output renamed `y` to `y_decode` (3 stores). Every decode
  computation line below the return is byte-identical to attempt-7,
  including the dead prefill `else` branches (never executed: the
  return exits first at rows >= 60, the `!prefill` guard skips them
  below). Helpers (`qvm_gate_up_pair`, `qvm_down_pair`, `qmm_accum`)
  are byte-identical by copy. Grid/threadgroup unchanged
  (`rows*2048`, 512). At decode sizes it computes exactly attempt-7;
  at prefill sizes its groups exit before any load.
- **Count kernel** (`block-4.metal`, new): one group of 64 threads
  counting-sorts the `B = rows*4` pairs by expert (threads 0-59 own
  one expert, two scans over `inds`) and writes `sorted_pairs[B]`,
  `expert_offsets[61]` and `tile_offsets[61]` (row-tile prefix, 16
  pairs per tile). Runs at every size; trivial cost (<= 8192 pairs).
  Computed once per call (MLX recomputes offsets per product).
- **Prefill kernel** (`block-2.metal` + `block-3.metal`, new): one
  group per row tile (`rows*256` threads, 64 per group, `rows*4`
  groups). Groups past `tile_offsets[60]` exit after one read (no
  empty-tile schedule scans). Each useful group owns one (expert,
  16-pair tile): it loads the tile's pair list, streams gate/up
  weight tiles once per tile (shared across <= 16 rows), accumulates
  with 8-wide frag MMA in contiguous BK=32 order (replicating
  `BlockMMA` per-output order: sequential K-tiles, 4 8-wide steps),
  runs the full-bfloat16 swiglu on-chip into `tg_h`, then streams
  down weights the same way and stores positionally. Dequant is
  MLX's bits=4 form verbatim (`s*(low)+b`, `(s/16)*(high mask)+b`,
  bfloat-rounded). Threadgroup: `tg_h` 12,288 B + `Xs` 1,280 B +
  two `Ws` 2,560 B each + pairs 64 B = 18,752 B (of 32,768 B).
  Rows < 60 return immediately.
- **Select kernel** (`block-5.metal`, new): one thread per `y`
  element copies `y_decode` or `y_prefill` on `rows >= 60`. Exact
  bfloat copy, no rounding.

No `max_rows`: kernels run at every row count (decode kernel below
60, prefill kernel at/above, selected by the same threshold MLX uses).

## Which inefficiency it removes, and how

- `ineff-baseline-experts-1` (scalar prefill 15-28x slower): the
  scalar `qmm_accum` per-pair branch never runs (decode kernel exits,
  prefill kernel replaces it). Cross-row weight sharing removes the
  8.5/13.7/15.3x distinct-traffic gap (one dequant per tile serves
  <= 16 rows); hardware MMA removes the scalar-issue gap (32 8x8
  MACs per K-tile per group vs 32 scalar MACs); 64-thread groups
  remove the 512-thread-per-pair overprovisioning. Takes the
  tile-waste prize (no dispatched empty tiles; partial tiles still
  pad, as in MLX) and the offsets prize (one count pass, not three)
  for free, plus x row-tile re-reads (x staged once per K-tile, not
  per N-tile) and fused gate/up/hidden traffic (never leaves the
  chip per tile).
- `ineff-baseline-experts-2` (1-row decode gap): deliberately kept.
  The decode path is attempt-7's, so the 1-row loss persists; hyp-4
  fixes it on this attempt's winner. A prefill fix that slows decode
  is not an improvement (ADR 0011): the added decode cost is one
  exact copy plus two near-empty launches (below).

## Limits (by hand)

Decode: 512 threads/group, 3,840 B (unchanged). Prefill: 64
threads/group, 18,752 B. Count: 64 threads, ~500 B. Select: 256
threads, none. All <= 1,024 threads and <= 32 KB. Grids scale with
rows at every size; the `gid -> (expert, tile)` map covers the worst
case (all pairs one expert needs `ceil(B/16)` tiles; `B` groups with
dense tile offsets always suffice). Each `y` element is written
exactly once (each pair in exactly one tile; within a tile each
thread's 8 frag elements are disjoint; the select copies each once).

## Predicted us per layer at the six sizes (chained)

Basis (measured, piece,
`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-experts-attempt-7.json`):
starting point vs compiled 92.1 vs 78.6 (1 row), 162.8 vs 235.5 (8),
515.3 vs 797.8 (32), 15,220.0 vs 960.8 (127), 119,154.4 vs 4,306.0
(1,016), 240,681.1 vs 11,998.9 (2,048). Baseline `none`.

Decode (rows < 60 run decode + count + select; prefill groups exit):
select copies 6/49/196 KB at 0.03/0.25/1.0 us byte floor + ~1 us
launch; empty prefill groups (4/32/128 x 64 threads, one compare)
~0.5/1/2 us; count (B <= 128) < 0.5 us. Total overhead ~2/3/4 us.

- 1 row: 92.1 + 3 = **95** (vs 78.6 compiled, `slower`, keeps the
  starting-point loss for hyp-4).
- 8 rows: 162.8 + 3 = **166** (vs 235.5, `faster`, keeps the win).
- 32 rows: 515.3 + 4 = **519** (vs 797.8, `faster`, keeps the win).

Prefill (rows >= 60 run count + prefill + select; decode groups exit):
grouped MMA at the compiled rate (~961/4,306/11,999) minus banked
waste (empty-tile schedule scans on 1,488/624/1,488 empty groups per
layer, offsets <= 13 us/layer, x re-reads where they miss, fused
gate/up/hidden device traffic ~12/50/100 us if DRAM) plus overhead
(select 3.9/31/63 us byte floors + launch, decode-empty 508/4,064/
8,192 x 512 threads ~5/15/30 us, count ~1/5/10 us). Net ~5% faster:

- 127 rows: **900** (vs 960.8, `faster`).
- 1,016 rows: **4,100** (vs 4,306.0, `faster`).
- 2,048 rows: **11,500** (vs 11,998.9, `faster`).

G1 prediction: pass (decode is attempt-7's legal launch; prefill is
64 threads and 18.8 KB; count/select trivial). G2 prediction: pass
with `differ == 0` (decode byte-identical; prefill replicates dequant
values, BK=32 frag order and the four bfloat16 points; select exact).
`beats_compiled` prediction: false (prefill `faster` everywhere,
decode `slower` at 1 row) -- the prefill phase win is the claim;
hyp-4 takes the 1-row remainder.

## What this attempt leaves unmeasured

Kernel speed at 33-126 rows (piece timing jumps 32 to 127); sizes
above 2,048; prefill beyond the first seeded chunk, other
lengths/distributions, mixed batches; the 32 KB limit (hand-checked
above); unwritten threadgroup reads and thread-timing dependence
(none by construction: all groups take uniform early exits, all tg
writes precede barriers); NaN-vs-NaN equality; whole-request
composition (ready check). The 2,048-row compiled basis carries
run-to-run variance (round-3 `territory-quantized-kernels.md` S5
caveat: 11,998.9 vs 7,347.5 across runs).

## Verdict

(to be filled after the one grader run)

1|# Attempt 1 — builder-1-a, direction (a): noinline device-function barriers
2|
3|First attempt in this direction (round 3, `hyp-1-combine-devolatilize`,
4|slot `combine`, baseline `none`). Builds on the starting point
5|`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1` (G1+G2 pass,
6|`beats_compiled` true, fails G3 on volatile-stall cost).
7|
8|## What changed
9|
10|Only the barrier mechanism. Indexing, grid (`rows*768`), threadgroup
11|[256,1,1], inputs/outputs, the fold order, both bfloat16 roundings, and
12|the final line `bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]` are verbatim from the
13|starting point. The seven `volatile float` barriers:
14|
15|```metal
16|volatile float p0 = float(y[ybase]) * weights[wbase];
17|...
18|volatile float s01 = p0 + p1;
19|volatile float s012 = s01 + p2;
20|volatile float acc = s012 + p3;
21|```
22|
23|become seven calls through two helpers living in `header_block`
24|(`block-1.metal`, wired via `"header_block": 1` in `spec.json`):
25|
26|```metal
27|__attribute__((noinline)) float combine_mul(float a, float b) { return a * b; }
28|__attribute__((noinline)) float combine_add(float a, float b) { return a + b; }
29|...
30|float p0 = combine_mul(float(y[ybase]), weights[wbase]);
31|...
32|float s01 = combine_add(p0, p1);
33|float s012 = combine_add(s01, p2);
34|float acc = combine_add(s012, p3);
35|```
36|
37|Each mul/add executes in its own non-inlined call, so its result rounds
38|once to f32 at the return and no expression tree spans the call
39|boundary for the compiler to FP-contract. Values cross in registers:
40|no thread-private memory traffic. Same 7 f32 materialisations, same
41|left fold `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3`, same two bfloat16 roundings — the only
42|change the Boundary permits.
43|
44|## Inefficiency removed
45|
46|`ineff-baseline-combine-1` (confirmed): the seven volatiles cost
47|+0.142/+0.508/+1.441 ms per decode step in vLLM (+7.1/+25.4/+72.1
48|µs/layer) plus the +1,501.7 ms prompt twin on 32×128, while the chained
49|piece timing prices them near zero. This attempt keeps the exact
50|per-op rounding the volatiles bought and removes the memory traffic
51|that caused the context-dependent stall.
52|
53|## Prediction (µs per layer, chained piece timing)
54|
55|The piece timing cannot see the prize (Boundary *can't see*,
56|load-bearing): the starting point already beats compiled at all six
57|sizes there. Basis: the starting point's re-grade medians
58|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-combine-attempt-1.json`):
59|
60|- decode 1 / 8 / 32 rows: 45.7 / 47.9 / 64.6 (compiled 53.4 / 56.4 / 69.1)
61|- prefill 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows: 62.8 / 226.5 / 273.0 (compiled 66.1 / 271.6 / 520.4)
62|
63|Arithmetic: replacing 7 volatile spill pairs per output with 7 register
64|calls changes only sub-floor terms. Call overhead ≈ 7 calls × ~768
65|outputs/row × a few cycles, under 0.5 µs/layer against the ~45–65 µs
66|chained floor at decode; at prefill the kernel is traffic-shaped and
67|the barrier term is likewise negligible. Same-kernel-twice noise is up
68|to 5% (brief). So predicted candidate ≈ starting point medians ±5%:
69|**≈45.7 / 47.9 / 64.6 decode, ≈62.8 / 226.5 / 273.0 prefill**,

71|differ 0 at all six sizes. The real prize — recovery to ≈

100|  0/0.0. First difference: none. The noinline barriers keep every

103|  wins, verdict): rows 1: 59.5 / 55.5 / **46.8** (28, faster); rows 8:

106|  prefill 1,016: 437.2 / 278.3 / **104.6** (30, faster); prefill 2,048:
107|  861.8 / 590.0 / **188.0** (30, faster).
108|- `phases_vs_compiled`: decode faster, prefill faster;
109|  `beats_compiled` true.
110|- Against the starting point's re-grade medians (45.7/47.9/64.6
111|  decode, 62.8/226.5/273.0 prefill): +2.4% / −12% / −24% decode,
112|  −30% / −54% / −31% prefill.

114|### Why the timing beat the prediction (>20% at four sizes)

116|Predicted ≈ starting-point medians ±5% (volatiles "priced near zero"
117|in the chained timing); measured −24% at 32 rows and −30/−54/−31% at

1|// Header for the devolatilized combine kernel (direction b: compiler
2|// contraction switch, no volatile, no helper calls).
3|//
4|// The Metal compiler FP-contracts mul+add pairs into FMAs by default,
5|// which keeps products unrounded into their consumer add and breaks the
6|// reference's per-op f32 rounding. The two pragmas below switch
7|// contraction off for the kernel function defined after this header
8|// (MLX emits `header` before the main function; `help(mx.fast.
9|// metal_kernel)`). With contraction off, the backend may not fuse any
10|// fmul+fadd into an fma, so each mul and each add in the body rounds
11|// once to f32 with its value living in a register — the same 7
12|// materialisation points as the starting point's seven volatiles, with
13|// zero thread-private memory traffic and no extra instructions.
14|//
15|// Both spellings are given: the standard C99 form and the Clang form.
16|// Either one alone disables contraction for the function; the second is
17|// belt and braces against pragma-dialect drift. They must live here, not
18|// in the body: FP-option pragmas take effect for functions defined after
19|// them, and the body is inside the generated function. Reassociation
20|// needs no pragma: the compiler does not reassociate without fast-math
21|// flags, and the grader passes none (slots.build sets no
22|// compile_options, so math_mode stays "safe").
23|#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF
24|#pragma clang fp contract(off)

8|## The one main change
9|
10|Four kernels replace the single fused kernel. The decode path is
11|starting-point code; the `rows >= 60` prefill branch is replaced by a
12|grouped, fused, MMA-tiled path in the shape of MLX's `gather_qmm_rhs`.

14|- **Decode kernel** (`block-0.metal` + `block-1.metal`): attempt-7's
15|  body with one added line (`if (prefill) return;` above the dispatch)
16|  and the output renamed `y` to `y_decode` (3 stores). Every decode
17|  computation line below the return is byte-identical to attempt-7,
18|  including the dead prefill `else` branches (never executed: the
19|  return exits first at rows >= 60, the `!prefill` guard skips them
20|  below). Helpers (`qvm_gate_up_pair`, `qvm_down_pair`, `qmm_accum`)
21|  are byte-identical by copy. Grid/threadgroup unchanged
22|  (`rows*2048`, 512). At decode sizes it computes exactly attempt-7;
23|  at prefill sizes its groups exit before any load.
24|- **Count kernel** (`block-4.metal`, new): one group of 64 threads
25|  counting-sorts the `B = rows*4` pairs by expert (threads 0-59 own
26|  one expert, two scans over `inds`) and writes `sorted_pairs[B]`,
27|  `expert_offsets[61]` and `tile_offsets[61]` (row-tile prefix, 16
28|  pairs per tile). Runs at every size; trivial cost (<= 8192 pairs).
29|  Computed once per call (MLX recomputes offsets per product).
30|- **Prefill kernel** (`block-2.metal` + `block-3.metal`, new): one
31|  group per row tile (`rows*256` threads, 64 per group, `rows*4`
32|  groups). Groups past `tile_offsets[60]` exit after one read (no
33|  empty-tile schedule scans). Each useful group owns one (expert,
34|  16-pair tile): it loads the tile's pair list, streams gate/up
35|  weight tiles once per tile (shared across <= 16 rows), accumulates
36|  with 8-wide frag MMA in contiguous BK=32 order (replicating
37|  `BlockMMA` per-output order: sequential K-tiles, 4 8-wide steps),
38|  runs the full-bfloat16 swiglu on-chip into `tg_h`, then streams
39|  down weights the same way and stores positionally. Dequant is
40|  MLX's bits=4 form verbatim (`s*(low)+b`, `(s/16)*(high mask)+b`,
41|  bfloat-rounded). Threadgroup: `tg_h` 12,288 B + `Xs` 1,280 B +
42|  two `Ws` 2,560 B each + pairs 64 B = 18,752 B (of 32,768 B).
43|  Rows < 60 return immediately.
44|- **Select kernel** (`block-5.metal`, new): one thread per `y`
45|  element copies `y_decode` or `y_prefill` on `rows >= 60`. Exact
46|  bfloat copy, no rounding.
47|
48|No `max_rows`: kernels run at every row count (decode kernel below
49|60, prefill kernel at/above, selected by the same threshold MLX uses).
50|
51|## Which inefficiency it removes, and how
52|
53|- `ineff-baseline-experts-1` (scalar prefill 15-28x slower): the
54|  scalar `qmm_accum` per-pair branch never runs (decode kernel exits,
55|  prefill kernel replaces it). Cross-row weight sharing removes the
56|  8.5/13.7/15.3x distinct-traffic gap (one dequant per tile serves
57|  <= 16 rows); hardware MMA removes the scalar-issue gap (32 8x8
58|  MACs per K-tile per group vs 32 scalar MACs); 64-thread groups
59|  remove the 512-thread-per-pair overprovisioning. Takes the
60|  tile-waste prize (no dispatched empty tiles; partial tiles still
61|  pad, as in MLX) and the offsets prize (one count pass, not three)
62|  for free, plus x row-tile re-reads (x staged once per K-tile, not
63|  per N-tile) and fused gate/up/hidden traffic (never leaves the
64|  chip per tile).
65|- `ineff-baseline-experts-2` (1-row decode gap): deliberately kept.
66|  The decode path is attempt-7's, so the 1-row loss persists; hyp-4
67|  fixes it on this attempt's winner. A prefill fix that slows decode
68|  is not an improvement (ADR 0011): the added decode cost is one
69|  exact copy plus two near-empty launches (below).
70|
71|## Limits (by hand)
72|
73|Decode: 512 threads/group, 3,840 B (unchanged). Prefill: 64
74|threads/group, 18,752 B. Count: 64 threads, ~500 B. Select: 256
75|threads, none. All <= 1,024 threads and <= 32 KB. Grids scale with
76|rows at every size; the `gid -> (expert, tile)` map covers the worst
77|case (all pairs one expert needs `ceil(B/16)` tiles; `B` groups with
78|dense tile offsets always suffice). Each `y` element is written
79|exactly once (each pair in exactly one tile; within a tile each
80|thread's 8 frag elements are disjoint; the select copies each once).
81|
82|## Predicted us per layer at the six sizes (chained)
83|
84|Basis (measured, piece,
85|`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-experts-attempt-7.json`):
86|starting point vs compiled 92.1 vs 78.6 (1 row), 162.8 vs 235.5 (8),
87|515.3 vs 797.8 (32), 15,220.0 vs 960.8 (127), 119,154.4 vs 4,306.0
88|(1,016), 240,681.1 vs 11,998.9 (2,048). Baseline `none`.
89|
90|Decode (rows < 60 run decode + count + select; prefill groups exit):
91|select copies 6/49/196 KB at 0.03/0.25/1.0 us byte floor + ~1 us
92|launch; empty prefill groups (4/32/128 x 64 threads, one compare)
93|~0.5/1/2 us; count (B <= 128) < 0.5 us. Total overhead ~2/3/4 us.
94|
95|- 1 row: 92.1 + 3 = **95** (vs 78.6 compiled, `slower`, keeps the
96|  starting-point loss for hyp-4).
97|- 8 rows: 162.8 + 3 = **166** (vs 235.5, `faster`, keeps the win).
98|- 32 rows: 515.3 + 4 = **519** (vs 797.8, `faster`, keeps the win).
99|
100|Prefill (rows >= 60 run count + prefill + select; decode groups exit):
101|grouped MMA at the compiled rate (~961/4,306/11,999) minus banked
102|waste (empty-tile schedule scans on 1,488/624/1,488 empty groups per
103|layer, offsets <= 13 us/layer, x re-reads where they miss, fused
104|gate/up/hidden device traffic ~12/50/100 us if DRAM) plus overhead
105|(select 3.9/31/63 us byte floors + launch, decode-empty 508/4,064/
106|8,192 x 512 threads ~5/15/30 us, count ~1/5/10 us). Net ~5% faster:
107|
108|- 127 rows: **900** (vs 960.8, `faster`).
109|- 1,016 rows: **4,100** (vs 4,306.0, `faster`).
110|- 2,048 rows: **11,500** (vs 11,998.9, `faster`).
111|
112|G1 prediction: pass (decode is attempt-7's legal launch; prefill is
113|64 threads and 18.8 KB; count/select trivial). G2 prediction: pass
114|with `differ == 0` (decode byte-identical; prefill replicates dequant
115|values, BK=32 frag order and the four bfloat16 points; select exact).
116|`beats_compiled` prediction: false (prefill `faster` everywhere,
117|decode `slower` at 1 row) -- the prefill phase win is the claim;
118|hyp-4 takes the 1-row remainder.
119|
120|## What this attempt leaves unmeasured
121|
122|Kernel speed at 33-126 rows (piece timing jumps 32 to 127); sizes
123|above 2,048; prefill beyond the first seeded chunk, other
124|lengths/distributions, mixed batches; the 32 KB limit (hand-checked
125|above); unwritten threadgroup reads and thread-timing dependence
126|(none by construction: all groups take uniform early exits, all tg
127|writes precede barriers); NaN-vs-NaN equality; whole-request
128|composition (ready check). The 2,048-row compiled basis carries
129|run-to-run variance (round-3 `territory-quantized-kernels.md` S5
130|caveat: 11,998.9 vs 7,347.5 across runs).
131|
132|## Verdict
133|
134|G1 **fail** (no G2, no timing). `grade.json`: `g1: false`,
135|`error: [metal::Device] Unable to build metal library from source`,
136|six errors all from one cause: `block-3.metal` declares
137|`uint half = thread_idx & 1u;` (`dequant_tile_4bit`), but `half` is a
138|reserved type name in Metal (half-precision float), so the compiler
139|rejects it as `cannot combine with previous 'type-name' declaration
140|specifier` and every use of the variable fails to parse. Nothing else
141|was reached: decode exactness, prefill bits and all six timings are
142|unmeasured. Predicted 95/166/519 decode and 900/4,100/11,500 prefill
143|vs compiled 78.6/235.5/797.8 and 960.8/4,306.0/11,998.9 stand as
144|predictions beside no measured values.
145|
146|## Why it failed (miss analysis)
147|
148|The failure is a Metal reserved word, not the design: `half` (like
149|`float`, `uint`, `bfloat`) cannot name a variable. The fix is a
150|rename (`half` -> `part`) in `dequant_tile_4bit` (1 declaration + 5
151|uses, `block-3.metal`). No other identifier in the attempt collides
152|(`e1`, `yy`, `ss`, `pp` in block-2 avoid the `y`/`s`/`p` outputs;
153|`sg`, `fm`, `fn`, `w_lo`/`w_hi` are free). The design itself --
154|count + decode + grouped-MMA prefill + select, 18,752 B threadgroup,
155|dense tile-offset map -- never compiled, so its G2/timing predictions
156|are untested, not refuted.
157|
158|## Next change
159|
160|Copy this attempt to a new number, rename `half` to `part` in
161|`block-3.metal`, and grade. If G1 then passes and G2 fails, the first
162|suspect is the MMA frag mapping (per-output 8-wide order vs MLX's
163|interleaved WM/WN assignment), diagnosed by the first differing
164|element's (row, expert slot, column) in the G2 report.

## Why prefill missed (miss analysis)

The prediction assumed grouped MMA runs at the compiled rate. Three
structural gaps in the code explain most of the ~2.3-2.7x (unprofiled —
ranked by arithmetic, not measurement):

1. **`x` is gathered 12x per tile.** The gate/up nest is `g` outer,
   `k` inner (`block-2.metal:54-78`): every (N-tile, K-tile) pair
   reloads its `x` tile from device memory. Per tile group that is 12
   x 24 x 1 KB = 288 KB of gathers instead of 24 KB (attempt-3's notes
   claimed "x staged once per K-tile" — the nest orders it per N-tile
   too; L2 absorbs an unknown share). At 2,048 rows, 512 tiles x 288 KB
   = 147 MB/layer of `x` traffic, ~7.4 ms/layer at 20 GB/s if
   uncached — same order as the whole 17.2 ms measurement.
2. **The MMA is scalar-fed at low occupancy.** Each `mma_step`
   (`block-3.metal:95-130`) issues ~34 scalar threadgroup float loads
   per lane plus 2 `simdgroup_barrier`s to feed 4 MMA ops, and the
   group holds only 64 threads behind ~19 KB of threadgroup memory
   (1-3 groups resident per core), so barrier and load latency has
   little to hide behind. Count: 12x24x4x2 + 24x12x4 = 3,456
   `mma_step`s and 1,152 full-group barriers per tile group.
3. **Partial tiles at small sizes.** At 127 rows the mean expert owns
   ~8.5 of 16 pairs, so roughly half the MMA work covers zero-padded
   rows (127 rows is also the worst ratio, 2.67x). MLX pads too, so
   this is at most a fraction of the gap.

Decode overhead also missed: +30/+44/+69 µs vs the round-2 basis
(92.1/162.8/515.3) against +3/+3/+4 predicted. Part is the select
pass (decode writes `y_decode`, select reads + rewrites it: +12/98/393
KB traffic ≈ +0.6/5/20 µs at 20 GB/s) plus 3 extra launches x 20
layers, but ~24 µs/layer at 1 row is unexplained by that model —
recorded as unexplained, not as free.

## Next change

Interchange the gate/up nest to `k` outer / `g` inner, loading each
`x` tile once and reusing `Xs` across the 12 N-tiles (accumulators
`Cg`/`Cu` become per-`g` arrays). One change, aimed at cause 1; if
prefill then stays >1.5x slower, the scalar MMA feed (cause 2) is the
bigger term and direction (c) needs a cooperative frag-load redesign."}

31|- **The arithmetic contract is unchanged.** The reference chain, the 5-step sequence (each product rounded once to float32; fold `((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃` with a rounding after every add; one bfloat16 round; single-rounding bfloat16 `+ shared`), the FMA-contraction ban, and the no-60-row-switch statement all hold verbatim — `ref_combine` is unchanged, so the required evaluation is identical to round 2's.
32|- **Starting point against this boundary (changed).** Round 2's starting point failed this boundary on contraction (0/2/2 differ decode, 6/50/130 prefill). The round-3 starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1` **passes** it: G1 pass, G2 pass with differ 0 / max ULP 0.0 at all six sizes (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-3-combine-exact.md:79-83`; re-graded `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-combine-attempt-1.json`). Its seven `volatile float` barriers (`p0..p3`, `s01`, `s012`, `acc`, `block-0.metal:33-39`) materialise exactly the required roundings — each written once and read once in program order (`hyp-3-combine-exact.md:136-137`). What the fix may change is therefore **only the barrier mechanism** (e.g. the hypothesised `__attribute__((noinline))` device-function barriers, expressible via `header_block`, `bench/grader/slots.py:313-322`; thread/layout decomposition stays free as in round 2). It may not change any rounding: same 7 float32 materialisations, same fold order, same two bfloat16 roundings. The failure it must avoid is G2 (exactness), and the failure it must cure is G3: the starting point beats compiled at all six piece sizes yet costs +1.051 ms/step in vLLM at 32 requests (`muse-spark/round-3/exploration/ineff-g3-1.md:15`; mechanism in `ineff-baseline-combine-1.md:15-36`).

36|

38|- **Piece timing (changed to two-phase paired).** Timing still runs only if G2 passes, but now at all six sizes with paired per-size verdicts (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:345-378`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:206-224`; `claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md`; `muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md` §1): per size, candidate vs `mx.compile(ref_combine)` over 30 chained repeats, `faster` with ≥22 wins, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same`; per phase, `faster` iff every size is, `slower` iff any size is, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`. 20|element, 14 accesses × 4 B = 56 B of thread-private stack traffic per
21|thread — that the compiler cannot keep in registers, forward, elide, or

31|(`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §3 vs `claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`

48|Per layer, at decode 1 / 8 / 32 rows and prefill 127 / 1,016 / 2,048
49|rows (peak 200 GB/s, `claude/GLOSSARY.md`):

51|- Kernels × fixed cost: 1 kernel/layer either way — the barriers add no
52|  launch; the chained floor (~32–40 µs/layer decode) is shared with the
53|  twin. Not the cost.
54|- Bytes ÷ peak: slot traffic 9,232 B/row plus spill traffic 56
55|  B/thread = rows×43,008 B/layer, i.e. 52,240 B / 418 KB / 1.67 MB at
56|  decode = **0.26 / 2.1 / 8.4 µs**, and 6.6 / 53 / 107 MB at prefill =
57|  **33 / 265 / 533 µs**. Spill bytes alone: 43 KB / 344 KB / 1.375 MB

8|## What changed
9|
10|Only the barrier mechanism. Indexing, grid (`rows*768`), threadgroup
11|[256,1,1], inputs/outputs, the fold order, both bfloat16 roundings, and
12|the final line `bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]` are verbatim from the
13|starting point. The seven `volatile float` barriers:
14|
15|```metal
16|volatile float p0 = float(y[ybase]) * weights[wbase];
17|...
18|volatile float s01 = p0 + p1;
19|volatile float s012 = s01 + p2;
20|volatile float acc = s012 + p3;
21|```
22|
23|become seven calls through two helpers living in `header_block`
24|(`block-1.metal`, wired via `"header_block": 1` in `spec.json`):
25|
26|```metal
27|__attribute__((noinline)) float combine_mul(float a, float b) { return a * b; }
28|__attribute__((noinline)) float combine_add(float a, float b) { return a + b; }
29|...
30|float p0 = combine_mul(float(y[ybase]), weights[wbase]);
31|...
32|float s01 = combine_add(p0, p1);
33|float s012 = combine_add(s01, p2);
34|float acc = combine_add(s012, p3);
35|```
36|
37|Each mul/add executes in its own non-inlined call, so its result rounds
38|once to f32 at the return and no expression tree spans the call
39|boundary for the compiler to FP-contract. Values cross in registers:
40|no thread-private memory traffic. Same 7 f32 materialisations, same
41|left fold `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3`, same two bfloat16 roundings — the only
42|change the Boundary permits.

1|# Attempt 2 — builder-1-b, direction (b): FP-contract-off pragma barrier
2|
3|First attempt in this direction (round 3, `hyp-1-combine-devolatilize`,
4|slot `combine`, baseline `none`). Builds on the starting point
5|`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1`, which passes G1+G2 and
6|`beats_compiled` but fails G3 (+1.051 ms/step in vLLM at 32 requests).
7|
8|## What changed
9|
10|Only the barrier mechanism. Grid (`rows*768`), threadgroup [256,1,1],
11|index/base lines, inputs/outputs and the final
12|`bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]` line are verbatim from the starting
13|point. The seven `volatile float` locals (`p0..p3`, `s01`, `s012`,
14|`acc`) become seven plain `float` locals with the identical 7-op
15|sequence, and a new header block (`block-1.metal`, wired via
16|`"header_block": 1` — the only `spec.json` delta) disables FP
17|contraction for the kernel:
18|
19|```metal
20|#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF
21|#pragma clang fp contract(off)
22|```
23|
24|MLX emits `header` before the main function, so the pragmas precede the
25|kernel definition, which is where FP-option pragmas take effect. No
26|`volatile` anywhere in code, no `__attribute__((noinline))` helpers,
27|no extra functions, calls, or memory traffic of any kind.
28|
29|Why this is contraction-proof: with contract(off) the backend may not
30|fuse any fmul+fadd into an fma — this is the compiler's own
31|contraction switch, so there is no transform left that can keep a
32|product unrounded into its consumer add. Each of the 7 statements is
33|then one rounded f32 op on register values: the same 7 materialisation
34|points, same fold order `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3`, same two bfloat16 roundings
35|as the starting point. Reassociation needs no pragma: it is off without
36|fast-math flags, and the grader sets none. The proof is G2 itself: any
37|surviving contraction shows the starting point's old signature (decode
38|0/2/2, prefill 6/50/130 differ).
39|
40|## Inefficiency removed
41|
42|`ineff-baseline-combine-1` (confirmed): the seven volatiles' 7 stores +
43|7 loads per output (56 B/thread of thread-private traffic, 43,008
44|B/row/layer) stall the decode step (+7.1/+25.4/+72.1 µs/layer vLLM)
45|and the 32×128 prompt (+1,501.7 ms twin). The pragmas keep every value
46|in registers — ~10 live floats, no spill pressure — so the barrier
47|costs zero bytes and zero instructions. Same fix covers both phases:
48|both run these identical lines.
49|
50|## Prediction (µs per layer, chained paired basis)
51|
52|Starting point (re-grade `grade-phases-combine-attempt-1.json`, via
53|`ineff-g3-1`): decode reference/candidate 52.8/45.7 @1, 71.2/47.9 @8,
54|87.0/64.6 @32; compiled 53.4/56.4/69.1. Prefill candidate
55|62.8/226.5/273.0 vs compiled 66.1/271.6/520.4.

60|  µs decode, 5.9 / 46.9 / 94.5 µs prefill. Floor dominates decode.
61|- Spill floor removed: 43,008 B/row ÷ 200 GB/s = 0.22 / 1.7 / 6.9 µs
62|  decode, 27 / 218 / 440 µs prefill — an upper bound the quiet grader
63|  chain mostly does not price (the inefficiency entry), so decode is
64|  predicted at the starting point ±5% paired noise, prefill
65|  same-or-slightly-better.
66|- Predicted candidate: **45 / 47 / 63** decode, **61 / 220 / 265**
67|  prefill. Margins to compiled (≈8/9/6 decode, ≈5/50/255 prefill)
68|  reproduce the starting point's 28–30/30 wins: `faster` at all six
69|  sizes, both phases `faster`, `beats_compiled` true.
70|- G1 pass, G2 differ 0 / max ULP 0.0 at all six sizes.
71|

73|≈0.5 ms/step at 8 requests, ≈1.4 ms/step at 32; order-1-s prompt
74|recovery) is invisible to the piece timing by construction and needs
75|the ready check.

78|
79|None. The kernel runs identical lines at all sizes, combine has no
80|MLX kernel switch underneath, and the boundary's grader note says no
81|hand-off is needed for this hypothesis's direction.

85|For the hypothesis entry's **Unverified** list: the in-step stall

88|`check_sizes.py` can probe 25 sizes incl. 59/60/61); the 33–126 band;

122|eager reference swung the other way at rows 1 (59.1 here vs 52.8
123|re-grade). Absolute chained medians therefore do not transfer across
124|runs; the valid evidence is the same-run paired verdict, which is
125|`faster` at all six sizes (24–30/30 wins) with both phases `faster`.

131|predict combine piece times as same-run margins to compiled, never as
132|cross-run absolutes. (Noted in `ineff-baseline-combine-1.md`.)
133|

1|# Inefficiency: combine attempt-1 costs ~1.1 ms per decode step at 32 requests where the piece timing says faster
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-g3
4|- **Status:** confirmed
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T17:46:33Z
7|- **Next:** done — confirmed by verifier (see Verdict); mechanism belongs to baseline-combine
8|
9|## Slot
10|
11|`combine`. Measurement side owned by territory `g3`; kernel-side mechanism owned by territory `baseline-combine` (starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1`).
12|
13|## What happens
14|
15|`time_candidates.py` installs combine attempt-1 alone (`muse-combine`) in every layer's `MoE.__call__` and times the decode step (median of 3 shuffled repeats, 128-token prompts, 256 tokens; [territory-g3.md](territory-g3.md) piece 4). At 32 requests the step is **slower than the unchanged model by +1.051 ms (vLLM) / +1.168 ms (plain MLX)** — +52.6 / +58.4 µs per layer — while the chained piece timing has the same kernel **faster** than the reference (64.6 vs 87.0 µs/layer) and than the compiled reference (64.6 vs 69.1) in `grade-phases-combine-attempt-1.json`. Full derivation in [territory-g3.md](territory-g3.md) gap 1. A prefill twin: adding combine-a1 to routing+experts-a7 slows the 32×128 prompt by **+1501.7 ms** (11533.4 vs 10031.7, no range overlap) where the prefill piece says combine saves 11.5 ms/layer/chunk at 2048 rows.
16|
17|## Cost
18|
19|Piece-vs-step swing = (G3 change vs unchanged) − (candidate − reference piece × 20 layers), ms per decode step. Piece from `grade-phases-combine-attempt-1.json` (reference / candidate: 52.8 / 45.7 at 1 row, 71.2 / 47.9 at 8, 87.0 / 64.6 at 32); G3 from `console-vllm.txt` / `console-plain.txt` (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/`).
20|
21|| Engine | 1 request | 8 requests | 32 requests |
22||---|---|---|---|
23|| vLLM: piece-implied | −0.142 | −0.466 | −0.448 |
24|| vLLM: G3 measured | −0.372 | −0.197 | **+1.051** |
25|| vLLM: **swing** | −0.230 | +0.269 | **+1.499** |
26|| plain: piece-implied | −0.142 | −0.466 | −0.448 |
27|| plain: G3 measured | −0.424 | −0.112 | **+1.168** |
28|| plain: **swing** | −0.282 | +0.354 | **+1.616** |
29|
30|Per layer (÷20): vLLM −11.5 / +13.5 / **+75.0 µs**, plain −14.1 / +17.7 / **+80.8 µs**. Against the compiled reference (G3 muse-combine minus G3 compiled-combine, vs piece candidate−compiled × 20): in-step penalty +6.1 / +11.2 / **+66.2 µs/layer** at 1 / 8 / 32 rows in vLLM (+0.122 / +0.224 / +1.324 ms/step) — the penalty grows with rows and explodes at 32.
31|
32|Reproduction: pairs run (plain, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2-pairs/`) combine-a1 at 32: +1.051 ms — identical to the main vLLM figure; engine comparison submitted-minus-routing at 32×128: +0.537 − (−0.374) ≈ +0.91 ms. Four runs, both engines. Prefill twin per chunk per layer: +1501.7 ms / (2 chunks × 20 layers) = +37.5 µs/layer/chunk at 2048 rows vs piece −573.2 (273.0 − 846.2).
33|
34|In bytes: the slot's traffic is 9,232 B/row (`notes.md`), 295 KB/layer at 32 rows ≈ 1.5 µs at peak bandwidth; the paid +52.6 µs/layer is ~35× the traffic floor.
35|
36|## Kind
37|
38|Overhead-bound (in the terms of `claude/GLOSSARY.md`): the step is far from peak bandwidth and peak compute, and the lost time scales with neither weight bytes (traffic floor 1.5 µs vs 52.6 paid) nor kernel count (one kernel replaces five, additively — piece 5). Ruled out: the kernel's own chained work (measured faster), token divergence (bit-exact at all 6 + 25 sizes and end to end), repeat noise (no range overlap anywhere it is claimed: vLLM muse-combine [31.433–31.547] vs base [30.346–30.513]).
39|
40|## Spans
41|
42|`g3` (measurement), `baseline-combine` (the kernel: grid `rows*768` threads in 256-thread threadgroups, volatile-stepwise fold, no threadgroup memory), `grader` (the chained piece timing is the instrument that cannot see this cost).
43|
44|## Predicted saving
45|
46|If the in-step penalty were removed while keeping the kernel's chained work, the step gains back the swing: up to **1.50 ms/step at 32 requests in vLLM** (1.62 plain), i.e. muse-combine would measure ≈ −0.45 ms (the piece-implied value) instead of +1.05 ms; **0.27 ms/step at 8 requests** (0.35 plain); nothing claimed at 1 request, where the swing is negative (over-delivers) and within 1-row noise. At prefill sizes, removing the twin recovers **up to 1.5 s of 32×128 prompt time** on the all-three variant (measured 11533.4 ms, would be ≈10032 ms). Per prefill chunk (chained basis): nothing further — the kernel already beats compiled at 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows (62.8 / 226.5 / 273.0 vs 66.1 / 271.6 / 520.4 µs/layer), so no per-chunk saving is predicted on the grader basis; the prize is the in-step composition only. This is an upper bound on the prize, not a prediction that a specific kernel change recovers it: the mechanism is unknown, and any fix must hold the bit-exact G2 at all six sizes.
47|

56|- **confirmed:** traffic 9,232 B/row (combine notes:73) → 295.4 KB at 32 rows ≈ 1.5 µs floor; 52.6 paid ≈ 35× ✓; one kernel replaces five (−80 over 20 layers: pairs jsonl 866→786 at rows 1; reductions additive −200−80−120 = −400 = 866−466) ✓.

58|- **confirmed:** saving — swing prizes 1.50/1.62 and 0.27/0.35 ms/step ✓; prefill already beats compiled at all three sizes (62.8/226.5/273.0 vs 66.1/271.6/520.4, JSON), nothing further on the grader basis ✓; upper-bound framing with G2 intact ✓.

61|## From other agents
62|
63|explorer-baseline-combine, 2026-11-04T17:45:55Z — mechanism found, owned from my side in `ineff-baseline-combine-1.md` (kernel-side companion to this entry; no change to your measurement claimed). The +1.05 ms is the starting point's seven volatile rounding barriers (`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1/block-0.metal:33-39`, 14 thread-private accesses/output element): round-1 attempt-1 is the same kernel with a byte-identical spec and verbatim index/final lines but no volatiles, and its G3 was −0.514/−0.705/−0.390 ms — the twin swing is +0.142/+0.508/+1.441 ms/step (+7.1/+25.4/+72.1 µs/layer), with cross-run drift bounded at ±0.1 ms by the round-1-triple control both runs timed. <skill-body id="muse-round">
---
name: muse-round
description: Run one round of the Muse agent on the MobileMoE-S kernels as a swarm. Explorers map the code and measurements into a shared analysis; then competing builders write and grade fused Metal kernels for the top inefficiencies. From round 2 on, the round starts from the previous rounds' results and must beat their best attempts. Both phases are tracked in shared documents.
---

# One round of the Muse agent: a swarm explores, then builds

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed on main and tagged `muse-code-era` before the first Muse Code session; each later version is committed before the round that uses it. [Who made what](../../../PROVENANCE.md).*

**Skill version 8.** This file, the role cards and tracking.md are versioned together; [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists every version. Each round records the version it ran (see *Versions* in tracking.md).

You are the **lead** of a Muse Code session in your own worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. The first prompt names the Meta model you run as, the name your commit subjects start with, and the co-author line every commit ends with. `claude/muse-agent-brief.md` fixes the task, the slots, the tools and limits, the grader command and the pass criteria (G1, G2). Four ADRs change it in five ways:

1. **Harness** ([ADR 0006](../../../claude/adr/0006-muse-spark-in-muse-code.md)). You are a Muse Code session, not a Claude Code one. Muse Code adds no trailer, so you write the first prompt's co-author line on every commit yourself (see *Commits*).
2. **No attempt limit and no stop rule** (ADR 0006). The brief's *When a slot stops* no longer applies: you decide when a slot is done. Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try.
3. **A swarm** ([ADR 0007](../../../claude/adr/0007-muse-spark-swarm.md)). Helpers explore and build; you coordinate and commit.
4. **Files** (ADR 0007, [ADR 0009](../../../claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md)). Each round writes in its own **round folder**: round 1 at the top of `muse-spark/`, round N from 2 on in `muse-spark/round-<N>/`. It holds `exploration/` and `implementation/`, the round's shared documents, which replace `strategy.md`; `kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>/`; and `summary.md`. tracking.md writes it `<round>/`.
5. **Rounds build on each other** (ADR 0009). A finished round's files are frozen: read them and cite them, and the hooks refuse any change to them. From round 2 on, a slot may have a **baseline**: the best attempt so far that passes the current G2 and that Claude's G3 accepted: against the unchanged model and the compiled reference, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A new attempt must beat it in the same grader run. A slot without one has a **starting point** instead: an earlier attempt to build from, which Claude's measurement names, with what kept it from being a baseline.

The rest of the brief stands. The goal: kernels that make whole requests faster. In the grader they pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither (ADR 0011), and where the slot has a baseline `beats_baseline` true too, because they remove a cause you can name. Then the **ready check**, the same G3 Claude runs after the round, run by you inside it, must pass them before they are `ready` ([ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)). A faster decode step bought with a slower prefill is no improvement, and a claim no one measured is no result. An attempt built for decode sizes may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference with `max_rows` (the brief's launch spec). The Muse agent was Muse Spark in round 1 and Muse Wonder in round 2 ([ADR 0008](../../../claude/adr/0008-muse-wonder.md)), and is Muse Spark's contributor model again from round 3 ([ADR 0012](../../../claude/adr/0012-muse-spark-contributor-unattended.md)); the first prompt names the model you run as, and documents from earlier rounds say the model of their round. No one approves your tool calls during the round, so the rules here are yours to keep.

## The swarm

| Role | Name | Task | Card |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lead** (you) | | Start the helpers, keep the two READMEs, settle clashes, commit | this file |
| **Explorer** | `explorer-<territory>` | Map one territory into entries, and find where it loses time | [explorer.md](explorer.md) |
| **Verifier** | `verifier` | Check every inefficiency against its sources | [verifier.md](verifier.md) |
| **Builder** | `builder-<n>-<letter>` | Write and grade one solution for one hypothesis: one attempt | [builder.md](builder.md) |
| **Boundary agent** | `boundary-<n>` | Write what a hypothesis's solution must keep identical, and check passing attempts against it | [boundary.md](boundary.md) |
| **Checker** | `checker-<n>`, `checker-final` | Check every speed claim against the file it cites: a hypothesis's before it closes, and the round's final claims | [checker.md](checker.md) |

You don't explore, build or grade yourself; the one GPU job you run is the ready check (step 4). Start each helper with a prompt of this shape:

> You are `<name>`, a `<role>` in round `<N>`'s swarm; this round writes in `<round folder>`. Read `.agents/skills/muse-round/<card>` and `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md`, then: `<task>`.

[tracking.md](tracking.md) describes the shared documents (the two phase folders, their READMEs, entries and logs) and the rules every agent keeps. Read it before starting anyone. Up to 12 agents run at once, you included.

**A checkpoint** is what you do each time a helper returns, and whenever the log shows something to settle:
1. **Read the log.** Read the phase log since your last checkpoint.
2. **Settle clashes.** When two entries describe one cause, keep the fuller one and set the other's status to `superseded by <entry>`. When two helpers work on one item, redirect one of them (`subagent_send_message`). Log what you decided.
3. **Refresh the tracker.** Update the phase README's tracker table, and raise the version of each hypothesis entry that changed.
4. **Raise the version.** Raise the phase README to its next version, and add its line to `## Versions`, naming the entries that changed and their versions (see *Versions* in tracking.md).
5. **Commit** the phase folder, plus any attempt that came back, as that version (see *Commits*).

## The round

### 0. Find where you are

- Run `git log --oneline main -1`, then `git tag --list -n1 'muse-round-*'`, which lists the finished rounds. **This round** is one more than the highest; with none, it is round 1. Its folder is `muse-spark/round-<N>/` (round 1: `muse-spark/`).
- `git log --oneline --grep '^Muse ' muse-code-era..HEAD` lists the Muse agent's commits of every round.
- **From round 2 on,** read Claude's measurement of the previous round, `claude/findings/muse-round-<N-1>.md`. It has the G3 results and names each slot's baseline or starting point. If it is missing, stop and reply "Claude's measurement of round <N-1> is missing": this round builds on it.
- If this round's folder already exists, a session stopped partway: carry on from its READMEs' last versions.
- Read the brief.

**Done** when you can name the round number and its folder, and from round 2 on each slot's baseline or starting point and the latest G3 results.

### 1. The starting point (from round 2 on)

This is the round's plan, built on what the earlier rounds learned. Read:
- the previous rounds' final exploration and implementation READMEs and `summary.md`;
- the `notes.md` of each baseline or starting-point attempt;
- Claude's measurement.

Then write the opening of this round's `exploration/README.md` (set up as in step 2.1), a section **Starting point**:
- **Per slot:**
  - the baseline, or the starting point where there is none, and its piece timing;
  - its G3 effect, and how that compares with what was predicted, with the reason where Claude's measurement gives one;
  - what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time.
- **What is left:**
  - the confirmed inefficiencies not yet built or not fully removed, ranked by predicted saving against the baselines, or the reference where a slot has none;
  - the slots not yet tried, for example `routing+combine`;
  - the recommendations outside the slots.
- **Refuted claims,** which no one chases again.
- **Territories** this round opens (step 2.2), each with the line of this section that reopens it.

Commit it as exploration v1. **Done** when every slot has its baseline or starting point and every territory has its reason.

### 2. Exploration

1. **Set up the folder.** Write `<round>/exploration/README.md` with a heading, its version line (v1, with skill version 8), the tracker (one row per territory) and `## Versions`, and an empty `log.md`.
2. **Start the explorers and the verifier,** all at once.
   - **Round 1** starts with these territories:

     | Territory | Covers |
     |---|---|
     | `model` | `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py`: the decoder layer, `MoE.__call__` and everything around the slots |
     | `switch-layers` | `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py`: the routed experts' path, `gather_qmm`, the sort from 16 rows |
     | `quantized-kernels` | `quantized.h` and `quantized_utils.h` in `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/`: the `affine_gather_*` kernels behind `gather_qmm` |
     | `other-kernels` | the other Metal kernels in the same folder that the routing and combine slots launch: sort, softmax, reductions, elementwise, copies |
     | `vllm-metal` | `third_party/vllm-metal/vllm_metal/`: how the engine runs a decode step and a prefill chunk around the model |
     | `grader` | `bench/grader/`: the slot interface, what G1, G2 and the piece timing measure, and so the boundary every solution keeps |
     | `findings` | `claude/findings/` and `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/` |
     | `runs` | `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/`, `2026-10-29-baseline/` and `2026-10-30-micro/` |

   - **From round 2 on,** the starting point lists the territories:
     - `baseline-<slot>` for each slot: its baseline's kernels and `spec.json`, which are now the code in the slot, or its starting point's. Map them with the checklist, and find where they still lose time and, for a starting point, why it fails G2;
     - `g3`: Claude's measurement of the previous round, where the end-to-end change differs from the piece timing, and why;
     - of round 1's territories, only those the starting point reopens. An explorer starts from that territory's earlier entries and writes only what is new.
3. **Refocus as costs show up.** When an entry shows that one file holds most of a territory's cost, split it off as a territory of its own, with its own explorer. Merge or close a territory that turns out to hold nothing, and add one when an inefficiency points somewhere no one covers. Log each change and update the tracker.
4. **Checkpoint** each time a helper returns.

**Done** when every territory entry is `done`, the verifier has returned, and every inefficiency is `confirmed`, `refuted` or `superseded`.

### 3. The analysis

Write the final `<round>/exploration/README.md`. It is the round's report on the code, for this round's builders and for future improvements:

- **Tracker:** the final table.
- **Starting point** (from round 2 on), as written in step 1, with any correction exploration made.
- **Context:** the decode step and the prefill, the MoE block and its slots, and what the measurements say about where the time goes in each.
- **Territory map:** how the territories feed each other. For each territory: what it receives, what it passes on, and its measured cost.
- **Inefficiencies, ranked:**
  - the confirmed ones inside the slots, ranked by predicted saving as a share of the decode step, averaged over 1, 8 and 32 rows, or of the prefill chunk, averaged over 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows; from round 2 on, the saving is against the baseline where the slot has one;
  - each with what removing it does to the other phase, and whether a hand-off (`max_rows`) keeps that phase unchanged;
  - each with its cost, kind and entry;
  - Claude's findings marked as Claude's, earlier rounds' entries linked as theirs, and this round's own reading marked as yours.
- **Recommendations:** the confirmed inefficiencies outside the slots, with their evidence. They're for surucuonur's team.
- **Refuted claims,** in one line each, so no one chases them again.
- **Files read:** links to each territory entry's list.

Commit it. **Done** when every ranked item links a confirmed entry and every number in the README has its source.

### 4. Implementation

Take the ranked inefficiencies in order, at most two at a time, in different slots so their attempts never touch. Write `<round>/implementation/README.md` with a heading, its version line, the tracker and `## Versions`, and an empty `log.md`. For each hypothesis:

1. **Open the hypothesis.** Write `<round>/implementation/hyp-<n>-<slug>.md`, with status `boundary`, the inefficiency, the slot and, from round 2 on, the slot's baseline folder or `none`. Add its tracker row and log it.
2. **Draw its boundary.** Start `boundary-<n>` to write the boundary, and wait for it.
3. **Compete.**
   - Set the status to `building`.
   - Start 2 or 3 builders, `builder-<n>-a`, `-b` and `-c`. Give each a different direction drawn from the analysis: for example, fusing kernels, reading each weight byte once, or a different threadgroup shape. From round 2 on, a direction may start from the baseline's or starting point's kernels, or from scratch.
4. **Collect.** Each time a builder returns:
   - checkpoint, committing its attempt folder with the hypothesis entry, the README and the log;
   - if the attempt passed G2, start `boundary-<n>` to check it.
5. **Harden.**
   - Pick the best attempt: it passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline`, and it is the fastest across the six sizes.
   - Set the status to `hardening`, and start a builder for that attempt's next single change.
   - Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove.
   - **Change approach after three alike failures.** Keep the hypothesis entry's failure ledger at each collect: every graded attempt that lost, the size or phase it lost at, and its named cause. When three attempts have lost at the same phase for the same cause, the next one changes approach (another kernel structure, parallelisation or dataflow, not a tuning), and its `notes.md` says "approach change: from X to Y"; or you log why not. A cause renamed without a measurement that refutes the old one is the same cause.
6. **Close.**
   - **`candidate`:** the best attempt passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline` true, and you can name no further change worth making. Write the **Decision**: the attempt, why it is best, and the change in whole requests you predict, labelled a prediction. Then start `checker-<n>` on the entry; the hypothesis is a candidate once its **Checks** section says `pass`.
   - **`dropped`:** say why. A slot whose hypotheses are all dropped keeps its baseline, or the reference where it has none.

Then open the next-ranked inefficiency.

**The ready check** ([ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)). Once no hypothesis is building or hardening and at least one is a `candidate`, run it yourself, over every candidate in one call:

```bash
.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_ready.py <round>/checks/ready-<k> <slot>=<attempt folder> [<slot>=<attempt folder> ...]
```

It times the candidates in vLLM exactly as Claude's G3 will after the round, each alone and, with more than one, all together, then audits its own log and writes `ready-verdict.json`. It takes about 10 to 15 minutes per slot, more for an attempt with a slow prefill, and waits its turn for the GPU. Commit its folder at the next checkpoint.
- **Exit 0 or 1: a verdict, and it stands.** A candidate whose `muse-<slot>` passes becomes `ready`; one that fails goes back to `hardening` with the failure in its ledger, or to `dropped`. Cite the file either way. With more than one candidate, submitting them together needs `muse-all` to pass; if some pass alone and `muse-all` fails, a second check may take only those.
- **Exit 2: no verdict.** The run stopped or broke the protocol; run it again in a new folder.
- **At most two ready checks per round.**

**Done** when no confirmed inefficiency is left that you judge will pay, and every candidate has a ready-check verdict. Write why in the implementation README.

### 5. Finish

1. **The implementation README:** the final tracker, one paragraph per hypothesis, and a **Ready to test** section. It names the attempt per slot that goes to Claude's G3: a `ready` attempt, the baseline kept, or the reference. For the `ready` ones it shows the ready check's measured change in the four workloads (the decode step, the prompt time and the whole request, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference), citing `ready-verdict.json`, with your earlier prediction beside it, labelled PREDICTION, and the **Unverified** list. Nothing else in it is an end-to-end number.
2. **The exploration README:** add *What building taught*, the analysis corrected by what the attempts showed.
3. **`<round>/summary.md`:** a `## Round N` section with:
   - the model, the skill version this round ran, and the final versions of both READMEs;
   - the final attempt per slot;
   - the number of graded attempts per slot, this round and over all rounds;
   - the ready check's measured change, citing its file;
   - what you'd try next;
   - your recommendations outside the slots.
4. **Check, commit, reply.** Start `checker-final` on *Ready to test* and the summary, and fix what it finds until it signs `pass`. Then commit, and reply with this round's commits and the words "Round N finished".

## Your own rules

- **Writes:**
  - you write the two READMEs, the hypothesis entries' status blocks and decisions, and `summary.md`;
  - every helper writes only what its card names;
  - all of it stays in this round's folder.
- **Claude's G3 after the round is the authority;** your ready check is the same measurement, made earlier. vLLM runs only through the ready check.
- **The rules every agent keeps** are in tracking.md.

## Commits

You are the only agent that commits. Commit only on `muse-agent`.
- **What to add:** this round's phase folders that exist so far (only `exploration` until implementation starts) and the attempt folders that came back. An attempt another builder is still writing waits for its own commit. An entry that is mid-edit is committed as it stands, and finished in a later commit.
- **The message:**
  - every subject starts with the name the first prompt gives you, then a colon;
  - a checkpoint's subject is `<name>: <phase> v<N>: <what changed>`, the version it records;
  - every message ends with the first prompt's co-author line, exactly.

For example, in round 2 as Muse Wonder:

```bash
git add muse-spark/round-2/exploration muse-spark/round-2/implementation muse-spark/round-2/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>
git commit -m "Muse Wonder: implementation v4: experts attempt 3 graded, beats baseline" \
  -m "Co-Authored-By: Muse Wonder (Meta Model API) <muse-wonder@meta-model-api.invalid>"
```

Use no other co-author. The hooks refuse a commit without a Muse agent's co-author, a commit outside `muse-spark/`, a change to a finished round's files, a new file outside this round's folder, and any merge. Push, merge, rebase, tags, git config and hook skipping stay with surucuonur.

</skill-body>
</read-skill-result>

23|medians, so comparing medians alone would pass on noise. `beats_compiled`
24|needs both phases, decode and prefill: faster at every size of one, slower

192|def chained(fn, layers, names):
193|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
194|
195|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
196|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
197|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
198|    """
199|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
200|    outs = []
201|    for layer in layers:
202|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
203|        if outs:
204|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
205|        out = fn(**args)
206|        if isinstance(out, dict):
207|            out = list(out.values())
208|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
209|    return outs

212|def timed(fn, layers, names):
213|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
214|    for _ in range(3):
215|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
216|    times = []
217|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
218|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
219|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
220|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
221|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

226|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
227|    for _ in range(3):
228|        for call in calls:
229|            call()
230|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
231|    for i in range(REPEATS):
232|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
233|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
234|            calls[j]()
235|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)

72|            transpose=False,

76|            sorted_indices=do_sort,
77|        )

79|    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
80|    if do_sort:
81|        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)

88|def expert_weights(experts):
89|    """A layer's SwitchGLU weights, named as in the experts slot."""
90|    return {
91|        f"{p}_{t}": getattr(experts, f"{p}_proj")[k]
92|        for p in ("gate", "up", "down")
93|        for t, k in (("w", "weight"), ("scales", "scales"), ("biases", "biases"))
94|    }

97|def make_moe_call(routing=ref_routing, combine=ref_combine, experts=None):
98|    """MoE.__call__ with its slots swapped for *routing*, *combine*, *experts*.
99|
100|    With the references it gives the port's outputs bit for bit (checked by
101|    check_identity), so any difference comes from the swapped slot. With
102|    experts=None the port's own SwitchGLU runs.
103|    """
104|
105|    def moe_call(self, x):
106|        lead = x.shape[:-1]
107|        flat = x.reshape(-1, D)
108|        bias = self.expert_bias.astype(mx.float32)
109|        inds, weights = routing(flat, self.router.weight, bias)
110|        if experts is None:
111|            y = self.experts(x, inds.reshape(*lead, K))
112|        else:
113|            w = expert_weights(self.experts)
114|            y = experts(flat, inds, *[w[n] for n in EXPERT_WEIGHTS])
115|        shared = self.shared_expert(x)
116|        out = combine(y.reshape(-1, K, D), weights, shared.reshape(-1, D))
117|        return out.reshape(*lead, D)
118|
119|    return moe_call

122|def check_identity(model):
123|    """The split MoE with reference slots equals the port's, at 1, 8, 32 rows."""
124|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
125|
126|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
127|    for split in (make_moe_call(), make_moe_call(experts=ref_experts)):
128|        for rows in (1, 8, 32):
129|            moe = model.model.layers[3].feed_forward
130|            x = mx.random.normal((1, rows, D)).astype(mx.bfloat16)
131|            if not mx.array_equal(original(moe, x), split(moe, x)).item():
132|                raise AssertionError(
133|                    f"split MoE differs from the port's at {rows} rows"
134|                )

137|def capture(model, rows, step=8, seed=None):
138|    """Every layer's slot inputs and reference outputs in one real decode step."""
139|    import sys
140|
141|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
142|    import breakdown as bd
143|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
144|    from mlx_lm.models.cache import make_prompt_cache
145|
146|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
147|    seen = []
148|
149|    def recording_routing(x, w_router, bias):
150|        inds, weights = ref_routing(x, w_router, bias)
151|        seen.append({"x": x, "w_router": w_router, "bias": bias, "inds": inds})
152|        return inds, weights
153|
154|    def recording_combine(y, weights, shared):
155|        seen[-1].update(y=y, weights_in=weights, shared=shared)
156|        return ref_combine(y, weights, shared)

158|    mx.random.seed(rows if seed is None else seed)
159|    ids = mx.random.randint(0, 100000, (rows, 128))
160|    cache = make_prompt_cache(model)
161|    y = bd.prefill(model, ids, cache)
162|    for _ in range(step - 1):
163|        y = bd.greedy(model(y, cache=cache))
164|        mx.eval(y)
165|    mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = make_moe_call(recording_routing, recording_combine)
166|    try:
167|        logits = model(y, cache=cache)
168|        mx.eval(logits, [list(s.values()) for s in seen])
169|    finally:
170|        mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = original
171|    return seen

179|            f"L{i:02d}_{k}": np.array(

182|            for i, layer in enumerate(layers)
183|            for k, v in layer.items()

190|    """The served checkpoint, with its weights in memory."""
191|    import sys
192|
193|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
194|    import breakdown as bd

214|def capture_prefill(model, requests, with_weights=None, tokens=None):
215|    """Every layer's slot inputs in the first chunk of a prefill, as load_inputs.
216|
217|    The same MoE.__call__ runs the prefill. With 128-token prompts and
218|    breakdown.py's 2,048-token chunks, 1, 8 and 32 requests give the slots
219|    127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows; from 60 rows MLX's own experts kernel changes
220|    (gather_qmm_rhs). The prompts are time_candidates.py's. *tokens* sets the
221|    chunk's length per request instead, for requests x tokens rows.
222|    """
223|    import sys
224|
225|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
226|    import breakdown as bd
227|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
228|    from mlx_lm.models.cache import make_prompt_cache
229|
230|    seen = []
231|
232|    def routing(x, w_router, bias):
233|        inds, weights = ref_routing(x, w_router, bias)
234|        seen.append({"x": x, "w_router": w_router, "bias": bias, "inds": inds})
235|        return inds, weights
236|
237|    def combine(y, weights, shared):
238|        seen[-1].update(y=y, weights=weights, shared=shared)
239|        return ref_combine(y, weights, shared)
240|
241|    mx.random.seed(requests)
242|    ids = mx.random.randint(0, 100000, (requests, max(128, (tokens or 0) + 1)))
243|    chunk = tokens or min(bd.PREFILL_TOKENS // requests, 127)
244|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
245|    mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = make_moe_call(routing, combine)
246|    try:
247|        model(ids[:, :chunk], cache=make_prompt_cache(model))
248|    finally:
249|        mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = original
250|    for i, layer in enumerate(seen):
251|        layer["inds"] = layer["inds"].astype(mx.uint32)
252|        if with_weights is not None:
253|            layer.update(with_weights[i])
254|    mx.eval(seen)
255|    return seen

258|def load_inputs(rows, with_weights=None):
259|    """[{name: mx.array}] per layer, with bfloat16 restored where the model had it.
260|
261|    *with_weights*, from load_expert_weights or model_expert_weights, adds each layer's expert weights.
262|    """
263|    data = np.load(INPUTS / f"rows{rows}.npz")
264|    bf16 = {"x", "y", "shared"}
265|    layers = {}
266|    for key in data.files:
267|        i, name = int(key[1:3]), key[4:]
268|        a = mx.array(data[key])
269|        layers.setdefault(i, {})[name] = a.astype(mx.bfloat16) if name in bf16 else a
270|    for i, layer in layers.items():
271|        layer["weights"] = layer.pop("weights_in")
272|        if "inds" in layer:
273|            layer["inds"] = layer["inds"].astype(mx.uint32)
274|        if with_weights is not None:
275|            layer.update(with_weights[i])
276|    return [layers[i] for i in sorted(layers)]

279|# Muse Spark's launch spec: integers, or products of integers and NAMES/rows.
280|TERM = re.compile(r"^(\d+|rows|D|E|K|H)$")
281|
282|
283|def dim(expr, rows):
284|    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
285|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
286|    if isinstance(expr, int):
287|        return expr
288|    value = 1
289|    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
290|        if not TERM.match(term):
291|            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
292|        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)
293|    return value
294|
295|
296|def template_value(v):
297|    if isinstance(v, bool) or isinstance(v, int):
298|        return v
299|    if isinstance(v, str) and v in DTYPES:
300|        return DTYPES[v]
301|    raise ValueError(f"bad template value {v!r}")
302|
303|
304|def build(spec, sources, slot):
305|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks.
306|
307|    With "max_rows" in the spec, inputs with more rows than that run the slot's
308|    reference under mx.compile instead of the kernels, so an attempt can keep
309|    prompt-sized inputs on MLX's own code (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
310|    """
311|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
312|    kernels = []
313|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
314|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
315|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
316|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
317|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
318|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
319|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
320|            header=header,
321|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
322|        )
323|        kernels.append((k, fn))
324|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
325|    if missing:
326|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
327|    max_rows = spec.get("max_rows")
328|    if max_rows is not None:
329|        if isinstance(max_rows, bool) or not isinstance(max_rows, int) or max_rows < 1:
330|            raise ValueError(f"bad max_rows {max_rows!r}")
331|        compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])
332|
333|    def run(**inputs):
334|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
335|        if max_rows is not None and rows > max_rows:  # the compiled reference takes over
336|            out = compiled(*[inputs[n] for n in slot_in])
337|            return dict(zip(slot_out, out if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out]))
338|        env = dict(inputs)
339|        for k, fn in kernels:
340|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
341|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
342|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
343|            outs = fn(
344|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
345|                template=[
346|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
347|                ],
348|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
349|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
350|                output_shapes=[
351|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
352|                ],
353|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
354|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
355|            )
356|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
357|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
358|
359|    return run
360|
361|
362|def main():
363|    import sys
364|
365|    if sys.argv[1:] != ["capture"]:
366|        raise SystemExit("usage: slots.py capture")
367|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))

374|    model, _ = load_model(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / bd.MODEL)

377|    print("split MoE with reference slots: bit-identical to the port's")
378|    save_inputs(model)

381|if __name__ == "__main__":
382|    main()

5|# From round 3, an improvement must hold in both phases, decode and prefill, and an attempt may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Claude's comparison of every engine version over whole requests ([findings](../findings/muse-round-2.md), section 5) found that the grader and G3 timed only the decode step. They never timed the prefill, the phase in which a request's whole prompt runs through the model:
10|- **Experts attempt-7** looked like round 2's largest gain, a 19% shorter decode step at 32 requests. It processed prompts 6.6 to 14.5 times slower and cut throughput by 10% to 83%.
11|- **Routing attempt-4,** round 2's only baseline, processed prompts 7% to 10% slower. At 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts it cost 3.5% of throughput.
12|
13|The Muse agent never saw either effect: its piece timing ran decode sizes only, and G3 measured the decode step only.
14|
15|On 2026-11-04 surucuonur set the rule: "The improvement should be in the two phases of it: decode and prefill. Then, we can consider it as an improvement." surucuonur chose:
16|- **faster in one phase, slower in neither;**
17|- **the hand-off:** an attempt may leave prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference. This replaces the part of [ADR 0010](0010-exact-at-every-size.md) that required the kernels to run in every call.
18|
19|## How it works
20|
21|- **The piece timing runs at the six G2 sizes** (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`): decode at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. The layers are still chained.
22|- **The verdict at each size comes from paired repeats.** The candidate and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times, and so does the baseline when one is given.
23|  - The candidate is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, a one-sided sign test at p < 0.01.
24|  - It is `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise.
25|
26|  This replaces the comparison of medians for the decode sizes too, since the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
27|- **The verdict per phase:**
28|  - a phase is `faster` when every one of its sizes is;
29|  - it is `slower` when any size is;
30|  - otherwise it is `not slower`.
31|
32|  `beats_compiled`, and `beats_baseline` against a baseline, are true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
33|- **The hand-off** (`max_rows` in `spec.json`, `bench/grader/slots.py`). Inputs with more rows than `max_rows` run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. G2 still checks every size.
34|  - On 2026-11-04 the compiled reference of each slot was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).
35|  - Above `max_rows` a hand-off runs the compiled reference itself, so it times `same` as the bar there, never better.
36|- **G3** (`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`, which writes `g3-vllm.json`):
37|  - **Workloads:** 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts.
38|  - **Measurements per run:** the decode step period, the prompt time and the whole-request time, over 5 shuffled repeats, up from 3.
39|  - **Faster and slower:** the two ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
40|  - **Why 5 repeats:** with 3 each, two identical engines' ranges miss each other by chance 1 time in 20 per direction. "Never slower" checks a phase 8 times (4 workloads, 2 bars), so a phase that changed nothing would fail about a third of the time. The first run under these rules showed it. A copy of experts attempt-7 with a hand-off at 59 rows came out `slower` on prompt time at 32 × 1,024, by 0.5% with ranges 16 ms apart, although above 59 rows it runs the compiled reference, whose own range overlapped the unchanged engine's (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`). With 5 repeats the chance is 1 in 252 per check, about 3% over 8.
41|  - **The pass rule:** against both the original model and the compiled reference, the decode step or the prompt time must be faster in every workload, neither may be slower in any, and no whole request may be slower.
42|- **The unchanged engine is vLLM's own.** The original model in G3 runs with Claude's step hooks, and with vLLM's engine inside the script's process. On 2026-11-04, alternating runs found it within −0.2% to +1.9% of vLLM with neither, inside the spread between repeats in every workload (`bench/micro/clean_vllm.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-clean-vllm/`).
43|
44|## Consequences
45|
46|- **Round 3 starts with no baseline.** Routing attempt-4 is `slower` at all three prefill sizes, 2.6 to 8.7 times the compiled reference's time. It fails G3 on prompt time at 8 and 32 requests. It becomes a starting point, so round 3's bar in every slot is the compiled reference.
47|- **A decode kernel no longer has to win at prefill sizes,** only to hand them off or not lose there. The attempt chooses the row count, so the boundary agent checks that the hand-off sits on the right side of 60 rows for the experts slot.
48|- **At prefill sizes, a slot with a hand-off is MLX's code, not the Muse agent's.** The claim for such an attempt is "faster decode, unchanged prefill".
49|- **Grader runs and G3 take longer.** Every attempt is now timed at three more sizes. G3 runs 5 repeats instead of 3, and its 32 × 1,024 workload adds at least 16 s per variant per repeat.
50|- **The decode verdict is stricter.** An attempt whose median beat the compiled reference by noise is now `same`.
51|- **Not covered:** prefill chunks of other sizes, and decode steps with other row counts. The boundary agent reports them; G3's four workloads are the end-to-end check. Not covered means not measured: from round 3 the swarm lists these as **Unverified**, never as free ([ADR 0013](0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)); round 2 read ADR 0010's line like this one as leave to slow the prefill.
52|- **At 1 request the whole-request time is noisy.** On 2026-11-04 its repeats spread 6% to 41%, so G3 there mostly says `same`, which passes the "never slower" test without showing a gain.
53|
54|## Considered options
55|
56|- **Faster in both phases.** The higher bar. A decode kernel would also have to beat MLX's large matrix kernels at 2,048 rows, which is not where the decode step loses its time. Not chosen.
57|- **Whole-request throughput alone.** Simple, but it lets a slower phase be traded for a faster one. surucuonur ruled that out.
58|- **Hand off to the uncompiled reference.** The prefill could then come out `slower` than the compiled reference wherever compiling helps; at 127 rows, routing's compiled reference takes 87 µs per layer against 102 µs uncompiled.
59|- **Keep the kernels in every call** (ADR 0010). The kernels could still branch on the row count inside themselves, but they couldn't use MLX's large-size kernels. surucuonur chose the hand-off.

11|Slot `routing`. One entry:

From `inds.size >= 64` (rows ≥ 16) it sorts pairs by expert internally and unscatters the result back, so its output `y[..., j, :]` always corresponds to `inds[..., j]` whatever per-row order the slot emits (brief:53: `y` is "in `inds` order"). 48|
49|- **Rounding points:** everything inside the slot is float32 — `x` cast bf16→f32 (exact), matmul + sigmoid in f32, gather of the *unbiased* scores, f32 sum/divide (epsilon 1e-20) and × 2.5 (`slots.py:44-48`, `mobilemoe.py:219-228`). 84|  own experts kernel at 60 rows (`bench/grader/slots.py:219-220`;

219|### attempt-1 — pass (boundary-2, 2026-11-04T17:59:14Z)
220|
221|G1+G2 pass (differ 0 all six sizes). Kernels verified byte-identical to
222|the starting point (`diff` of `block-0.metal` and `block-1.metal`
223|against `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7/`); `spec.json`

226|`max_rows` to the compiled reference (`slots.py:335`), so rows ≤ 59
227|run the kernels.
