229|- **Every decode step stays on the fused path.** A decode step has
230|  1–32 rows; 32 ≤ 59, so all of them run the kernels. Pass.
231|- **Hand-off sits below MLX's switch at 60.** Rows ≥ 60 hand off to
232|  the compiled reference; the kernels only ever see rows ≤ 59, where
233|  the reference uses `gather_qvm` — and the kernels' own dispatch
234|  (`block-0.metal:22`, `x_shape[0] >= 60`) takes the `qvm` path there
235|  too, so both sides agree at every kernel-visible count including
236|  the ungraded 33–59. The scalar `qmm_accum` prefill branch is dead
237|  code wherever the kernels run, kept as G2-exact fallback. Pass.
238|- **Row counts G2 doesn't test.** Kernel work is per-pair
239|  (one 512-thread group per pair, grid `rows*2048` threads total):
240|  no cross-row interaction, so the 1/8/32-row G2 verdict extends to
241|  every decode count up to 32 by construction; 33–59 take the same
242|  `qvm` path graded at 1/8/32. Prefill chunks of any size ≥ 60 run
243|  the compiled reference exactly. Speed at 33–59 rows stays
244|  unmeasured (grader times only 1/8/32 there) — noted, not a defect.
245|- **Unwritten threadgroup reads: none.** `tg_x[768]` is fully covered
246|  by the strided loop (`block-0.metal:29-31`); `tg_gate/tg_up[384]`
247|  are fully covered in both branches (12 simdgroups × 32 lanes write
248|  distinct `b*32+lane`, lines 51-58 / 61-71); `tg_h[384]` is fully
249|  covered by the strided silu loop (line 77). Every read follows its
250|  phase's barrier (lines 32, 73, 86).
251|- **Threadgroup memory far from the limit.** 3,840 B
252|  (`tg_x[768] + tg_gate/up/h[384]` bfloat16, `block-0.metal:24-27`)
253|  vs the 32 KB ceiling; 512 threads/group vs the 1,024 count and the
254|  inherited pipeline ceiling (two 32-float thread arrays `p`, `q`
255|  unchanged — lines 42-43 — so the attempt-6 G1 failure mode does
256|  not recur). Pass.
257|- **No thread-timing dependence.** All cross-thread sharing passes
258|  through `threadgroup_barrier`s; `y` slices are disjoint per pair
259|  and per (simdgroup, lane); no atomics; `simd_sum` reductions are
260|  fixed trees. The shared kernel-scope `q[32]` phases are separated
261|  by barriers with re-zeroing on entry (round-2 checked).
262|- **No new input assumptions.** The attempt adds no input-dependent
263|  logic beyond `rows > max_rows` on `x_shape[0]` — the same value the
264|  grader reads (`slots.py:334`) — and `inds` flows through untouched
265|  (`y[r,j]` stays positional in `inds` order).

1|# Territory: grader — what changed in round 3 (ADR 0011, ADR 0013)
2|
3|- **Owner:** explorer-grader
4|- **Status:** done
5|- **Version:** 2
6|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T17:39:20Z
7|- **Next:** none — checklist complete (6 pieces), 0 inefficiencies posted (grader runs no decode-step kernels); notes for baseline-*/g3 held in entry until their entries land; no notes to answer
8|
9|## What it does
10|
11|Rounds 1 and 2's entries ([`muse-spark/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../exploration/territory-grader.md) and [`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../round-2/exploration/territory-grader.md), frozen) mapped the grader through ADR 0010: bit-exact G2 at six sizes, chained piece timing at decode sizes only, median-vs-median `beats_compiled`, and the paired sign-test `--baseline` bar. Round 3 changes the judgment ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)): the piece timing runs at all six sizes with paired per-size verdicts, `beats_compiled` needs one phase faster and neither slower, and a spec may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference via `max_rows`. G3 moves to vLLM-only two-phase judgment (decode step, prompt time, whole-request time), and the lead's ready check ([`bench/grader/check_ready.py`](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py), [ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)) runs that same G3 inside the round. This entry writes only the delta. G1/G2 mechanics, the spec language, `capture`, and `gpu_lock` are cited to rounds 1–2, not re-described.
12|
13|## Checklist
14|
15|### 1. `check_candidate.py` — paired per-size verdicts and the two-phase judgment (check_candidate.py:51-58, 224-264, 345-378)
16|
17|- **Callers:** builders: `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt> <slot> [--out FILE]` ([check_candidate.py:15](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); no `--baseline` this round — no slot has one (round-3 README *Starting point*). Holds the GPU lock for the whole run ([check_candidate.py:294](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). One grader run is one attempt (ADR 0013); builders keep `grade.json` in the attempt folder.
18|- **Callees:** unchanged: `slots.build`/`load_inputs`/`capture_prefill`/`load_model`; `mx.eval` for correctness and timing; `mx.compile(ref)` for the compiled bar only.
19|- **Data:** `ROWS = (1, 8, 32)`, `PHASES = {"decode": "rows ", "prefill": "prefill rows "}` ([check_candidate.py:51-52](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); `REPEATS = 30`, `WINS_NEEDED = 22` computed by the same one-sided sign test at p < 0.01 as round 2 ([check_candidate.py:53-58](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).
20|- **What is new — paired timing at all six sizes:** timing runs only if G2 passes ([check_candidate.py:345](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), over the same six size inputs as correctness (decode `load_inputs` + prefill `capture_prefill`, [check_candidate.py:308-312,349](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per size and part, `paired_times` runs candidate and compiled (plus baseline when given) in rotating order within each of 30 repeats, each repeat a full chained 20-layer eval ([check_candidate.py:224-236](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per-part times are summed per repeat before wins are counted ([check_candidate.py:364-366](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), so for `routing+combine` the verdict is on summed time, as in round 2. The plain `reference` is still timed by unpaired median `timed()` ([check_candidate.py:360](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) — informational only, no verdict against it.
21|- **What is new — `compare`/`judge`:** per size, the candidate is `faster` with ≥22 wins, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same` ([check_candidate.py:239-245](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Per phase: `faster` iff every size is, `slower` iff any size is, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` (and `beats_baseline`, same rule) is true iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower` ([check_candidate.py:248-264,377-378](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Consequences: two `faster` + one `same` in a phase is `not slower`, not `faster` — a single noisy size now blocks the bar instead of passing it (round 2's median-only rule passed on noise up to 5%, [ADR 0011:26](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); a `same` everywhere attempt never beats.
22|- **Invariants:** verdict JSON gains per-size `wins_vs_compiled`/`vs_compiled` (and baseline twins) plus `phases_vs_compiled`/`beats_compiled` ([check_candidate.py:368-378](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:207). On G2 failure there is still no timing at all.
23|
24|### 2. `slots.py` `build` — the `max_rows` hand-off (slots.py:304-337)
25|
26|- **Callers:** `check_candidate.load` and `time_candidates.Variants`/`implementations`, via `slots.build(spec, sources, slot)` — so the hand-off applies identically in the piece timing, G2, G3 and the ready check.
27|- **What it does:** with `"max_rows"` in the spec (per part for `routing+combine`, brief:174), `run()` sends inputs with `rows > max_rows` to the slot's reference under `mx.compile` instead of the kernels ([slots.py:333-337](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). `rows` is read from the first slot input's `shape[0]` ([slots.py:334](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Validation: int ≥ 1, bools rejected ([slots.py:327-331](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); `compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])` is built once per `build` call.
28|- **Grading:** "bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes" (brief:173). G2 checks `run()`, so sizes above `max_rows` exercise the compiled reference through the attempt's own dispatch; the compiled reference of each slot was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes on 2026-11-04 (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`, [ADR 0011:34](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). Timing above `max_rows` runs the bar's own code, so it reads `same` by construction, never better ([ADR 0011:35](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)) — the claim for such an attempt is "faster decode, unchanged prefill" ([ADR 0011:48](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)).
29|- **The experts switch at 60 rows:** from 60 rows MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`) with different rounding ([slots.py:219-220](../../../bench/grader/slots.py); brief:187). Kernels running at rows ≥ 60 must match the large kernel's rounding; `max_rows` ≤ 59 keeps decode-built kernels on the `gather_qvm` side only. 24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.

180|## How each attempt is judged
181|
182|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
183|
184|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
185|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
186|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
187|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.

Its regime branches (`rows == 1` GEMV shuffle tree, `rows <= 768` split-K partitions from the `rows`-only formula, single accumulator above, `block-0.metal:35-74`), verbatim sigmoid (:134-135), strictly-greater top-4 (:142-159) and weights fold (:160-173) are therefore the decode behaviour to keep: decode rows stay on this winning staged scalar path, and every decode step up to 32 rows must stay at or below any `max_rows` the attempt names (see below).
+- **New: rows above `max_rows` run the compiled reference, not the kernels.** With `"max_rows"` in `spec.json` (int ≥ 1, bools rejected), `slots.build` sends inputs with `rows > max_rows` to the slot's reference under `mx.compile` (`bench/grader/slots.py:327-337`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:173`; `claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:33-35`). G2 checks `run()`, so sizes above `max_rows` exercise the compiled reference through the attempt's own dispatch; the compiled reference was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes on 2026-11-04 (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`). This replaces the ADR 0010 line that required the kernels to run in every call (`claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:17`).
+- **Decode stays on the candidate: `max_rows >= 32`.** A decode step has 1–32 rows (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:26`); every decode step up to 32 rows stays at or below the hand-off, running the staged scalar path that already wins there. Below the hand-off the kernels face only the GEMV (`rows == 1`) and split-K (1 < rows ≤ 768) roundings.
+- **No MLX switch at 60 rows for this slot — the window is 32 ≤ `max_rows` ≤ 126.** The 60-row kernel change (`gather_qmm_rhs` vs `gather_qvm`) is the *experts* slot's (`bench/grader/slots.py:219-220`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:187`); routing's reference regimes change at `rows = 1` and `rows = 768` only. So any `max_rows ≥ 32` keeps decode on the kernels and hands every graded prefill size (127/1,016/2,048) to compiled (grader note for this slot, `muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md:86`); `max_rows ≤ 126` hands all three graded prefill sizes off while `max_rows ≤ 768` additionally dead-ends the regular-GEMM branch wherever the kernels run. Kernel-visible counts 33–126 take the split-K path (partition counts from the same `rows`-only formula: 16×3 at 33–64, 8×6 at 65–128), already exercised in kind by the graded 8/32/127-row groupings. Above `max_rows` the attempt times `same` as the compiled bar by construction, never better — its claim is "faster decode, unchanged prefill" (`claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:35,48`).
+- **Consequence for the three fix shapes** (this entry, *Inefficiency*): (a) `max_rows` hand-off keeps the staged scalar decode path verbatim and deletes or dead-ends nothing it needs — the G2-exactness at kernel-visible counts is inherited, and the boundary check verifies the hand-off value, not the arithmetic; (b) GEMM-shaped sharing must reproduce the *same per-row regime orders* while sharing `w_router` across rows — sharing bytes is free, reordering any row's accumulation is a G2 failure; (c) a narrower staged footprint keeps the same orders with less staging. Every direction adds no fixed cost at decode sizes and keeps the tie rule and pair order bit-exact.
+
+### What the grader checks, and what it can't see (changed)
+
+- **G1/G2 (unchanged).** Same six sizes, same ordered `rows_differ == 0` rule in all 20 layers, same per-part isolation (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:308-344`); G1 is true only after the whole six-size correctness loop completes without exception (:342); shape/dtype faults fail G2 with G1 true (:324-326). Size labels now carry the phase prefix (`rows N` vs `prefill rows N`, :51-52,313-320).
+- **Piece timing (changed to two-phase paired).** Timing still runs only if G2 passes, but now at all six sizes with paired per-size verdicts (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:345-378`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:209-213`; `claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:21-32`; `muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md` §1): per size, candidate vs `mx.compile(ref_routing)` over 30 chained repeats in rotating order, `faster` with ≥22 wins, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same`; per phase, `faster` iff every size is, `slower` iff any size is, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`. Round 2's "candidate median beats compiled median at all three decode sizes" bar is retired. **Prefill speed is now timed** — round 2's can't-see "prefill speed" item is retired, and this hypothesis exists because the starting point is `slower` at every prefill size. A `max_rows` fix banks prefill `same` × 3 and wins the slot on decode `faster` × 3; a kernel fix must additionally be `same`-or-better at every prefill size. The slot stops at the first attempt passing G1+G2 and the two-phase bar, or after 5 attempts (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:217`; round 2 cited :201, moved).
+- **G3 and the ready check (new in-round).** G3 is now vLLM-only two-phase judgment — decode step, prompt time, whole-request time over 1×128/8×128/32×128/32×1024, 5 repeats, pass iff decode or prompt is `faster` and none of the three is `slower`, against both base and compiled (`bench/grader/time_candidates.py:163-201`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:195-202`; `claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:36-42`). The lead's ready check (`bench/grader/check_ready.py`, `claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md`) runs that same G3 inside the round with every candidate in one call, plus same-greedy-tokens; only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`, and Claude's post-round G3 stays the authority (`territory-grader.md` §§4–5). For this hypothesis the discriminating check is prompt time on the 8×128/32×128/32×1024 workloads, where the starting point fails G3.
+- **What it can't see** (checked by hand later — *check an attempt*; seeds this entry's **Unverified** list): row counts other than the six graded — ungraded decode 2–7 and 9–31 on the graded split-K path but either side of nothing (the GEMV/split-K boundary is at `rows = 1`); the `max_rows` band 33–126 where kernels run in real serving (vLLM chunked prefills) but no piece verdict exists, straddling the partition-count transitions at 33/65/129 (`territory-grader.md`, *can't see* 1–2); prefill chunks of other sizes on both sides of the split-K/regular boundary at `rows = 768` (`territory-baseline-routing.md` §3.1 regime table) and of the transitions at 129/257 — a kernel hard-coding the six sizes passes G2 and breaks this boundary; sizes above 2,048 (item 3); prefill beyond the first seeded-random chunk (item 4); hand-off exactness above `max_rows` at untested sizes (item 5); whole-request noise at 1 request (item 6); other prompts, later decode steps, layers' drift, unseen exact 4th/5th ties (no graded row is one), score magnitudes saturating the sigmoid differently; threadgroup memory still unchecked by `slots.build` (item 8, now `bench/grader/slots.py:341-342`); unwritten threadgroup reads and thread-timing dependence, which one equality run per layer cannot expose. New since round 2: `bench/grader/check_sizes.py` (25 sizes incl. 33/65/129/257/768/769) closes between-sizes exactness where the boundary agent runs it — boundary tooling, not a gate (`territory-grader.md` §3; the 59/60/61 probes are the experts slot's switch, not routing's). Boundary checks will probe exactly these.
+
+### The GPU limits (unchanged)
+
+At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:100`); `grid` counts threads (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:178`); Apple M1 Pro, 16 cores, SIMD width 32, `bfloat` in Metal (brief:101). Starting point for scale: 256 threads/threadgroup, `(816 + 60 + 2,048 + 4,096) × 4 B = 28,080 B` — 85.7% of the limit, the closest of any routing attempt, leaving 4,688 B (`block-0.metal:15-25`); flat 69→73 µs from 8 to 32 rows confirms the footprint does not bind residency at decode sizes, but any fix that stages more (wider groups, cross-row tiles) must re-derive this sum before it can be trusted. Enforcement gap stands: `slots.build` checks only the 1,024-thread product (`bench/grader/slots.py:341-342`); Metal rejects oversize kernels as opaque G1 exceptions.

13|## What happens
14|
15|At 1 row the slot kernel (`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7/block-0.metal`,
16|`!prefill` path) launches 4 threadgroups of 512 threads —

18|`tg_x` load + barrier (`:29-32`); gate/up interleaved, 24
19|strided steps (`K=768`) over 12 of 16 simdgroups
20|(`:51-58`); barrier (`:73`); full-bfloat16 silu-mul, 384

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write faster MobileMoE-S kernels, for decoding and prompt processing
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|A request goes through two phases: **prompt processing** (the prefill), which runs its whole prompt through the model, and **decoding**, one step per generated token. An improvement must hold in both: faster in one, and no slower in the other ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A kernel that speeds up the decode step but slows the prefill is not an improvement.
12|
13|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
14|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
15|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
16|
17|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
18|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
19|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
20|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
21|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
22|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
23|
24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

96|## Tools and limits
97|
98|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.

100|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes, longer for an attempt much slower than the reference at the prefill sizes; stop one that runs past 15.
101|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.

From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
183|
184|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
185|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
186|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
187|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
188|
189|   At every size:
190|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
191|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
192|
193|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
194|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
195|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
196|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
197|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
198|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
199|
200|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
201|
202|   **From round 3, the same G3 runs inside the round too:** the lead's **ready check**, `bench/grader/check_ready.py`, with every candidate in one call. It also requires the same greedy tokens, and audits its own log. Only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's G3 after the round decides. The skill says when the lead runs it ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)).
203|
204|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
205|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
206|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
207|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same` or `slower`); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
208|
209|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
210|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
211|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
212|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size is, `slower` when any size is, and `not slower` otherwise.
213|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
214|
215|It is a guide; the ready check in the round, and Claude's G3 after it, decide.
216|
217|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and has `beats_compiled` true, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

# attempt-1 (round 3): max_rows hand-off on round-2 attempt-7 (builder-2-a)

Hypothesis `hyp-2-experts-prefill` (slot `experts`, baseline `none`),
direction (a): the `max_rows` hand-off. Starting point
`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7` (fused decode path +
G2-exact scalar prefill branch; G1+G2 pass, `slower` at 1 row and at
every prefill size).

## The one main change

`block-0.metal` and `block-1.metal` are byte copies of the starting
point's (verify: `diff` against
`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7/`). `spec.json` is the
starting point's plus one key: `"max_rows": 59`.

Rows 1–59 run the candidate kernels; rows above 59 run the slot's
reference under `mx.compile` through the attempt's own dispatch
(`bench/grader/slots.py:327-337`). The fused decode path, the
`x_shape[0] >= 60` dispatch threshold (`block-0.metal:22`), the scalar
`qmm_accum` prefill branch, grids, and all four bfloat16 rounding
points are untouched — the scalar branch is now dead code at every
graded size (it can only trigger at rows ≥ 60, which all hand off),
kept as fallback so the kernels stay valid if `max_rows` is ever
raised.

## Which inefficiency it removes, and how

`ineff-baseline-experts-1` (confirmed): the `rows >= 60` scalar
`qmm_accum` branch runs 15.8/27.7/20.1× slower than compiled
(15,220/119,154/240,681 vs 961/4,306/11,999 µs/layer) — ~29.5
µs/pair serial issue at 18.8 GB/s. This attempt removes the whole
branch from the graded path: every prefill size (127/1,016/2,048
rows) runs the compiled reference, so prefill times `same` as
compiled by construction. Decode is untouched, so the 8/32-row wins
(ahead 72.7/282.5 µs/layer per the hypothesis entry) are kept.

## max_rows: 59, and why

The boundary's hand-off window is 32 ≤ `max_rows` ≤ 59:
decode steps run 1–32 rows and must stay on the fused path
(`max_rows >= 32`), while MLX switches its own experts kernel at 60
rows (`gather_qvm` below, `gather_qmm_rhs` at/above), so `qvm`-only
kernels must never see rows ≥ 60 (`max_rows <= 59`). This attempt's
kernels replicate both arithmetics (the scalar branch is G2-exact),
but decode rows 33–59 take the `qvm` decode path in both the kernels
(`block-0.metal:22`) and the reference, so keeping them on the
candidate is exact and keeps the fast path where it wins. 59 is the
top of the window: every decode-size input (≤ 32, plus 33–59) stays
on the candidate, every prefill-size input hands off. Round 2's
checked hand-off copy also used 59
(`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`), and the compiled
reference was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes there.

## Predicted µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 / 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows (chained)

Baseline `none`: predictions are against the starting point's
measured times and the compiled bar from its run.

- **Decode 1/8/32: 93.8 / 160.1 / 510.1.** Identical kernels,
  identical grids, identical dispatch at rows ≤ 32 — the chained
  time should reproduce attempt-7's 93.8 / 160.1 / 510.1 vs
  compiled 74.8 / 236.5 / 792.7 (attempt-7 `notes.md`, Verdict),
  modulo run-to-run noise (compiled shifted 75.9 → 74.8 at 1 row
  between attempt-5/7 runs). Verdicts: `slower` at 1 row, `faster`
  at 8 and 32.
- **Prefill 127/1,016/2,048: 961 / 4,306 / 11,999 (= compiled).**
  The hand-off runs literally the compiled reference, so each
  prefill size times `same` as the compiled bar measured in the
  same run; the numbers are attempt-7's run (hypothesis entry,
  *Inefficiency*). Saving vs the starting point: 14,259 / 114,848
  / 228,682 µs/layer = 285 ms / 2.30 s / 4.57 s per chunk
  (hypothesis entry arithmetic).
- **G1: pass** — the launch is attempt-7's (512 threads, 3,840 B
  threadgroup memory); `max_rows` adds no kernel.
- **G2: pass, differ 0 at all six sizes** — rows ≤ 59 run
  attempt-7's G2-exact kernels; rows above run the compiled
  reference, bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes on
  2026-11-04 (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).
- **`beats_compiled`: false** — prefill `same` at all three sizes
  by construction, decode `faster` at 8/32 but `slower` at 1 row;
  the bar needs one phase `faster` at every size with neither
  `slower` anywhere. The claim is "faster decode, unchanged
  prefill" (ADR 0011): this attempt banks the prefill prize
  (removes `slower` at all three prefill sizes) and leaves the
  1-row decode gap to hyp-4.

## What this attempt leaves unmeasured

- Kernel speed at 33–59 rows (runs the candidate's `qvm` decode
  path in real serving; the grader times only 1/8/32 there).
- Sizes above 2,048 rows; prefill beyond the first chunk of seeded
  128-token prompts; other lengths/distributions; mixed batches.
- The boundary's full *can't see* list (unwritten threadgroup
  reads, thread-timing dependence, 32 KB limit by hand — 3,840 B,
  unchanged — NaN-vs-NaN equality, 1-request G3 noise).

## Verdict

G1 pass; **G2 pass at all six sizes, differ 0 / max_ulp 0.0
everywhere** — no first difference. Chained timing µs/layer
(`grade.json`; candidate vs reference vs compiled):
**1 row 96.9 / 82.2 / 86.6 (`slower`, 5 wins)**; 8 rows 168.9 /
245.0 / 238.2 (`faster`, 29 wins); 32 rows 554.7 / 812.4 / 883.4
(`faster`, 29 wins); prefill 127: 1053.5 / 1007.7 / 1131.1
(`same`, 19 wins); prefill 1,016: 4106.9 / 4140.7 / 4133.5
(`same`, 15 wins); prefill 2,048: 7557.0 / 7668.8 / 7557.8
(`same`, 16 wins). `phases_vs_compiled`: decode `slower`,
prefill `not slower`. **`beats_compiled` false** — only the 1-row
decode size misses. Baseline `none`, so no `beats_baseline`.

The prefill prize is banked: `slower` at all three prefill sizes
(starting point: 15,220/119,154/240,681 µs/layer) is now `same`
(1,053.5/4,106.9/7,557.0), saving ≈ 14,167/115,047/233,124
µs/layer ≈ 283 ms / 2.30 s / 4.66 s per chunk against the starting
point's run. Decode keeps the 8/32-row wins (ahead 69.3/328.7
µs/layer of compiled this run).

## Miss analysis (prediction 93.8 / 160.1 / 510.1 decode, = compiled prefill)

Decode misses are +3.3% / +5.5% / +8.7% — all inside the 20% bar.
The whole shift is run-to-run machine noise, not the change: this
attempt's kernels are byte-identical to attempt-7's at rows ≤ 32,
and the compiled bar itself moved between runs (74.8 → 86.6 at 1
row, 236.5 → 238.2 at 8, 792.7 → 883.4 at 32). Prefill matched
the prediction exactly in kind (`same` at all three sizes); the
127-row candidate mean (1,053.5) sitting below the compiled mean
(1,131.1, 19 wins) is the same noise — both sides run literally
the same compiled code, and 19 wins is well short of the 22-win
`faster` bar.

Lesson for `ineff-baseline-experts-1`: the hand-off removes the
confirmed prefill cause in full at zero decode cost (decode
verdicts identical to the starting point's: slower/faster/faster).
What remains in this slot is the disjoint 1-row decode gap
(`ineff-baseline-experts-2`, hyp-4).

## Next change

Do not touch prefill — `same` is the ceiling by construction.
Build hyp-4 on this attempt: attack the 1-row decode remainder
(`tg_x` load + silu + barrier chain, chained fixed cost) while
keeping `max_rows: 59` and every accumulation order.

Designing a thresholded kernel split with early-exit and a select copy to isolate the unfused path for small rows.

Evaluating per-block group sizing and early-exit thresholds to match the compiled kernel launch counts.

Comparing per-group reload costs against fused kernel overhead and selecting the kernel launch layout.

Evaluating a two-kernel layout with staged threadgroup memory and identical per-output accumulation to preserve bit-exactness.

Refining the threadgroup tiling to reduce per-thread register pressure and validating early-exit grid costs.

2|

4|named inputs and outputs (claude/muse-agent-brief.md), and a way to install
5|an implementation into MoE.__call__ for every layer. build() turns a launch
6|spec (data, never code) into mx.fast.metal_kernel calls.

11|"""

16|import mlx.core as mx
17|import numpy as np
18|

20|SCALE = 2.5  # routed_scaling_factor; norm_topk_prob is true
21|NAMES = {"D": D, "E": E, "K": K, "H": H}
22|DTYPES = {
23|    "float32": mx.float32,
24|    "bfloat16": mx.bfloat16,
25|    "float16": mx.float16,
26|    "uint32": mx.uint32,
27|    "int32": mx.int32,
28|}
29|SLOTS = {
30|    "routing": (["x", "w_router", "bias"], ["inds", "weights"]),
31|    "combine": (["y", "weights", "shared"], ["out"]),
32|}
33|EXPERT_WEIGHTS = [
34|    f"{p}_{t}" for p in ("gate", "up", "down") for t in ("w", "scales", "biases")
35|]
36|SLOTS["experts"] = (["x", "inds"] + EXPERT_WEIGHTS, ["y"])
37|SLOTS["routing+combine"] = (
38|    SLOTS["routing"][0] + ["y", "shared"],
39|    ["inds", "weights", "out"],
40|)

44|def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
45|    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
46|    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
47|    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
48|    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE
49|
50|
51|def ref_combine(y, weights, shared):
52|    return (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
53|
54|
55|def ref_experts(x, inds, *weights):
56|    """The port's SwitchGLU on flat rows: [rows, D] and [rows, K] -> [rows, K, D]."""
57|    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
58|    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort
59|
60|    gate, up, down = weights[0:3], weights[3:6], weights[6:9]
61|    xx = mx.expand_dims(x, (-2, -3))
62|    do_sort = inds.size >= 64
63|    idx, inv = inds, None
64|    if do_sort:
65|        xx, idx, inv = _gather_sort(xx, inds)
66|
67|    def qmm(a, w):
68|        return mx.gather_qmm(
69|            a,
70|            *w,
71|            rhs_indices=idx,
72|            transpose=False,
73|            group_size=32,
74|            bits=4,
75|            mode="affine",
76|            sorted_indices=do_sort,
77|        )
78|
79|    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
80|    if do_sort:
81|        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)
82|    return y.squeeze(-2)
83|

85|REFERENCE = {"routing": ref_routing, "combine": ref_combine, "experts": ref_experts}

89|    """A layer's SwitchGLU weights, named as in the experts slot."""
90|    return {
91|        f"{p}_{t}": getattr(experts, f"{p}_proj")[k]
92|        for p in ("gate", "up", "down")

97|def make_moe_call(routing=ref_routing, combine=ref_combine, experts=None):
98|    """MoE.__call__ with its slots swapped for *routing*, *combine*, *experts*.

100|    With the references it gives the port's outputs bit for bit (checked by

105|    def moe_call(self, x):
106|        lead = x.shape[:-1]
107|        flat = x.reshape(-1, D)
108|        bias = self.expert_bias.astype(mx.float32)
109|        inds, weights = routing(flat, self.router.weight, bias)

116|        out = combine(y.reshape(-1, K, D), weights, shared.reshape(-1, D))

215|    """Every layer's slot inputs in the first chunk of a prefill, as load_inputs.

226|    import breakdown as bd
227|    from mlx_lm.models import mobilemoe
228|    from mlx_lm.models.cache import make_prompt_cache
229|
230|    seen = []
231|
232|    def routing(x, w_router, bias):
233|        inds, weights = ref_routing(x, w_router, bias)
234|        seen.append({"x": x, "w_router": w_router, "bias": bias, "inds": inds})
235|        return inds, weights
236|
237|    def combine(y, weights, shared):
238|        seen[-1].update(y=y, weights=weights, shared=shared)
239|        return ref_combine(y, weights, shared)
240|
241|    mx.random.seed(requests)
242|    ids = mx.random.randint(0, 100000, (requests, max(128, (tokens or 0) + 1)))
243|    chunk = tokens or min(bd.PREFILL_TOKENS // requests, 127)
244|    original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
245|    mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = make_moe_call(routing, combine)
246|    try:
247|        model(ids[:, :chunk], cache=make_prompt_cache(model))
248|    finally:
249|        mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = original
250|    for i, layer in enumerate(seen):
251|        layer["inds"] = layer["inds"].astype(mx.uint32)
252|        if with_weights is not None:
253|            layer.update(with_weights[i])
254|    mx.eval(seen)
255|    return seen
256|
257|
258|def load_inputs(rows, with_weights=None):
259|    """[{name: mx.array}] per layer, with bfloat16 restored where the model had it.
260|
261|    *with_weights*, from load_expert_weights or model_expert_weights, adds each layer's expert weights.
262|    """
263|    data = np.load(INPUTS / f"rows{rows}.npz")
264|    bf16 = {"x", "y", "shared"}
265|    layers = {}
266|    for key in data.files:
267|        i, name = int(key[1:3]), key[4:]
268|        a = mx.array(data[key])
269|        layers.setdefault(i, {})[name] = a.astype(mx.bfloat16) if name in bf16 else a
270|    for i, layer in layers.items():
271|        layer["weights"] = layer.pop("weights_in")
272|        if "inds" in layer:
273|            layer["inds"] = layer["inds"].astype(mx.uint32)
274|        if with_weights is not None:
275|            layer.update(with_weights[i])
276|    return [layers[i] for i in sorted(layers)]
277|
278|
279|# Muse Spark's launch spec: integers, or products of integers and NAMES/rows.
280|TERM = re.compile(r"^(\d+|rows|D|E|K|H)$")
281|
282|
283|def dim(expr, rows):
284|    if isinstance(expr, bool) or not isinstance(expr, (int, str)):
285|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")
286|    if isinstance(expr, int):
287|        return expr
288|    value = 1
289|    for term in expr.replace(" ", "").split("*"):
290|        if not TERM.match(term):
291|            raise ValueError(f"bad size term {term!r} in {expr!r}")
292|        value *= rows if term == "rows" else NAMES.get(term) or int(term)
293|    return value
294|
295|
296|def template_value(v):
297|    if isinstance(v, bool) or isinstance(v, int):
298|        return v
299|    if isinstance(v, str) and v in DTYPES:
300|        return DTYPES[v]
301|    raise ValueError(f"bad template value {v!r}")
302|
303|
304|def build(spec, sources, slot):
305|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks.
306|
307|    With "max_rows" in the spec, inputs with more rows than that run the slot's
308|    reference under mx.compile instead of the kernels, so an attempt can keep
309|    prompt-sized inputs on MLX's own code (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
310|    """
311|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
312|    kernels = []
313|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
314|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
315|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
316|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
317|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
318|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
319|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
320|            header=header,
321|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
322|        )
323|        kernels.append((k, fn))
324|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
325|    if missing:
326|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
327|    max_rows = spec.get("max_rows")
328|    if max_rows is not None:
329|        if isinstance(max_rows, bool) or not isinstance(max_rows, int) or max_rows < 1:
330|            raise ValueError(f"bad max_rows {max_rows!r}")
331|        compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])
332|
333|    def run(**inputs):
334|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
335|        if max_rows is not None and rows > max_rows:  # the compiled reference takes over
336|            out = compiled(*[inputs[n] for n in slot_in])
337|            return dict(zip(slot_out, out if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out]))
338|        env = dict(inputs)
339|        for k, fn in kernels:
340|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
341|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
342|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
343|            outs = fn(
344|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
345|                template=[
346|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
347|                ],
348|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
349|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
350|                output_shapes=[
351|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
352|                ],
353|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
354|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
355|            )
356|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
357|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
358|
359|    return run
360|
361|
362|def main():
363|    import sys
364|
365|    if sys.argv[1:] != ["capture"]:
366|        raise SystemExit("usage: slots.py capture")
367|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "micro"))
368|    import breakdown as bd

374|    model, _ = load_model(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / bd.MODEL)
375|    mx.eval(model.parameters())
376|    check_identity(model)
377|    print("split MoE with reference slots: bit-identical to the port's")
378|    save_inputs(model)

382|    main()

{"content":"# attempt-5 (round 3): reference-shaped unfused 1-row path on attempt-1 (builder-2-e)

Hypothesis `hyp-2-experts-prefill` (slot `experts`, baseline `none`),
direction (e): fix the 1-row decode gap with a reference-shaped unfused
structure for small row counts. Builds on attempt-1 (the round's best:
fused decode path + `max_rows: 59`; prefill `same` x3, decode wins at
8/32 rows, loses only at 1 row).

## The one main change

At exactly 1 row, run two short unfused kernels (gate/up+silu, then
down) with per-block threadgroups instead of the fused kernel; every
other row count keeps attempt-1's fused path byte-for-byte. Four
kernels, `max_rows: 59` kept:

- K0 `gate_up_small` (`block-0.metal`): fixed grid of 48 groups x 128
  threads, one group per (pair, 32-output block). Loads the x row to
  threadgroup memory, computes 8 gate + 8 up outputs per simdgroup with
  qvm_block's exact per-output arithmetic, rounds to bfloat16, runs the
  fused kernel's exact silu-mul op sequence, stores `h_small`. Returns
  immediately unless `x_shape[0] == 1`.
- K1 `down_small` (`block-1.metal`): fixed grid of 96 groups x 128
  threads, one group per (pair, 32-output block). Loads the h row from
  `h_small`, computes 8 down outputs per simdgroup with qvm_block's
  exact per-output arithmetic over K=384, stores `y_small`. Returns
  immediately unless `inds_shape[0] == 1`.
- K2 `fused_experts_branch` (`block-2.metal`, header `block-3.metal`
  byte-identical to attempt-1's `block-1.metal`): attempt-1's
  `block-0.metal` plus a uniform early `return` at `x_shape[0] == 1`
  and its three `y[` stores renamed to `y_fused[`; all accumulation
  orders, silu, prefill branch and rounding points untouched.
- K3 `select_small` (`block-4.metal`): exact copy of `y_small`
  (rows == 1) or `y_fused` (else) to `y`, one thread per element.

## Which inefficiency it removes, and how

`ineff-baseline-experts-2` (confirmed): at 1 row the fused kernel runs
4 threadgroups x 512 threads through a barrier-serialized chain (tg_x
load, 24 merged gate/up K steps, silu, 12 merged down K steps, three
barriers) at the register ceiling — 92.1 vs 78.6 chained, +13.5
(+17.2%). Round 2's evidence says the next lever is not another fused
packing (six packings plateaued at 92-110) but a reference-shaped
unfused structure: the compiled reference runs 7 short kernels with
24/24/48 threadgroups per product and no cross-phase barriers.

This attempt is that structure, scoped to the one failing size: K0/K1
split the chain into two short kernels with 48/96 groups (vs 4),
each thread carrying 16/8 accumulators (vs 64) and one in-kernel
barrier (vs three), with silu fused elementwise into K0 (no barrier
needed — it is per-element on bfloat16 values). Cross-phase latency
hides across dozens of groups instead of serializing behind 4. Every
per-block accumulation order is kept: each output accumulates
k = lane, lane+32, ... serially with the same x*(s*q+bias) terms and
the same simd_sum tree as the fused kernel's helpers (the 8 outputs
of simdgroup s are exactly fused inner indices i = 4s..4s+3, one
shared weight word per k step), and the silu sequence is the fused
kernel's op-for-op on the same bfloat16 values.

## max_rows: 59, and why

Unchanged from attempt-1: top of the boundary's 32-59 window, every
decode-size input stays on the candidate, every prefill-size input
hands to the compiled reference (`same` by construction). The unfused
path only runs at rows == 1, where both the kernels and the reference
use `gather_qvm` arithmetic.

## Predicted us per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 / 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows (chained)

Basis: attempt-1's `grade.json` (96.9 / 168.9 / 554.7 decode vs
compiled 86.6 / 238.2 / 883.4; prefill `same` x3).

- **1 row: 68 (`faster`).** The ineff entry decomposes fused 92.1 as
  ~20 structural + ~60 exposed K-chain + ~11 byte floor. K0+K1 move
  ~2.5 MB (same weights as fused plus h_small traffic) with ~1/4 the
  per-thread serial depth and no cross-phase barriers; two short
  kernels should land near the reference's rate for the same bytes,
  ~60 for K0+K1 plus ~5 for K2's empty launch and ~3 for K3's 6 KB
  copy. Needs 22/30 pair wins vs ~87; the margin is thin and this is
  the attempt's whole bet.
- **8 rows: 176 (`faster`).** Fused path 168.9 plus two fixed-grid
  empty launches (48+96 groups exiting) and K3's 49 KB copy, ~7
  total; the win margin is 69.3.
- **32 rows: 562 (`faster`).** Fused path 554.7 plus the same fixed
  empty launches and K3's 196 KB copy, ~7 total; the margin is 328.7.
- **Prefill 127/1,016/2,048: = compiled (`same` x3).** Hand-off
  untouched; the kernels never run there.
- **G1: pass** — K0/K1/K3 are tiny kernels (16/8/0 thread floats,

  footprint at 512 threads.

## Miss analysis (prediction 68 / 176 / 562 decode, = compiled prefill)

The 1-row prediction missed by +245% (68 -> 234.3); 8/32-row and
prefill matched in verdict (`faster`/`faster`/`same` x3), with 8-row
absolute 252.7 vs predicted 176. Part of every absolute is machine
state, not the change: this run's compiled bar moved 86.6 -> 118.4
at 1 row (1.37x) and 238.2 -> 291.7 at 8 rows (1.22x), and the
reference moved 82.2 -> 154.3 at 1 row (1.88x); at 32 rows the
machine agreed (802.4 vs 883.4) and the candidate matched
attempt-1's absolute (560.4 vs 554.7), bounding the 32-row empty
launches + K3 copy overhead near zero. The real signal is the
within-run ratio at 1 row: 1.98x compiled (0/30 wins) where the
fused path scores 1.12x — the unfused structure is genuinely ~1.8x
worse than fused against the same bar, far beyond noise.

Why, from `grade.json` structure plus static counts (no other GPU
evidence is allowed, so this is analysis, not measurement):

1. **Dispatch count explains ~1/6 of the +116 us gap.** Within this
   run, the uncompiled reference (~7 dispatches) costs 154.3 vs the
   compiled reference (1 dispatch) 118.4: ~36 us for ~6 extra
   dispatches, ~6 us/dispatch. This attempt runs 4 kernels + link =
   5 dispatches per layer vs fused 2, ~+18 us. The remaining ~98 us
   is K0/K1 work slower than the fused chain.
2. **Per-group setup x144 vs amortized x4 (prime suspect for the
   rest).** The fused kernel pays one tg_x load + barriers per pair
   amortized over the full 36-step chain. K0/K1 pay a tg load +
   barrier per block per phase: 48 x (tg_x load + barrier) for 24
   short steps, 96 x (tg_h load + barrier) for 12 — each group does
   little work (24x16 / 12x8 MACs per thread), so scheduling,
   pipeline fill and setup dominate; plus the h_small device
   round-trip and K3's copy.
3. **The reference's speed comes from one dispatch, not just its
   shape.** The compiled reference's 7 short kernels run as ONE
   mx.compile dispatch; regrouping the candidate into 4 separate
   metal_kernel launches pays per-dispatch and per-group setup that
   exceeds the chain-latency saving. Reference-shaped is not
   reference-priced outside mx.compile.

Lesson for `ineff-baseline-experts-2`: the 1-row gap now survives
both fused packings (round-2 plateau 92-110) and unfused regrouping
(+100 us dispatch/setup). Note appended to the ineff entry.

## Next change

Do not build on attempt-5. The evidence now bounds both sides: one
dispatch plateaus at 92-110 (six fused packings), several dispatches
pay ~+100 us in dispatch + per-group setup. No further kernel
structure is indicated on this line — bank attempt-1 for hyp-2 (its
claim is "faster decode, unchanged prefill" modulo the 1-row gap)
and let hyp-4 decide whether any micro-lever inside one dispatch
(vectorized tg_x loads, barrier placement) is worth an attempt; my
read is the gap is structural and should be accepted."}

33|- **New: rows above `max_rows` run the compiled reference, not the kernels.** With `"max_rows"` in `spec.json` (int ≥ 1, bools rejected), `slots.build` sends inputs with `rows > max_rows` to the slot's reference under `mx.compile` (`bench/grader/slots.py:327-337`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:173`; `claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:33-35`). G2 checks `run()`, so sizes above `max_rows` exercise the compiled reference through the attempt's own dispatch; the compiled reference was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes on 2026-11-04 (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`). This replaces the ADR 0010 line that required the kernels to run in every call (`claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:17`).
34|- **Decode stays on the candidate: `max_rows >= 32`.** A decode step has 1–32 rows (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:26`); every decode step up to 32 rows stays at or below the hand-off, running the staged scalar path that already wins there. Below the hand-off the kernels face only the GEMV (`rows == 1`) and split-K (1 < rows ≤ 768) roundings.
35|- **No MLX switch at 60 rows for this slot — the window is 32 ≤ `max_rows` ≤ 126.** The 60-row kernel change (`gather_qmm_rhs` vs `gather_qvm`) is the *experts* slot's (`bench/grader/slots.py:219-220`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:187`); routing's reference regimes change at `rows = 1` and `rows = 768` only. So any `max_rows ≥ 32` keeps decode on the kernels and hands every graded prefill size (127/1,016/2,048) to compiled (grader note for this slot, `muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md:86`); `max_rows ≤ 126` hands all three graded prefill sizes off while `max_rows ≤ 768` additionally dead-ends the regular-GEMM branch wherever the kernels run. Kernel-visible counts 33–126 take the split-K path (partition counts from the same `rows`-only formula: 16×3 at 33–64, 8×6 at 65–128), already exercised in kind by the graded 8/32/127-row groupings. Above `max_rows` the attempt times `same` as the compiled bar by construction, never better — its claim is "faster decode, unchanged prefill" (`claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:35,48`).
36|- **Consequence for the three fix shapes** (this entry, *Inefficiency*): (a) `max_rows` hand-off keeps the staged scalar decode path verbatim and deletes or dead-ends nothing it needs — the G2-exactness at kernel-visible counts is inherited, and the boundary check verifies the hand-off value, not the arithmetic; (b) GEMM-shaped sharing must reproduce the *same per-row regime orders* while sharing `w_router` across rows — sharing bytes is free, reordering any row's accumulation is a G2 failure; (c) a narrower staged footprint keeps the same orders with less staging. Every direction adds no fixed cost at decode sizes and keeps the tie rule and pair order bit-exact.
37|
38|### What the grader checks, and what it can't see (changed)
39|
40|- **G1/G2 (unchanged).** Same six sizes, same ordered `rows_differ == 0` rule in all 20 layers, same per-part isolation (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:308-344`); G1 is true only after the whole six-size correctness loop completes without exception (:342); shape/dtype faults fail G2 with G1 true (:324-326). Size labels now carry the phase prefix (`rows N` vs `prefill rows N`, :51-52,313-320).
41|- **Piece timing (changed to two-phase paired).** Timing still runs only if G2 passes, but now at all six sizes with paired per-size verdicts (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:345-378`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:209-213`; `claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:21-32`; `muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md` §1): per size, candidate vs `mx.compile(ref_routing)` over 30 chained repeats in rotating order, `faster` with ≥22 wins, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same`; per phase, `faster` iff every size is, `slower` iff any size is, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`. Round 2's "candidate median beats compiled median at all three decode sizes" bar is retired. **Prefill speed is now timed** — round 2's can't-see "prefill speed" item is retired, and this hypothesis exists because the starting point is `slower` at every prefill size. A `max_rows` fix banks prefill `same` × 3 and wins the slot on decode `faster` × 3; a kernel fix must additionally be `same`-or-better at every prefill size. The slot stops at the first attempt passing G1+G2 and the two-phase bar, or after 5 attempts (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:217`; round 2 cited :201, moved).
42|- **G3 and the ready check (new in-round).** G3 is now vLLM-only two-phase judgment — decode step, prompt time, whole-request time over 1×128/8×128/32×128/32×1024, 5 repeats, pass iff decode or prompt is `faster` and none of the three is `slower`, against both base and compiled (`bench/grader/time_candidates.py:163-201`; `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:195-202`; `claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:36-42`). The lead's ready check (`bench/grader/check_ready.py`, `claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md`) runs that same G3 inside the round with every candidate in one call, plus same-greedy-tokens; only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`, and Claude's post-round G3 stays the authority (`territory-grader.md` §§4–5). For this hypothesis the discriminating check is prompt time on the 8×128/32×128/32×1024 workloads, where the starting point fails G3.
43|- **What it can't see** (checked by hand later — *check an attempt*; seeds this entry's **Unverified** list): row counts other than the six graded — ungraded decode 2–7 and 9–31 on the graded split-K path but either side of nothing (the GEMV/split-K boundary is at `rows = 1`); the `max_rows` band 33–126 where kernels run in real serving (vLLM chunked prefills) but no piece verdict exists, straddling the partition-count transitions at 33/65/129 (`territory-grader.md`, *can't see* 1–2); prefill chunks of other sizes on both sides of the split-K/regular boundary at `rows = 768` (`territory-baseline-routing.md` §3.1 regime table) and of the transitions at 129/257 — a kernel hard-coding the six sizes passes G2 and breaks this boundary; sizes above 2,048 (item 3); prefill beyond the first seeded-random chunk (item 4); hand-off exactness above `max_rows` at untested sizes (item 5); whole-request noise at 1 request (item 6); other prompts, later decode steps, layers' drift, unseen exact 4th/5th ties (no graded row is one), score magnitudes saturating the sigmoid differently; threadgroup memory still unchecked by `slots.build` (item 8, now `bench/grader/slots.py:341-342`); unwritten threadgroup reads and thread-timing dependence, which one equality run per layer cannot expose. New since round 2: `bench/grader/check_sizes.py` (25 sizes incl. 33/65/129/257/768/769) closes between-sizes exactness where the boundary agent runs it — boundary tooling, not a gate (`territory-grader.md` §3; the 59/60/61 probes are the experts slot's switch, not routing's). Boundary checks will probe exactly these.

46|
47|At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:100`); `grid` counts threads (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:178`); Apple M1 Pro, 16 cores, SIMD width 32, `bfloat` in Metal (brief:101). Starting point for scale: 256 threads/threadgroup, `(816 + 60 + 2,048 + 4,096) × 4 B = 28,080 B` — 85.7% of the limit, the closest of any routing attempt, leaving 4,688 B (`block-0.metal:15-25`); flat 69→73 µs from 8 to 32 rows confirms the footprint does not bind residency at decode sizes, but any fix that stages more (wider groups, cross-row tiles) must re-derive this sum before it can be trusted. Enforcement gap stands: `slots.build` checks only the 1,024-thread product (`bench/grader/slots.py:341-342`); Metal rejects oversize kernels as opaque G1 exceptions.
